*Theotokion:* The unwedded Maiden, beholding Thee, the adornment of the faithful, Who art fair in beauty, having neither form nor comeliness in Thy suffering, cried aloud maternally and with love glorified Thee.[^7630]

*Other Canon, to the Most Holy Theotokos.*[^7631]

*Tone and Heirmos the same.*[^7632]

*Troparion 1:* Thou hast power to do whatsoever thou desirest; thou hast a Son...[^7633]

...inclined unto thy supplications; thou hast strength and dominion, an unconquerable intercession, O Lady Birthgiver of God: therefore save thy servant.[^7634]

*Troparion 2:* O Lady of the world, helper unto all, deliverance and salvation unto those on earth: deliver thou thy servants who praise thee in faith from manifold troubles and passions and distress.[^7635]

*Troparion 3:* Thou art the protectress of the world, O Virgin; thou art the boast of Christians and our hope: be thou protectress and confirmation, joy and deliverance unto my wretched soul, O Divinely-Blessed One.[^7636]

*Troparion 4:* O hope and protectress of the hopeless, shameless helper unto all: having opened unto me the heavenly doors, bring me unto thy Son, O Lady, and save me who am gone astray.[^7637]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:* Beholding Thee Who suspended all the earth without restraint upon the waters hanging upon the Place of the Skull, creation was shaken with great dismay, crying aloud: There is none holy save Thee, O Lord.[^7638]

*Troparion 1:* Beholding Thee Who suspended all the earth without restraint upon the waters lifted up upon the Tree and pierced in the ribs, the sun was darkened, knowing Thee, O Lord, as the Enlightenment of all.[^7639]

*Troparion 2:* By Thy nails, O Long-Suffering One, the evil-doer who of old wounded Adam in Paradise is wounded, and having been wounded, he remains incurable unto ages; while we the faithful have found healing from all wounds.[^7640]

*Martyrikon 1:* When the Angelic choir beheld the companies of martyrs being slaughtered for the sake of the Lamb Who was slain, it marveled how material men conquered immaterial enemies, receiving the crowns of victory.[^7641]

*Martyrikon 2:* Being clothed with power, O Holy Ones, in the strength of the only Almighty One, ye wrestled with the enemy, and trampled his powerless might, receiving crowns from God.[^7642]

*Theotokion:* When thou didst behold Him Who was born of thee wounded by a spear, thou wast wounded in heart, O all-pure, All-Immaculate One, and marveling, thou saidst: What hath the most lawless assembly rendered unto Thee, O Child?[^7643]

*Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos. Tone and Heirmos the same.*[^7644]

*Troparion 1:* With the waters of salvation give drink, O Virgin-Mother Maiden, delivering from darkness and the unquenchable flame of fire thy supplicants, O Most Pure One, who honor thee as the Birthgiver of God and glorify thee in faith.[^7645]

*Troparion 2:* Being wholly scabbed with the wounds of transgressions, I flee unto thee, O Birth-giver of God, and pray: do thou destroy the wounds thereof and save me, granting me divine health.[^7646]

*Troparion 3:* Ruling over all creatures, O pure Birthgiver of God, show me, who am enslaved by cruel offenses and unseemly deeds, free from them by thy divine power.[^7647]

*Troparion 4:* I know and understand thy tender compassion, O most pure Birthgiver of God! Therefore I flee unto thee and pray: that I may obtain thy help, O Bride of God, so that I may find purification of my evils.[^7648]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:* Foreseeing Thy divine emptying upon the Cross, Habakkuk cried aloud in terror: Thou didst cut through the dominion of the mighty, O Good One, joining Thyself unto those in hades as all-powerful.[^7649]

*Troparion 1:* Having stretched forth Thy hands, O Lord, taking away the lack of restraint toward tasting of the tree, Thou wast sacrificed upon the Tree, having willed to save the dead; and from Thy ribs Thou didst drop forth forgiveness unto those described.[^7650]

*Troparion 2:* Thou didst endure to suffer, O Most Good One, that Thou mightest loose us from irrational passions; Thou didst taste of gall, O Master, pouring forth divine sweetness unto me; Thou wast put to death, granting life unto me.[^7651]

*Martyrikon 1:* Bearing the fire of divine love in their rational soul, the passion-bearers of Christ quenched the flame of the transgressors and appeared as illuminating candles.[^7652]

*Martyrikon 2:* Having separated themselves from carnal friendship, the divine friends of the King of all pressed forward steadfastly unto every torment, and having conquered, were crowned with glory.[^7653]

*Theotokion:* Without passion I gave birth to Thee; and how do I now behold Thee partaking of passion? How dost Thou endure this, cried aloud the Virgin, O unoriginate Son? I glorify Thy longsuffering.[^7654]

*Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos. Heirmos the same.*[^7655]

*Troparion 1:* Having despaired of my salvation, calling aloud I cry unto thee, and stretch forth my hands...[^7656]

...stretch forth: have mercy upon me, O Lady Mother of God, and be thou my helper and protection.[^7657]

*Troparion 2:* I am gripped by the tempests of immeasurable passions and sins; with tears I cry unto thee: O pure Lady, by thy divine guidance do thou save me.[^7658]

*Troparion 3:* Making easy for me the fearful trial at the departure of my soul and its parting from the body, O Virgin Lady: show me to be a partaker of the divine rest there.[^7659]

*Troparion 4:* Behold my affliction, behold, O Most Pure One, my sighings; behold my despair, and show forth thy great grace upon me, filling my humble soul with gladness.[^7660]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:* Unto Thee I rise early, O Word of God, Who for tender mercy's sake didst empty Thyself unchangeably, and dispassionately didst bow down even unto passions: grant peace unto me who am fallen, O Lover of mankind.[^7661]

*Troparion 1:* Thou wast seen as dead upon the Place of the Skull, Who didst slay hades by the passion of Thy flesh; hanging there, O Christ, Thou hadst neither form nor comeliness, desiring in Thy love for mankind to adorn me.[^7662]

*Troparion 2:* Desiring to nail fast the passionate affections of the first Adam, Thou wast nailed fast with nails, and being pierced with a spear, Thou dost forbid the fiery sword, O Christ, to bar the entrance unto Thy servants.[^7663]

*Martyrikon 1:* Following the passions of the Master, the choirs of martyrs were nailed unto the tree, and were deprived of both hands and feet, being directed divinely unto the path of honorable martyrdom.[^7664]

*Martyrikon 2:* With a perfect mind, O martyrs of Christ, ye utterly cast down the proud mind that exalts itself in audacity, having humbled yourselves in imitation of Him Who exalted all through humility of heart.[^7665]

*Theotokion:* Thou didst sprout forth from the root of Jesse, O Virgin, and as a flower didst bring forth the Planter of the world, Who dried up the sprouts of godlessness by the divine plant of the Cross, which He received in the flesh.[^7666]

*Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos. Heirmos the same.*[^7667]

*Troparion 1:* Piously glorifying thee as the true Birthgiver of God, O Pure One, and kissing thine...[^7668]

...icon, through thy supplications unto thy Son we indeed enjoy enlightenment and unceasing joy with all the saints, being delivered from fire and torment.[^7669]

*Troparion 2:* According to the multitude of thy mercies and tender compassion, O Good One, unto me who flee unto thee in faith and ask thy prayers, grant purification of sins and pardon of offenses, O Birthgiver of God, Ever-Virgin.[^7670]

*Troparion 3:* From cruel despair, brought on by frequent tribulations of life, passions, sorrows, and demonic attacks, deliver me, O good and most pure Virgin; and grant me the comfort and enlightenment of salvation.[^7671]

*Troparion 4:* Having spent my life in slothfulness, I anger thee, O Virgin; I, the wretched one, am ever in despondency, and neglect thy mercy. Yet I pray thee, O Good One: permit me not to become a cause of rejoicing for demons, and food for Gehenna.[^7672]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:* Jonah was caught, but not held fast in the belly of the sea monster; for bearing the image of Thee Who didst suffer and wast given over unto burial, he came forth from the beast as from a bridal chamber; and he cried unto the guard: Ye who observe vain and false things have forsaken this mercy.[^7673]

*Troparion 1:* Crossing his hands of old, Jacob prefigured the Cross when blessing the children; therefore, O Most High, ascending thereon, Thou dost loose mankind from the ancient curse, and dost now pour forth blessing unto those who bless Thee, O only Blessed and Most Good Creator.[^7674]

*Troparion 2:* Prefiguring Thy passion, O Word, the great Moses of old lifted up the brazen serpent upon the tree, snatching those who looked upon it from the venomous biting of serpents; for when Thou, O Master, wast crucified, we all the faithful were delivered from the injury of the God-detested serpent.[^7675]

*Martyrikon 1:* As though another were suffering, the divine and honorable sufferers of old endured their suffering, foreseeing eternal recompense and rejoicing. By their prayers, O merciful Christ, deliver those who hymn Thee from temptations, sins, and adversities.[^7676]

*Martyrikon 2:* By the streams of their blood, the honorable and divine passion-bearers stopped the torrents of delusion, and truly appeared as fountains...[^7677]

...pouring forth the water of the knowledge of God unto the faithful. By their prayers, O Savior of the world, shower down forgiveness unto all, both life and purification of sins, and great mercy.[^7678]

*Theotokion:* Beholding the Chief Shepherd and Master lifted up upon the Tree, the Ewe-lamb wept and cried aloud maternally: What is this new mystery, O Child? How is it that, being immortal by essence, Thou hast received death, desiring to deliver mankind from corruption?[^7679]

*Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos. Heirmos the same.*[^7680]

*Troparion 1:* I fall down before thee and pray, O pure Lady of the world! Destroy the passions of my soul, the cruel desires of the flesh, and the defeats of my mind; and cast down utterly by thy power the demonic malice and snares, O Most Pure One, and save me.[^7681]

*Troparion 2:* Enlighten by thy prayers, O Virgin Mother, my mind darkened by the murk of wicked thoughts, by the mist of pleasures, and by the darkness of transgressions, O thou who didst bring forth the Divine Light; and flash forth upon me the unceasing enlightenment of repentance and grace.[^7682]

*Troparion 3:* Direct me unto the divine paths, O Mother of the King of all, delivering me from the trackless paths of passions and sin, and guiding me unto incorruptible life; for thou art the cause of all good things and the salvation of mankind, saving from corruption and leading upward unto salvation.[^7683]

*Troparion 4:* Having borne as a young Child Him Who is before all ages, O Pure One: pray Him unceasingly for the world, O all-blessed Virgin Mother; and as a most pure Mother, entreat the remission of my sins, having ever great boldness toward thy Son, O Pure One.[^7684]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:* Ineffable wonder! He Who delivered the holy youths from the flame in the furnace is laid in the tomb a breathless corpse, for the salvation of us who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God our Deliverer.[^7685]

*Troparion 1:* When the Jewish assembly condemned Thee upon the Cross, beholding it the earth was shaken, the sun hid its light; and those who were in darkness beheld the light, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God our Deliverer.[^7686]

*Troparion 2:* Thou didst endure reproach, O Savior, being beaten with a reed and crowned with thorns...[^7687]

...as a king, being crowned voluntarily, O Christ God, for the salvation of us who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God our Deliverer.[^7688]

*Martyrikon 1:* Ye are bound, O all-praised martyrs, loath to loose the delusion of the devil; ye endure torments and unjust death, desiring life on high, and crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God our Deliverer.[^7689]

*Martyrikon 2:*[^7690] Ye stood in the midst of the flame, O all-praised martyrs, manifestly burning up delusion; and not being burned by the dew of divine grace, ye cried aloud, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God our Deliverer.[^7691]

*Theotokion:* Thou art crucified voluntarily, O unoriginate Son, cried aloud the Birthgiver of God, beholding Thee: I am now engulfed with sorrow of soul; Thou diest, Who grantest life unto those who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God our Deliverer.[^7692]

*Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos. Heirmos the same.*[^7693]

*Troparion 1:* Confirm my soul upon the rock of the desires of my Creator, O pure Lady, having stilled by thy prayers the tempest of pleasures and the tumult of passions, and granting me divine tranquility and peace.[^7694]

*Troparion 2:* Grant me a shower of tears, O most pure Lady, washing away all defilement and the mire of passions from my soul, presenting me pure unto the Creator, and delivering me from all torments.[^7695]

*Troparion 3:* Having acquired thee as intercessor and unconquerable confirmation, O blameless and pure Lady: may we appear superior to the assaults and snares of the enemy, and be delivered from dread and eternal condemnation.[^7696]

*Troparion 4:* The night of my wicked sins holds me fast, and the mist of lawlessness and the depth of evils, lo, covers me; lead me forth from the pit of sin, O Birthgiver of God and intercessor of the faithful.[^7697]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:* Be astonished in fear, O heaven, and let the foundations of the earth be shaken; for lo, He Who dwells in the highest is numbered among the dead, and is lodged as a stranger in a narrow tomb. Ye youths, bless Him; ye priests, hymn Him; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^7698]

*Troparion 1:* Thou drinkest the cup which Thou didst desire, O Christ, through the passion of the Cross, pouring forth unto me fountains of forgiveness from Thy life-bearing ribs, unto me who died for the sake of the rib. Hymning Thee...[^7699]

...I sing: Ye youths, bless Him; ye priests, hymn Him; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^7700]

*Troparion 2:* When the lawless people condemned Thee to be crucified, O Jesus, in the midst of transgressors, O Lord, Giver of life, the earth was shaken, and all sang in fear: Ye youths, bless Him; ye priests, hymn Him; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^7701]

*Martyrikon 1:* Honorable before God was your death, O sufferers; for partaking of many passions, ye showed yourselves to be communicants of the honorable passions of Christ, crying aloud with one mind: Ye youths, bless Him; ye priests, hymn Him; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^7702]

*Martyrikon 2:* Truly your weapons against the array of enemies were not carnal, O martyrs, but hope, faith, and truth; through which having attained unto God, ye were joined unto the angelic choirs, crying aloud unto the Master: Ye youths, bless Him; ye priests, hymn Him; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^7703]

*Theotokion:* O Most High, unoriginate Son, enduring spitting, reproaches, and the Cross, being beaten mockingly with a reed, the Birthgiver of God cried aloud: I glorify Thy longsuffering, Whom the youths bless, the priests hymn, and the people supremely exalt unto all ages.[^7704]

*Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos. Heirmos the same.*[^7705]

*Troparion 1:* Having given birth to Christ the Light, through thy luminous entreaties and prayers, O Virgin, fill with the unwaning Light thy servants who in faith piously hymn thee; for by thy prayer and thine intercession thou art mighty to save whomsoever thou wilt.[^7706]

*Troparion 2:* Evil troubles and sorrows of hades have found me, and severe necessities and sicknesses cruelly hold and destroy me; but I invoke thy help, O Virgin: do thou deliver me from these troubles, directing me unto true tranquility.[^7707]

*Troparion 3:* Overthrow the hostile hosts by thy might, O good Birthgiver of God, of those who war against me and torment me exceedingly, and rejoice at my ruin: guarding, preserving, and delivering me from their wicked frenzy and cruel craftiness.[^7708]

*Troparion 4:* Behold my sorrow, O Pure One, which the multitude of sins hath brought upon me; and quench the furnace of my fiery passions with the dew of thy divine prayer, that I may hymn thy fervent protection, O Maiden, and supremely exalt thee unto all ages.[^7709]

*My soul magnifies the Lord.*[^7710]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:* Weep not for Me, O Mother, beholding in the tomb the Son Whom thou didst conceive in the womb without seed; for I shall arise and be glorified, and as God I shall exalt in glory unceasingly those who magnify thee in faith and love.[^7711]

*Troparion 1:* That Thou mightest deliver from corruption him who decayed through the sweet tasting of the tree, O only Savior, as Good One Thou didst will to be crucified in the flesh and put to death. We hymn unceasingly, O Jesus, Thy great compassion and Thy power.[^7712]

*Troparion 2:* O how didst Thou endure pains, being stretched out upon the Cross, snatching me from cruel pains, O Savior? How, being crowned with thorns, didst Thou burn up all the thorns of passions? How, having been given vinegar to drink, didst Thou mingle for us the cup of gladness?[^7713]

*Martyrikon 1:* Being all oppressed and cast into prisons, and cruelly dismembered in your limbs, O Sufferers, and stretched harshly upon wheels, and given over to be eaten by wild beasts, ye denied not Christ, the Master of all.[^7714]

*Martyrikon 2:* Brighter than the sun's rays shines the all-radiant and celebrated memory of the sufferers; and it ever enlightens the souls of the pious, and drives away the darkness of passions and temptations, and scatters the profound demonic gloom.[^7715]

*Theotokion:* Thou bearest Him Who bears all things, and holdest as an infant upon thine arm Him Who delivered us from the hand of the adversary enemy, O most pure Lady; and thou seest Him lifted up upon the wood of the Cross, Who delivered us from the pit of malice.[^7716]

*Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos. Heirmos the same.*[^7717]

*Troparion 1:* Utterly from the heart I offer myself unto thee, and place all my hope in thee: through thee may I find deliverance from sins; through thee may I appear a partaker of the future kingdom and glory, O pure Birthgiver of God.[^7718]

*Troparion 2:* Having found thee as intercessor and protection, hope and wall, refuge, purification, and deliverance from cruel things, O Most...[^7719]

...Pure One, we are saved from assaults and troubles, sicknesses and passions, and unceasingly honor thy power.[^7720]

*Troparion 3:* Firm salvation and certain hope, who didst make heavenly the human race, who didst pour forth divine rain upon us, O Virgin Birthgiver of God: save us from passions and troubles and from eternal fire.[^7721]

*Troparion 4:* Having ineffably given birth to the supremely unoriginate Word of the Father, the Only-Begotten Son and God: pray Him unceasingly, O pure Maiden, that they may be delivered from troubles and from every threat, who magnify thee in faith and love.[^7722]

*It is truly meet. Exaposteilarion and the rest.*[^7723]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Cross, Tone 6:*[^7724]

*Sticheron 1:* In the Cross have I hope, and boasting therein I cry aloud: O Lord, Lover of mankind, cast down the pride of those who do not confess Thee to be God and man.[^7725]

*Verse: We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord... And look upon Thy servants and upon Thy works, and guide their sons.*[^7726]

*Sticheron 2:* Being hedged about by the Cross, we oppose the enemy, fearing neither his craftiness nor his entrapment; for the proud one hath been brought to naught and trampled down upon the Tree by the power of Christ Who was crucified.[^7727]

*Verse: And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us, and direct the works of our hands upon us; yea, direct the work of our hands.*[^7728]

*Martyrikon:* O Lord, in the commemoration of Thy saints, all creation keeps festival; the heavens rejoice with the angels, and the earth is glad with men. By their prayers have mercy upon us.[^7729]

*Glory... both now... Stavrotheotokion:* I was indeed nailed as a man upon the Tree, and was put to death, and was laid in the tomb as dead; but as God in glory, O Mother, pure Virgin, I rise again on the third day.[^7730]

*It is good to give praise. Trisagion and the rest.*[^7731]

*On Friday, The Beatitudes, Tone 6:*[^7732]

*Troparion 1:* Remember me, O God my Savior, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom, and save me as the only Lover of mankind.[^7733]

*Troparion 2:* Having spread forth Thy palms upon the Tree, Thou didst embrace the nations who hymn Thy tender compassion, O Christ our God.[^7734]

*Troparion 3:* Thou wast nailed upon the Tree voluntarily, and by Thy power, O Christ, Thou didst utterly shatter the stings of the proud one...[^7735]

...O Christ, Thou didst utterly shatter.[^7736]

*Troparion 4:* Delighting in torments, O passion-bearers, ye were counted worthy of the delight of Paradise, praying unceasingly for the world.[^7737]

*Glory: Triadikon:* Deliver us from all torment, O Father, and Son, and Spirit Who shares the throne, Thy servants, O Lord.[^7738]

*Both now: Stavrotheotokion:* Beholding Thee stretched out upon the Cross, the Virgin sighed with tears; by her prayers save us, O Lord.[^7739]

## Saturday: All Saints and the Departed[^7740]

*On Friday Evening.*[^7741]

*On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera to the Holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, and Venerables, Tone 6:*[^7742]

*Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*[^7743]

*Sticheron 1:* Walking in the footsteps of Christ's passions, the whole assembly of martyrs went steadfastly unto many contests, and preached Him as God before ungodly tormentors and lawless kings, and endured many torments, expecting to receive heavenly honors; seeing which they now rejoice, and stand before the Lord with all the choirs of bodiless powers.[^7744]

*Sticheron 2:* A God-chosen flock, imitators of Christ the Chief Shepherd were ye, O all-sacred shepherds: ye preserved unharmed unto the end the divine treasures of piety, having driven away the wild wolves, and guided it well into the heavenly fold; wherein being now established, remember with love those who praise you, and with boldness pray unto Christ for our souls.[^7745]

*Sticheron 3:* Having lived venerably, all ye venerable fathers, ye conquered the demons, and having quenched the burning consciences of the torment of passions, ye valiantly endured, O Blessed Ones; and ye now rejoice with the heavenly powers, for in the flesh ye were likened unto the life of those bodiless ones; with whom pray Christ, the most good God, to find deliverance from falls...[^7746]

...unto those who honor you.[^7747]

*Other Stichera to the Martyrs, Tone and Podoben the same:*[^7748]

*Sticheron 1:* Thy martyrs, O Lord, denied Thee not, neither did they depart from Thy commandments. By their prayers have mercy upon us. *(Twice)*[^7749]

*Sticheron 2:* Passion-bearing martyrs, citizens of heaven, having suffered upon earth, endured many torments. By their prayers, O Lord, and by their entreaty, preserve us all.[^7750]

*Glory... both now... Theotokion (Dogmatikon):* Who will not call thee blessed, O all-holy Virgin? Who will not hymn thy birthgiving without defilement? For the Only-Begotten Son, Who shone forth timelessly from the Father, the same came forth from thee, O Pure One, having become ineffably incarnate: being God by nature, and having become man by nature for our sake: not divided into two persons, but known unconfusedly in two natures. Him do thou entreat, O pure and all-blessed one, that our souls may be saved.[^7751]

*O Joyful Light. Prokeimenon of the day.*[^7752]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera to the Martyrs, Tone 6:*[^7753]

*Sticheron 1:* Those who suffered for Thy sake, O Christ, endured many torments, and received perfect crowns in the heavens: that they may pray for our souls.[^7754]

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes... so our eyes look unto the Lord our God, until He have mercy on us.*[^7755]

*Sticheron 2:* Thy Cross, O Lord, became an unconquerable weapon unto the martyrs; for beholding impending death and foreseeing future life, they were strengthened by their hope in Thee; by their prayers have mercy upon us.[^7756]

*Verse: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us... Our soul is exceedingly filled with the reproach of the prosperous, and with the contempt of the proud.*[^7757]

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):* Thy creative command was my beginning and foundation; for desiring to fashion me as a living creature out of invisible and visible nature, Thou didst fashion my body from the earth, and didst give me a soul by Thy divine and life-creating breathing. Therefore, O Savior, give rest unto Thy servants in the land of the living, and in the tents of the righteous.[^7758]

*Glory... both now... Theotokion:* By the prayers of her who gave Thee birth, O Christ, of Thy martyrs, and apostles, and prophets, and hierarchs, venerable ones, and righteous...[^7759]

...righteous, and of all the saints, give rest unto Thy departed servants.[^7760]

*On Friday at Compline.*[^7761]

*Supplicatory Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos.*[^7762]

*Tone 6. Ode 1. Heirmos:* He was my helper and protector unto salvation; this is my God, and I will glorify Him; the God of my father, and I will exalt Him; for gloriously is He glorified.[^7763]

*Refrain: Most Holy Lady Theotokos, save us.*[^7764]

*Troparion 1:* Cast me not away, O Good One, abhor me not, nor despise me, who have fervently fled beneath thy tender compassion, O Pure One; but grant me to be nourished in thee by grace.[^7765]

*Troparion 2:* O good Theotokos, helper of the sorrowing, receive the sighing from my soul, and deliver me from all the immeasurable evils which I have cruelly committed.[^7766]

*Glory:* Unto thee I fall down, O Good One, intercessor for the sorrowful: deliver me from the eternal fire, and the darkness, and the abyss, who have lived evilly throughout my whole life.[^7767]

*Both now:* Woe is me! How shall I entreat Thee, O Deliverer, my Jesus, having sinned immeasurably against Thee? Therefore I bring unto Thee as intercessor the Pure One who gave Thee birth: have mercy and save me.[^7768]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:* Establish, O Lord, upon the rock of Thy commandments my shaken heart, for Thou alone art holy and Lord.[^7769]

*Troparion 1:* I fall down before thee, O Mother of the Word: receive me with thy compassions; and grant forgiveness of transgressions unto me who ask, by thy fervent prayers.[^7770]

*Troparion 2:* Have mercy on me, O Lady, have mercy, and deliver me from every malice, and the affliction of demons, and eternal torment.[^7771]

*Glory:* Subdue, O Lady, the bitter drunkenness of my pleasures, granting me the divine sobriety of repentance and saving conversion.[^7772]

*Both now:* O Parent of God, who ineffably gavest birth unto the Lord and Ruler of all, entreat Him that He may save thy flock.[^7773]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:* The Prophet heard of Thy coming, O Lord, and was afraid, that Thou wast about to be born of a Virgin and appear unto men, and he said: I heard the report of Thee, and was afraid; glory to Thy power, O Lord.[^7774]

*Troparion 1:* Ceaselessly do I scratch the wounds of my soul with love of pleasure, and the pains of ulcers have been added unto me...[^7775]

...pains, and I remain insensible and incurable; have mercy, O Parent of God, and heal and save me by thy prayers.[^7776]

*Troparion 2:* The darkness of sin hath covered my soul, O Parent of God, so that I walk as in night in the light, ignorant of Christ's commandments; O thou who gavest birth to the Divine Light, have mercy on me and enlighten me, I pray.[^7777]

*Glory:* The Word of the living God came down into thy womb, O Virgin-Mother, and taking from thy most pure blood my whole nature, He comes twofold in one Hypostasis; entreat Him to save our souls.[^7778]

*Both now:* Diligently have I pursued bodily desires and all pleasures, and I am wholly corrupted, defiled, and abominable; O most pure Parent of God, have mercy and save me by thy tender compassion.[^7779]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:* Enlighten, I pray, him who rises early from the night, O Lover of mankind, and guide me unto Thy commandments, and teach me, O Savior, to do Thy will.[^7780]

*Troparion 1:* I have kindled for myself the fire of Gehenna, doing unfitting deeds, and have cruelly drawn upon myself the wrath of God; help me, O Pure One, and forsake me not.[^7781]

*Troparion 2:* Ceaselessly do I ask remission of transgressions, yet I cease not committing most lawless deeds, and I grieve thee, O Most Pure One; O cleansing of the faithful, have compassion on me.[^7782]

*Glory:* Whom thou hast borne from thy blood, O Pure One, perfect man and true God, Jesus: entreat Him that we may be delivered from eternal fire.[^7783]

*Both now:* O Impassable Gate, I pray: open unto me the doors of true repentance, and show me the paths of repentance, O Pure One, who art the guide of all.[^7784]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:* I cried with all my heart unto the merciful God, and He heard me from the lowest hades, and brought up my life from corruption.[^7785]

*Troparion 1:* The waves of improper thoughts now submerge me; but do thou, O Lady, guide me by thy tender compassion unto the calm haven of true repentance.[^7786]

*Troparion 2:* Having acquired thee as hope and unconquerable wall, and a firm protectress, O Maiden...[^7787]

...we are delivered from transgressions, and cruel passions, and every harm.[^7788]

*Glory:* I fall down before thee, O pure Virgin, and cry aloud with weeping, O Theotokos: deliver my wretched soul from the future judgment and the eternal fire.[^7789]

*Both now:* Thou art the strength, O Most Pure One, of those infirm in soul through thy supplications; therefore despise me not who am sick in soul, but heal me.[^7790]

*Then, Lord, have mercy (40 times). Glory... both now...*[^7791]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 6:* For the tender compassion of Thy mercies, O Christ, Thou camest down to earth, and taking flesh of the Virgin, Thou didst sanctify all, and didst call all from earth to heaven; therefore, hoping in Thee, we shall never err, but are delivered by Thee from present assaults; for Thou art our Savior, O our Creator God.[^7792]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:* We have sinned, we have transgressed, we have done unrighteously before Thee, neither have we kept nor done as Thou hast commanded us; but deliver us not up utterly, O God of the fathers.[^7793]

*Troparion 1:* When my wretched soul must endure separation from the body, and there will be none to deliver it or comfort it: then stand forth, O Lady, and deliver me from the malice of demons.[^7794]

*Troparion 2:* I fall down before thee, and offer fervent drops of tears; I know thy love for mankind, I know thy longsuffering and meekness: do thou now have mercy on me, O Pure One, pardon and save me.[^7795]

*Glory:* Have mercy, O Virgin, upon my passionate and wretched soul; see the turmoil of passions, see also the inconstant burning of the flesh; and grant me saving help and deliverance.[^7796]

*Both now:* The Son and Word, consubstantial and co-unoriginate with the Father, took flesh from thee, equal, endowed with mind and soul, unchangeably, as He Himself knows; and He renewed our nature therein for the better, O pure Virgin.[^7797]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:* Whom the heavenly hosts glorify, and Cherubim and Seraphim tremble before: let every breath and creation sing, bless, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^7798]

*Troparion 1:* I am at a loss pondering my deeds, and I tremble before the Judge of the dread tribunal; what defense shall I, the wretched one, then offer? O Lady...[^7799]

...Lady of the world, be thou my protectress.[^7800]

*Troparion 2:* Do not thou thyself, O Lady, cast me away from thy face when I look upon thine icon; but be merciful unto me, and alter my present condemnation.[^7801]

*Glory:* O Bride of God, unwedded Mary! Deliver me from every wicked harm as I, thy servant, cry unto thee; and stand by me in the future trial, O only protectress of Christians.[^7802]

*Both now:* That Thy Son might deify mankind, O Lady, He appeared from thee as perfect man; entreat Him therefore to show me, perfectly cleansed, a partaker of His divine kingdom.[^7803]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:* O Virgin who didst receive from the Angel the "Rejoice," and gavest birth to thy Creator: save those who magnify thee.[^7804]

*Troparion 1:* Thou alone art the protectress of mankind, O Most Pure One! Thou art the wall of Christians, O Pure One! Thee do I now present as an intercessor unto Christ for me the humble one, that by thy prayers He may have mercy on me the wretched.[^7805]

*Troparion 2:* I have wrought the works of night, and the night of torment is now about to cover me justly, convicted, and to receive all torment of hades; but O pure Virgin who didst bear the Judge and God, deliver me from every torment.[^7806]

*Glory:* I have spent the time of my life in evils, and have drawn near unto the gates of hades, and all unprepared do I go thither. Help me, O good Theotokos, for in thee have I placed my hope.[^7807]

*Both now:* O good-loving Lady, adornment of Angels, glory of Martyrs: with these pray that we may find mercy and remission of debts, and that all may be able rightly to finish the course of our life, doing divine things.[^7808]

*It is truly meet. Trisagion. After the Our Father: troparia and the rest as usual.*[^7809]

*On Saturday at Matins.*[^7810]

*After the first Kathisma, Sessional Hymns to the Martyrs, Tone 6:*[^7811]

*Sessional Hymn 1:* Thou art ever a light unto the righteous, O Lord! For the saints, having been enlightened in Thee, shine ever as luminaries...[^7812]

...having quenched the lamp of the ungodly. By their prayers, O our Savior, enlighten Thou my lamp, and save me.[^7813]

*Verse: Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel.*[^7814]

*Sessional Hymn 2:* Having endured the struggle of suffering, O saints, and received from Thee the honors of victory, they brought to nought the devices of the lawless, and received incorruptible crowns. Being entreated by them, O God, grant us great mercy.[^7815]

*Glory... both now... Theotokion:* Thou Who didst call Thy Mother blessed, camest to Thy passion by voluntary counsel, shining forth upon the Cross, desiring to seek out Adam, saying unto the Angels: Rejoice with Me, for the lost coin is found. O our God Who hast ordered all things wisely, glory to Thee.[^7816]

*After the second Kathisma, Sessional Hymns to the Martyrs, Tone 6:*[^7817]

*Sessional Hymn 1:* The suffering standing in the contest, and the wounds of torment upon the martyrs: and the choirs of the bodiless stood holding the honors of victory: the all-wise ones amazed tormentors and kings; they cast down the apostate by the confession of Christ. O Lord Who didst strengthen them, glory to Thee.[^7818]

*Verse: Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel.*[^7819]

*Sessional Hymn 2:* O Lord, the memory of Thy saints today is shown forth as the Paradise that was in Eden; for therein all creation rejoices, and by their supplications Thou grantest us peace and great mercy.[^7820]

*Verse: Many are the afflictions of the righteous, and out of them all the Lord will deliver them.*[^7821]

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):* Truly all things are vanity, and life is but a shadow and a dream; for in vain doth everyone born of earth disquiet himself, as the Scripture saith: when we have acquired the world, then do we dwell in the grave, where kings and paupers are together. Therefore, O Christ God, give rest unto the departed, as the Lover of mankind.[^7822]

*Glory... both now... Theotokion:*

*Tone 6, Podoben: "O hope of the world" (Наде́жде мі́ра):*[^7823] O defense of those born of earth, protectress Mary, who didst bear in time the timeless Son and Word of God: entreat Him earnestly, as His Mother, with the martyrs, and prophets, and divine fasters, to save those who have departed.[^7824]

*Canon to the Holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, Venerables, and the Departed.*[^7825]

*(Whose acrostic is: With words I honor the lovers of the Word.) A work of Joseph.*[^7826]

*Tone 6. Ode 1. Heirmos:* The sensory Pharaoh was drowned with all his host, but Israel, having passed through the midst of the sea, cried aloud: Let us sing unto the Lord our God, for gloriously is He glorified.[^7827]

*Refrain: Holy Martyrs, pray to God for us.*[^7828]

*Troparion 1:* With radiant mind ye enlightened those in darkness, and having put to shame the impious tormentors, O Martyrs, being clearly victorious, ye passed over unto the unwaning light.[^7829]

*Refrain: Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us.*[^7830]

*Troparion 2:* The hierarchs of Christ, and the choir of the venerable, and of the prophets, and the unique solemnity of all the righteous, shining with virtuous beauties, have entered into the heavenly mansions.[^7831]

*Refrain: All Saints, pray to God for us.*[^7832]

*Troparion 3:* The whole multitude of women, having betrothed themselves unto Christ and trampled underfoot with manly labors him who slew Eve by cruel deceit, are called blessed with divine songs.[^7833]

*Glory: Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):* Thou Who from the earth didst create man in the beginning, O Christ: give rest to the souls of Thy servants, we pray, in the mansions of the righteous and in places of refreshment, as Thou art most good.[^7834]

*Both now:* More sacred than the Cherubim and Seraphim, O Pure One, wast thou revealed, having given birth to the Creator of creation; entreat Him unceasingly to have compassion upon thy servants who glorify thee.[^7835]

*Another Canon to the Departed.*[^7836]

*(Whose acrostic is: A sixth song I sing for the departed.) We sing it in order where there is no Menaion. A work of Theophanes.*[^7837]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:* Traversing the deep on foot as on dry land, Israel, seeing Pharaoh their pursuer drowning, cried aloud: Let us sing a song of victory unto God.[^7838]

*Verse: Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel.*[^7839]

*Troparion 1:* In the heavenly chambers the noble martyrs ever pray Thee, O Christ: vouchsafe the faithful whom Thou hast removed from the earth to obtain eternal blessings.[^7840]

*Verse: Give rest, O Lord, to the souls of Thy departed servants.*[^7841]

*Troparion 2:* Having adorned all things, Thou didst create between them man, a mixed creature, both of humility and greatness; therefore give rest, O Savior, to the souls of Thy servants.[^7842]

*Glory:* In the beginning Thou didst establish me as a dweller and worker of Paradise...[^7843]

...yet when I transgressed Thy commandment, Thou didst drive me out; therefore give rest, O Savior, to the souls of Thy servants.[^7844]

*Both now:* He Who from a rib created of old Eve our first mother, is clothed in flesh from thy most pure womb, whereby, O Pure One, He hath destroyed the power of death.[^7845]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:* Having established the thoughts of my soul upon the firm rock of Thy faith, establish me, O Lord; for I have Thee, O Good One, as refuge and affirmation.[^7846]

*Troparion 1:* Blended with bodily pains, the sufferers looked rejoicing toward the painless recompense; and now they soothe our many pains by grace.[^7847]

*Troparion 2:* Driving away evil beasts with a firm understanding, the divine hierarchs delivered unharmed from their malice the divine nurslings of Christ.[^7848]

*Troparion 3:* The choir of Venerables, voluntarily submitting beneath the yoke of the Lord, mortified carnal wisdom, and received eternal life.[^7849]

*Glory: Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):* Deliver from eternal fire those who in piety have departed from this life, O Christ, and grant remission of their debts, O Good One, and eternal delight.[^7850]

*Both now:* The women who loved Christ, standing about thee who didst ineffably give Him birth, O most pure Lady, dance in chorus with joyful mind.[^7851]

*Canon to the Departed. Heirmos:* There is none holy like Thee, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and established us upon the rock of Thy confession.[^7852]

*Troparion 1:* Having lawfully suffered, Thy martyrs, O Giver of life, adorned with crowns of victory from Thee, earnestly intercede for eternal honor for the departed faithful.[^7853]

*Troparion 2:* Having chastened me who had gone astray of old with many wonders and signs, at last Thou didst empty Thyself, being compassionate; and having sought, Thou didst find and save me.[^7854]

*Glory:* Vouchsafe those who have passed over unto Thee from the fleeting, inconstant corruption, to dwell with joy in eternal habitations, O Good One, having justified them by faith and grace.[^7855]

*Both now:* There is none blameless like thee, O most pure Mother of God; for thou alone...[^7856]

...didst conceive in thy womb the true God before the ages, Who destroyed the power of death.[^7857]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:* I heard, O Lord, the report of Thee, and was afraid; I understood Thy works, and was filled with awe: glory to Thy power, O Lord.[^7858]

*Troparion 1:* Standing, the passion-bearers beheld the proud one trampled under their feet, and thankfully they glorified the Creator of all.[^7859]

*Troparion 2:* Armed with the splendors of words unto the light of understanding, the hierarchs saved men from the darkness of heresies.[^7860]

*Troparion 3:* Appearing as burning coals through fervent understanding toward God, and having burned up material passions, the Venerable are greatly glorified.[^7861]

*Glory: Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):* Ruling over both the living and the dead, O Lord: give rest to those whom Thou hast removed, with all who have well-pleased Thee, O Master.[^7862]

*Both now:* The Lord, O Most Pure One, having ineffably clothed Himself in flesh from thee, received the company of women who contended courageously.[^7863]

*Canon to the Departed. Heirmos:* Christ is my power, God and Lord, the venerable Church sings in God-befitting manner, crying out from a pure mind, feasting in the Lord.[^7864]

*Troparion 1:* Manifesting a greater knowledge of wisdom, and in Thy gifts an all-perfect goodness, O Master, Thou didst unite the choirs of martyrs with the Angels.[^7865]

*Troparion 2:* Vouchsafe the departed who have passed unto Thee to obtain Thine ineffable glory, O Christ, where is the habitation of those who rejoice, and the sound of pure gladness.[^7866]

*Glory:* Receive those singing of Thy divine dominion, whom Thou hast received from the earth: making them children of light, cleansing the mist of sin, O Plenteous in mercy.[^7867]

*Both now:* As a most pure receptacle, a blameless church, an all-holy ark, a virginal place of sanctification: thee, the beauty of Jacob, hath the Master chosen.[^7868]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:* O Christ Who hast shone forth light unto the world: enlighten my heart, as I cry to Thee from the night, and save me.[^7869]

*Troparion 1:* Having clothed yourselves in the garment woven of grace from on high, O sufferers, ye stripped the enemy bare.[^7870]

*Troparion 2:* With the holy prophets let us honor the God-wise high priests, and...[^7871]

...the venerable who have well-pleased God.[^7872]

*Troparion 3:* In psalms and songs let us praise the company of women, as having well-pleased God rightly.[^7873]

*Glory: Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):* In the habitations of Thy righteous, O Lord, establish Thy servants, overlooking their sins in this life.[^7874]

*Both now:* Delivering us from every harm of the enemy, thou hast appeared, O Lady, praying to Christ the only compassionate One.[^7875]

*Canon to the Departed. Heirmos:* With Thy divine light, O Good One, illumine, I pray, the souls of those who rise early unto Thee with love, that they may know Thee, O Word of God, as the true God, calling them back from the darkness of sin.[^7876]

*Troparion 1:* Offered as a consecrated whole burnt-offering and as the first-fruits of human nature unto God Who is glorified, the Martyrs ever intercede for our salvation.[^7877]

*Troparion 2:* Vouchsafe Thy departed faithful servants heavenly dwelling and the distribution of gifts, O Lord, granting them deliverance from transgressions.[^7878]

*Glory:* O Thou Who alone art the Life-creator by nature, Who art truly an unsearchable abyss of goodness: vouchsafe Thy kingdom unto those who have reposed, O Merciful, only Immortal One.[^7879]

*Both now:* Strength and song is He Who was born of thee unto the world, O Lady, and became salvation unto the lost, delivering from the gates of hades those who bless thee in faith.[^7880]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:* Swallowed by the whale of sin, I cry unto Thee, O Christ: as the Prophet, deliver me from corruption.[^7881]

*Troparion 1:* By the flow of your divine blood ye drowned the noetic enemies; and ye watered the hearts of the faithful, O Passion-bearers.[^7882]

*Troparion 2:* Having crucified yourselves to the world and passions, O Venerable ones and all-wise Hierarchs, ye were counted worthy of divine glory.[^7883]

*Troparion 3:* As is due, let us call blessed the choir of prophets, and the assembly of honorable women who strove well.[^7884]

*Glory: Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):* Give rest, O God, to the souls of those who have departed before, with Thine elect, overlooking their transgressions.[^7885]

*Both now:* O thou who didst bear Christ in the flesh, mortify the passions of my flesh, and...[^7886]

...quicken my soul, O Virgin, by thine intercession.[^7887]

*Canon to the Departed. Heirmos:* Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, having fled to Thy calm haven, I cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Plenteous in mercy.[^7888]

*Troparion 1:* Being nailed to the Cross, Thou didst gather unto Thyself the choirs of martyrs who imitated Thy passion, O Good One; therefore we pray Thee: give rest to those who have departed unto Thee.[^7889]

*Troparion 2:* When Thou comest in Thine ineffable glory dreadfully to judge the whole world, be well pleased, O Deliverer, that the faithful servants whom Thou hast taken from the earth may meet Thee radiantly upon the clouds.[^7890]

*Glory:* Being the Fountain of life, O Master, in divine strength bringing out the bound, settle Thy servants who have departed unto Thee in faith in the delight of Paradise.[^7891]

*Both now:* Unto the earth we returned having transgressed the commandment of God; but for thy sake, O Virgin, we were lifted up from earth to heaven, having shaken off mortal corruption.[^7892]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:* Thou Who didst hear the song of Thy holy Children and didst bedew the burning furnace: blessed art Thou, O Lord.[^7893]

*Troparion 1:* Let us honor with songs the passion-bearers of Christ, who quenched the flame of cruel godlessness with showers of blood.[^7894]

*Troparion 2:* The all-glorious Hierarchs, having dispelled the winter of heresies, passed rejoicing unto the divine springtime.[^7895]

*Troparion 3:* By endurance ye inherited the rich grace of the Spirit, O Fasters, and destroyed a multitude of demons.[^7896]

*Glory:* Vouchsafe those who in faith have departed from this life to inherit the haven of Thy sweetness, O Merciful One, as Thou art plenteous in mercy.[^7897]

*Both now:* He Who showed thee to be a pure Virgin even after childbirth hath saved the choirs of holy women who followed thee.[^7898]

*Canon to the Departed. Heirmos:* The Angel made the furnace dew-yielding for the holy Children; while the command of God, consuming the Chaldeans, persuaded the tormentor to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^7899]

*Troparion 1:* Delivered by Thy blood from the first transgression, the Martyrs...[^7900]

...and being sprinkled with their own blood, they clearly prefigure Thy slaying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^7901]

*Troparion 2:* Thou didst put to death raging death, O most life-originating Word; but receive in Thy faith those who have reposed, who hymn Thee, O Christ, and say: Blessed is the God of our fathers.[^7902]

*Glory:* Having enlivened me, man, with divine inbreathing, O Sovereign Master origin of Godhead: vouchsafe the departed Thy kingdom, to sing unto Thee, O Savior: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^7903]

*Both now:* Thou wast higher than all creatures, O All-immaculate One, having conceived God Who shattered the gates of death and broke the bars; therefore, O Pure One, we the faithful hymn thee as Mother of God.[^7904]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:* In the furnace Thy venerable Children imitated the Cherubim, chanting the thrice-holy hymn: Bless, sing the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^7905]

*Troparion 1:* Valiantly wounded by the surge of tortures, the divine Martyrs, having passed through by grace into deep calm, reached the kingdom on high.[^7906]

*Troparion 2:* The venerable and all-wise Hierarchs, having shone forth like the sun, enlighten the universe with the rays of their teachings and the brightness of their healings.[^7907]

*Troparion 3:* Glorious Prophets and Chief Priests, all venerable and righteous ones, multitudes of martyrs and women: preserve all your flock unshaken by demons.[^7908]

*Glory: Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):* Let us hymn the righteous from of old and the God-speaking Prophets, and let us cry aloud with compunction: By their prayers, O Word, give rest unto those who have reposed in faith.[^7909]

*Both now:* The choir of women loved thee, O Virgin, as neighbor wholly to God, and was brought after thee unto the Master of all, praising thee with one accord, O Most Pure One.[^7910]

*Canon to the Departed. Heirmos:* From the flame Thou didst pour out dew for the holy Children, and didst consume with fire the sacrifice of the righteous one and the water; for Thou, O Christ, doest all things by the mere act of willing; Thee do we supremely exalt unto all ages.[^7911]

*Troparion 1:* Steadfastly showing forth their struggles, they received crowns of victory, the...[^7912]

...Martyrs, passion-bearers of Christ, crying aloud: Thee, the Lord, do we supremely exalt unto the ages.[^7913]

*Troparion 2:* Receive gently, and give rest as Thou art compassionate, unto the faithful who have holily left earthly things and departed unto Thee, the Master, who supremely exalt Thee unto the ages.[^7914]

*Glory:* Now in the land of the meek, be well pleased, O Savior, that all who have reposed before may take up their dwelling, having justified them through faith in Thee and by grace, who supremely exalt Thee unto the ages.[^7915]

*Both now:* We all call thee blessed, O All-blessed One, as having given birth unto the Word truly existing and blessed, Who became flesh for our sake, Whom we supremely exalt unto all ages.[^7916]

*My soul doth magnify the Lord.*[^7917]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:* O Virgin who didst receive from the Angel the "Rejoice," and gavest birth to thy Creator: save those who magnify thee.[^7918]

*Troparion 1:* As pure sheep ye were brought unto the Master, O Passion-bearing Martyrs: pray Him to save our souls.[^7919]

*Troparion 2:* As pastors upon the pasture of piety, O Hierarchs, ye shepherded the faithful; and now ye have taken up your dwelling in the divine sheepfold.[^7920]

*Troparion 3:* With the holy Hierarchs and Prophets, and with the choir of women who suffered valiantly, let us call blessed the choirs of the venerable.[^7921]

*Glory: Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):* The perpetual joy whereof the assemblies of the Saints partake: vouchsafe the departed to obtain this, O Plenteous in mercy.[^7922]

*Both now:* O Virgin who didst give birth to the Light, enlighten my soul, driving away the darkness of sin and of my slothfulness.[^7923]

*Canon to the Departed. Heirmos:* It is not possible for men to see God, upon Whom the ranks of Angels dare not gaze; but through thee, O All-pure One, the Word Incarnate appeared unto men; Whom magnifying with the heavenly hosts, we call thee blessed.[^7924]

*Troparion 1:* Hope strengthened the choirs of the martyrs, and winged them with burning desire unto Thy love, prefiguring for them the truly unshaken rest to come; whereof vouchsafe the departed faithful, O Good One.[^7925]

*Troparion 2:* Be well pleased, O Christ, that those who have reposed in faith may obtain Thy radiant and divine illumination, and the rest in the bosom of Abraham, as Thou alone art merciful unto them...[^7926]

...granting it, and accounting them worthy of eternal blessedness.[^7927]

*Glory:* O Thou Who art by nature good and compassionate, and the Desirer of mercies, and an abyss of loving-kindness: settle in the place where Thy light shines, O Savior, those whom Thou hast translated from this place of affliction and the shadow of death.[^7928]

*Both now:* We know thee, O Pure One, to be the holy Tabernacle, and the Ark, and the Tablets of the Law and of grace; for for thy sake forgiveness was granted unto those justified by the blood of Him Who was incarnate from thy womb, O All-immaculate One.[^7929]

*It is good to give praise: Litany, Exapostilarion, and the usual Psalms.*[^7930]

*At the Praises, Stichera of the Martyrs, Tone 6:*

O Lord, at the memory of Thy Saints all creation keeps festival; the heavens rejoice with the Angels, and the earth is glad with men: by their prayers have mercy on us.[^7931]

O Lord, if we had not Thy Saints as intercessors, and Thy goodness showing mercy upon us, how should we dare, O Savior, to hymn Thee, Whom the Angels ceaselessly glorify? O Knower of hearts, spare our souls.[^7932]

The memory of the Martyrs is joy unto those that fear the Lord; for having suffered for Christ's sake, they received crowns from Him; and now with boldness they pray for our souls.[^7933]

Our God is marvelous in His chosen and holy ones. Rejoice and be glad, all ye His servants; for He hath prepared for you crowns and His kingdom. But we pray you, forget us not also.[^7934]

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):* Pain came upon Adam through the tasting of the tree of old in Eden, when the serpent vomited out venom; for on account thereof all-generational death entered in, devouring man; but the Master came and cast down the serpent, and granted us resurrection. Unto Him therefore let us cry aloud: Spare, O Savior, and give rest with the Saints unto those whom Thou hast received, as Thou art the Lover of mankind.[^7935]

*Glory... both now... Theotokion:* Thou art our God, Who in wisdom createst and fulfillest all things: Thou didst send Prophets, O Christ, to foretell Thy coming; and Apostles, to proclaim Thy majesty. And the former...[^7936]

...indeed prophesied Thy coming, while the latter enlightened the nations by baptism; and the martyrs obtained that which they desired; and the choir of both entreats Thee, together with her that bare Thee: Give rest, O Lord, to the souls which Thou hast received; and vouchsafe us Thy kingdom, O Thou Who didst endure crucifixion for the sake of me the condemned, my Deliverer and God.[^7937]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera for the Departed, Tone 6.*[^7938]
*Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*

Possessing incomprehensible compassion toward us, and an inexhaustible fountain of divine goodness, O Plenteous in mercy: settle those who have departed unto Thee, O Master, in the land of the living, in the beloved and longed-for dwellings, granting an abiding possession; for Thou didst shed Thy blood for all, O Savior, and didst redeem the world with a life-bearing price.[^7939]

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken, O Lord [LXX Ps. 64:5].*[^7940]

Thou didst willingly endure life-creating putting-to-death, and didst pour out life, and gavest eternal nourishment unto the faithful; wherein station those who have reposed in the hope of resurrection, pardoning all their transgressions by grace, as Thou alone art without sin, and alone art good and the Lover of mankind, that Thy name may be sung by all, O Christ, and Thy saving love for mankind be glorified.[^7941]

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things [LXX Ps. 24:13].*[^7942]

Knowing Thee, O Christ, Who rulest over the living with authority of divine origin, and exercisest lordship over the dead, we pray Thee: give rest unto Thy faithful servants who have departed unto Thee the only Benefactor, with Thine elect, O Lover of mankind, in the place of comfort, in the brightness of the Saints; for Thou art the Desirer of mercy, and as God savest those whom Thou didst create after Thine image, O only Plenteous in mercy.[^7943]

*Glory... both now... Theotokion:* Thou didst appear as a God-befitting dwelling, O Most Pure One; for thou didst contain God, and gavest birth unto Christ, O unwedded Virgin-Mother, in two essences, yet in one Hypostasis. Him do thou entreat, O Pure One, the only-begotten Firstborn, Who preserved thee an immaculate Virgin even after...[^7944]

...childbirth: to give rest in the light and in incorruptible blessedness unto the souls of those who have reposed in faith.[^7945]

*It is good to give praise: Trisagion. After Our Father: Troparion, Litany, and Dismissal.*[^7946]

*On Saturday, The Beatitudes, Tone 6:*

Remember me, O God my Savior, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom, and save me as Thou alone art the Lover of mankind.[^7947]

O Lover of mankind Who didst glorify the prophets and teachers, and the venerable and righteous: by their prayers save our souls.[^7948]

Having not feared the onslaught of fire and sword and wild beasts, O glorious Passion-bearers, ye were accounted worthy of life everlasting.[^7949]

Station with all the saints and righteous ones, O Word, those whom Thou hast translated in faith from temporal things, that we may glorify Thee.[^7950]

*Glory: Triadikon:* O Almighty Trinity, praised in unity! Station in the bosom of Abraham the faithful whom Thou hast translated from the earth.[^7951]

*Both now:* Blessed hast thou appeared in all generations; for thou gavest birth ineffably unto God Who is truly blessed, O Most Pure One.[^7952]

*End of Tone 6.*

*[Engraved Tailpiece: An ornamental baroque vignette in the form of a chalice with floral garlands and arabesques, marking the conclusion of Tone 6]*[^7953]

# PART 07 — TONE 7: SUNDAY AND WEEKDAY OFFICES (SATURDAY VESPERS THROUGH SATURDAY MATINS)

*[Engraved Headpiece: An ornamental baroque frieze depicting the Most Pure Theotokos holding the Pre-eternal Christ Child, surrounded by holy prophets, angels, and foliate cartouches, marking the beginning of Tone 7]*[^7954]

*On Saturday Evening.*
*At Little Vespers.*
*On "Lord, I have cried," we set 4 verses, and sing 3 Resurrection Stichera, repeating the first.*
*Tone 7:*

*Sticheron 1 (Resurrectional):* Come, let us rejoice in the Lord, Who shattered the dominion of death and enlightened the human race, crying aloud with the Bodiless Powers: O our Creator and Savior, glory to Thee! *(Twice)*[^7955]

*Sticheron 2 (Resurrectional):* Thou didst endure the Cross and burial for our sake, O Savior, and by death, as God, Thou didst put death to death; therefore we worship Thy third-day Resurrection: O Lord, glory to Thee![^7956]

*Sticheron 3 (Resurrectional):* Beholding the Resurrection of the Creator, the Apostles were astonished, singing the angelic praise: this is the glory of the Church, this is the richness of the Kingdom! O Thou Who didst suffer for our sake: O Lord, glory to Thee![^7957]

*Glory... both now... Theotokion (Dogmatikon), Tone 7:* Truly dread and ineffable is the mystery wrought in thee, O Immaculate One! The Word Who is the Cause of all, above cause and word, being incarnate by the Holy Spirit, thou didst bear, taking flesh of thee, remaining unchangeably in His own nature; for when both came together subsistently in a single Hypostasis, twofold in nature He proceeds: perfect God and perfect man, manifest in both perfections by active properties; for having suffered upon the Cross in the flesh, He remained impassible in His Godhead; dying as man, as God He lived again on the third day, casting down the dominion of death, and delivering mankind from corruption. Him, as the Deliverer and Savior of our race, O Mother of God, do thou entreat, to send down upon us the great mercy of His tender compassions.[^7958]

*O Gladsome Light. Prokeimenon: "The Lord is King," three times. Vouchsafe, O Lord.*[^7959]

*At the Aposticha, Resurrection Sticheron, Tone 7:* Risen from the tomb, O Savior of the world, Thou didst raise up men together with Thy flesh: O Lord, glory to Thee![^7960]

*Other Stichera, to the Most Holy Theotokos.*

*Other Stichera, to the Most Holy Theotokos, Tone 7.*
*Tone 7, Podoben: "Having disregarded temporal things" (Неради́вше ѡ҆ вре́менныхъ):*

*Verse: I will remember thy name in every generation and generation [LXX Ps. 44:18].*[^7961]

*Sticheron 1:* Thou wast the East of the noetic Sun, O Virgin, in the setting of our nature; but as thou hast boldness, entreat Him, O all-hymned Mother of God: to free our souls from immeasurable transgressions.[^7962]

*Verse: Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear [LXX Ps. 44:11].*[^7963]

*Sticheron 2:* Clearly didst thou bud forth, O Virgin, as a rod from the root of Jesse, which destroyed the plant of deceit from the root; but as thou hast boldness, unceasingly pray, O All-hymned One, to uproot the passions of my heart, and to plant therein His fear, and to save me.[^7964]

*Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy countenance [LXX Ps. 44:13].*[^7965]

*Sticheron 3:* O all-holy Gate of God! Deliver me from the gates of hades, and show me the path of repentance, turning away from which the gates lead unto life; O guide of the lost, preserve the race of faithful men, and save our souls.[^7966]

*Glory... both now... Theotokion:* From thee, O all-holy Virgin Mother of God, was Christ our God ineffably born, truly being the pre-eternal God and a new man: being on the one hand eternal, and on the other having become man for our sake; for by Himself He saves the property of each nature: on the one hand shining forth in miracles, and on the other confirming by passions. Therefore being one and the same, He both dies as man and rises as God; entreat Him, O pure unwedded One, that our souls may be saved.[^7967]

*Then, Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart: Trisagion, and after Our Father: Troparion: "Thou didst shatter death by Thy Cross." Theotokion: "As the treasure of our resurrection." Litany and Dismissal.*[^7968]

*[Engraved Vignette: Small ornamental foliate tailpiece] On Saturday at Great Vespers.*
*On "Lord, I have cried," we set 10 verses, and sing Resurrection Stichera, Tone 7.*
*(Composition of John of Damascus):*[^7969]

*Sticheron 1 (Resurrectional):* Come, let us rejoice in the Lord, Who shattered the dominion of death and enlightened the human race, crying aloud with the Bodiless Powers: O our Creator and Savior, glory to Thee![^7970]

*Sticheron 2 (Resurrectional):* Thou didst endure the Cross and burial for our sake, O Savior, and by death, as God, Thou didst put death to death; therefore we worship Thy third-day Resurrection: O Lord, glory to Thee![^7971]

*Sticheron 3 (Resurrectional):* Beholding the Resurrection of the Creator, the Apostles were astonished, singing the angelic praise: this is the glory of the Church, this is the richness of the Kingdom! O Thou Who didst suffer for our sake: O Lord, glory to Thee![^7972]

*Other Stichera, Eastern (by Anatolius), in the same Tone:*

*Sticheron 4:* Even though Thou wast seized, O Christ, by lawless men, yet Thou art my God, and I am not ashamed; Thou wast struck upon the shoulders, and I deny Thee not; Thou wast nailed upon the Cross, and I conceal it not; in Thy Resurrection do I boast, for Thy death is my life. O Almighty Lord and Lover of mankind, glory to Thee![^7973]

*Sticheron 5:* Fulfilling David's prophecy, Christ revealed His majesty in Zion unto the disciples, showing Himself praised and ever glorified, with the Father and the Holy Spirit: first indeed bodiless as the Word, and afterwards incarnate for our sake, and put to death as man, and risen with power as the Lover of mankind.[^7974]

*Sticheron 6:* Thou didst descend into hades, O Christ, even as Thou didst will; Thou didst overthrow death, as God and Master; and Thou didst rise on the third day, raising Adam with Thyself from the bonds of hades and corruption...[^7975]

...crying aloud and saying: Glory to Thy Resurrection, O only Lover of mankind![^7976]

*Sticheron 7:* Thou wast laid in the tomb as one asleep, O Lord, and Thou didst rise on the third day as mighty in strength, raising Adam with Thyself from mortal corruption, as Thou art Almighty.[^7977]

*Other Stichera, to the Most Holy Theotokos (by Paul of Amorium), Tone 7.*[^7978]
*Tone 7, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*

*Sticheron 8 (Theotokion 1):* Thou art the joy of Angels, thou art the glory of men, thou art the hope of the faithful, O all-hymned Lady, our protectress; and unto thee do we flee in every need, that by thy supplications we all who hymn thee, O Bride of God, may be delivered from the soul-destroying arrows of the enemy and from all afflictions.[^7979]

*Sticheron 9 (Theotokion 2):* Thou art my hope, O Mother of God, thou art my protectress, and a wall and a refuge, O all-hymned Lady, who didst bear God in the flesh without man, the Savior of the world; do thou by thy supplications deliver us from the temptations, dangers, and distresses that encompass us, O only refuge of Christians.[^7980]

*Sticheron 10 (Theotokion 3):* Subdue the surgings of my flesh, quench the flame of my passions, take away from me, O Mother of God, the wicked burning of my desire; and turn my stubborn habit, O Virgin, from every demonic impulse, that in quietness of heart and in dispassion of my soul I may hymn thee, the all-hymned.[^7981]

*Glory... both now... Theotokion (Dogmatikon):* Thou wast known as a Mother above nature, O Mother of God, yet thou didst remain a virgin above word and reason; and the wonder of thy childbirth no tongue can tell; for since thy conceiving was all-glorious, O Pure One, incomprehensible is the manner of thy giving birth; for where God wills, the order of nature is overcome. Therefore, knowing thee to be the Mother of God, we all pray thee fervently: entreat Him that our souls may be saved.[^7982]

*O Gladsome Light. Prokeimenon of the day, and the rest as usual.*[^7983]

*At the Aposticha, Resurrection Stichera, Tone 7:*
*Sticheron 1:* Risen from the tomb, O Savior of the world, Thou didst raise up men together with Thy flesh: O Lord, glory to Thee![^7984]

*Other Stichera (Alphabetical):*
*Verse: The Lord is King, He is robed in majesty [LXX Ps. 92:1].*[^7985]

*Sticheron 2:* Come, let us worship Him Who rose from the dead and enlightened all things; for from the tyranny of hades He delivered us by His third-day Resurrection, granting us life and great mercy.[^7986]

*Verse: For He hath established the world, so that it cannot be moved [LXX Ps. 92:1].*[^7987]

*Sticheron 3:* Having descended into hades, O Christ, Thou didst lead captivity captive; and having risen on the third day, Thou didst raise us with Thyself, who glorify Thine all-powerful rising, O Lord and Lover of mankind.[^7988]

*Verse: Holiness becomes Thy house, O Lord, unto length of days [LXX Ps. 92:5].*[^7989]

*Sticheron 4:* Thou didst appear awesome, O Lord, lying in the tomb as one asleep; but having risen on the third day as mighty, Thou didst raise Adam with Thyself, who cried: Glory to Thy Resurrection, O only Lover of mankind![^7990]

*Glory... both now... Theotokion:* Beneath thy protection, O Lady, do all we earth-born flee, crying aloud unto thee: O Mother of God, our hope, deliver us from immeasurable transgressions, and save our souls.[^7991]

*Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart: Trisagion, and after Our Father: we sing the Resurrectional Troparion, Tone 7:*
*Resurrectional Troparion, Tone 7:* Thou didst destroy death by Thy Cross, Thou didst open paradise to the thief, Thou didst change the weeping of the Myrrh-bearers, and didst command Thine Apostles to preach: that Thou art risen, O Christ God, granting unto the world great mercy.[^7992]

*Glory... both now... Theotokion:* As the treasure of our resurrection, O All-hymned One, lead up from the pit and the depth of transgressions those who hope in thee; for thou hast saved those guilty of sin, having given birth to our Salvation: who before childbirth wast a Virgin, and in childbirth a Virgin, and after childbirth still remainest a Virgin.[^7993]

*[Engraved Vignette: Ornamental foliate divider]*

*On Saturday at Compline.*
*Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos, Tone 7.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:* Unto Him Who shattered warfare with His arm, and submerged the three-tiered chariot riders, let us sing as unto our Deliverer God, for He hath been glorified.[^7994]

*Refrain: Most Holy Lady Theotokos, save us.*[^7995]

*Troparion 1:* As an adornment with singing, and a God-befitting song of thanksgiving, we bring gifts unto thee: the "Rejoice," now, O Pure One, for from sorrow thou hast bestowed joy upon us.[^7996]

*Troparion 2:* The grace of thy mercy and the strength of thy protection we will not keep silent, O most pure Virgin; for from cruel distresses thou hast saved us.[^7997]

*Troparion 3:* Having been delivered from various temptations and afflictions by thy maternal prayers, O Most Pure One, with one accord and fervently we all sing songs of thanksgiving unto thee.[^7998]

*Both now:* Variously adorned with fringes, as with golden virtues and with the graces of the Spirit, O Most Pure One, having adorned thyself as the Bride of the Father, thou hast truly been shown forth as the Mother of God.[^7999]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:* O Lord and Savior, Who in the beginning didst establish the heavens by Thy all-powerful Word, and all the host thereof by the all-effecting and Divine Spirit: establish me upon the unshakable rock of the confession of Thee.[^8000]

*Troparion 1:* Diligently do we offer voices of thanksgiving unto the majesty of divine joy, as unto the cause of our gladness from the beginning, honoring her as our protectress.[^8001]

*Troparion 2:* Having been delivered from distresses through thee, and having obtained joy for thy sake, O unwedded Mother, we all glorify thee as the good bestower and lauded protectress.[^8002]

*Glory:* Receiving the transformation of our transgressions and adversities through thy divine prayer, O Mother of Christ God, we faithfully hymn Thee with thankful voices, as the cause of good things.[^8003]

*Both now:* She who is the fountain of joy ever pours forth streams of immortality, and herself saves all, as an ever-living thanksgiving unto us, the Mother of Christ God.[^8004]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:* The virtue of Thine ineffable wisdom, O Christ God, hath covered the heavens by Thy dispensation, O Lover of mankind.[^8005]

*Troparion 1:* Rejoicing, we offer unto thee a worthy song of rejoicing, O pure Virgin, having been delivered from distresses by thy prayers.[^8006]

*Troparion 2:* With thanksgiving, O pure Virgin, we bring forth a hymn unto thee with hands of the soul, leaping for joy with divine songs, having been delivered from much sorrow.[^8007]

*Glory:* Passionate sins have raised up many distresses against us; but by thy divine protection, O Pure One, deliver us.[^8008]

*Both now:* Blessed truly are they that honor thee, O most pure Mother of God, for through thee have we been delivered from sin and sorrow.[^8009]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:* Night without light is unto the unbelieving, O Christ, but illumination unto the faithful in the sweetness of Thy words; therefore I rise early at dawn unto Thee, and hymn Thy Divinity.[^8010]

*Troparion 1:* Thou didst give birth, O Virgin, unto Christ the consumer of sin, by Whom the world was saved from adversities and sicknesses;...[^8011]

...therefore, "Rejoice!" we also cry unto thee, having been delivered from sorrows.[^8012]

*Troparion 2:* Encompassed by various adversities, O pure Sovereign Lady, and by sorrow and affliction and grievous circumstance, in our despair we found thee as the hope of gladness.[^8013]

*Glory:* As a treasury of salvation for us thy servants, O Pure One, thou drivest away adversities and keepest us unharmed; therefore, partakers of thy many good things, we thank thee with songs.[^8014]

*Both now:* We thank thee, having been delivered through thee from many sins, and weaknesses and sicknesses, and grievous ailments, O most pure Sovereign Lady; for thou art a steadfast hope unto thy faithful servants.[^8015]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:* Fallen into the depth of sins, O Good One, as Jonah from the sea monster I cry aloud unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, and save me, O Lover of mankind.[^8016]

*Troparion 1:* Angelic tongues cannot worthily sing thy praises, O Pure One; yet we now, undertaking as servants, bring Gabriel's greeting unto thee.[^8017]

*Troparion 2:* Having fallen into the depth of sorrow and tribulation through our sins, we have been delivered through thee from distress and adversities, O Virgin, pure Mother of God.[^8018]

*Glory:* The whole world hath been made debtor, O Pure One, to give thanks, and praise, and piously glorify thy grace; for through thee have we been delivered from perils and sorrows.[^8019]

*Both now:* Both in night and in day, openly and in secret, we who faithfully glorify thee flee beneath thy protection, O most pure Virgin.[^8020]

*Lord, have mercy, three times. Glory... both now...*[^8021]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 7:* O Lord, we are Thy people, and the sheep of Thy pasture: as a Shepherd turn us who have gone astray; gather us who have been scattered by corruption; have mercy on Thy flock, O Lover of mankind; have compassion on Thy people, through the prayers of the Mother of God, O Thou Who alone art without sin.[^8022]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:* Cast into the fiery furnace, the venerable Children turned the fire into dew, crying aloud thus with singing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers.[^8023]

*Troparion 1:* A thankful rejoicing do we bring unto thee, O Mother of God, for truly through thee have we been delivered from every evil undertaking; and with one accord we sing unto thee: Blessed art thou.[^8024]

*Troparion 2:* At evening we took up our abode in weeping of sorrows, and in expectation of evils: but by thy God-befitting shelter, O Virgin, having been deified, we found joy in the morning; for thou hast saved us.[^8025]

*Glory:* Having all acquired thy protection toward God as a divine refuge, in adversities and persecutions and sins we flee unto thee, and through thee receive transformation, O Most Pure One.[^8026]

*Both now:* The grace of thy prayer, O Pure One, we proclaim with lips and with spirit, O Glorious One: for for thy sake are we all delivered from adversities and tempest and grievous sorrows, and the passions of sin.[^8027]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:* Him Who is awesome unto the Cherubim, and marvelous unto the Seraphim, and the Creator of the world: ye priests and servants, and spirits of the righteous, sing, bless, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^8028]

*Troparion 1:* Having been delivered from the tempest of sin, and from passions, and from adversities by thy prayers, O good Mother of God, with a thankful voice we cry aloud unto thee: "Rejoice!" for through thee have we passed from sorrow into joy.[^8029]

*Troparion 2:* Despise not those held fast in sicknesses and adversities, O Good One: but giving ear unto our poor supplication, free us from great afflictions, that we may faithfully hymn thy mercy, O Pure One.[^8030]

*Glory:* O cause of the dissolution of transgressions, raise us up now from sorrows, adversities, and passions of men, and from unseemly temptation; and by thy divine supplications, O Mother of God, most gloriously deliver us from them.[^8031]

*Both now:* Thy compassions are ever sent down upon all, O Christ, truly by grace and by the supplications of her that bare Thee; for from Thee, O merciful Savior, do we Christians receive Thy mercy.[^8032]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:* Her that is a Mother above nature, and a Virgin according to nature, the only blessed one among women, let us the faithful magnify with songs as the Mother of God.[^8033]

*Troparion 1:* A worthy rejoicing, with a voice of acclamation, do we now offer unto thee, O Virgin, with the Angel...[^8034]

...Gabriel, having been delivered from various temptations, O Mother of God, by thy prayers.[^8035]

*Troparion 2:* Divine joy and gladness and exultation, O Virgin that knewest not man, hath multiplied unto us from God; for lo, we who weep grievously rejoice by thy prayers.[^8036]

*Glory:* I will sacrifice a sacrifice of praise, and with tongue and voice diligently render a song of thanksgiving unto thee, O Virgin, that praying unto thee, I may be delivered through thee in the day of affliction.[^8037]

*Both now:* We piously rejoice together, O Most Pure One, in thy divine Childbearing; for thou hast gushed forth joy for us from adversities and sorrows. Therefore unto thee do we also thankfully accomplish a hymn, faithfully praising thee.[^8038]

*It is truly meet: Trisagion Prayers, Our Father: Troparia and the rest.*[^8039]

*On Sunday Morning at the Midnight Office.*[^8040]
*Canon to the Most Holy and Life-Originating Trinity. (The acrostic whereof is: I praise the Trinity, the monarchical nature.) A composition of Metrophanes.*[^8041]
*Tone 7. Ode 1. Heirmos:* By Thy nod the watery nature, formerly flowing easily, was transformed into dry land, O Lord. Therefore Israel, having journeyed on foot dry-shod, sings unto Thee a song of victory.[^8042]

*Refrain: Most Holy Trinity our God, glory to Thee.*[^8043]

*Troparion 1:* Open Thou the noetic mouth of my heart, and my material lips unto Thy praise, O thrice-radiant single Godhead of all: to sing unto Thee, O Author of Light, a song of thanksgiving.[^8044]

*Troparion 2:* That Thou mightest show forth the superabundant riches of Thy goodness, O Trinity of immeasurable power, Thou didst create man, an earthly image of Thy sovereign Lordship, O Creator.[^8045]

*Troparion 3:* O Unoriginate Mind, Who didst beget the co-ever-existing Word, and didst cause to shine forth the co-unoriginate Spirit: vouchsafe us to worship conformably the One God by essence, in three Hypostases.[^8046]

*Theotokion:* Thou didst appear unto Moses at the bush, O Word of God, as a cleansing fire that consumed not at all, prefiguring Thine incarnation, whereby Thou didst fashion men anew.[^8047]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:* O Lord and Savior, Who in the beginning didst establish the heavens by Thy all-powerful Word, and all the host thereof by the all-effecting and Divine Spirit: establish me upon the unshakable rock of the confession of Thee...[^8048]

...and all the host thereof by the all-effecting and Divine Spirit: establish me upon the unshakable rock of the confession of Thee.[^8049]

*Troparion 1:* Hymning Thee, the single, thrice-radiant, and all-effecting Master, we ask deliverance from sins and temptations, O God of immeasurable power: therefore despise not those who praise Thy goodness in faith.[^8050]

*Troparion 2:* A branch hath appeared from the Father, as from an unoriginate root, God the Word, equal in power with the co-sprouting and Divine Spirit; and therefore we the faithful glorify the one Lordship in threefold Persons.[^8051]
