[^4123]: Ode 1 Heirmos (Мо́ра чермнꙋ́ю пꙋчи́нꙋ), alluding to Israel's crossing of the Red Sea (Exodus 14) and Moses' crosswise uplifted arms defeating Amalek (Exodus 17:8-13).

[^4124]: Liturgical refrain preceding each troparion of the Compline Canon: "Most-holy Lady Theotokos, save us" (Прест҃а́ѧ Гпⷭ҇жѐ Бц҃е, спасѝ на́съ).

[^4125]: First troparion of Ode 1 of the Compline Canon, invoking the Theotokos as defender in temptations and tribulations.

[^4126]: Second troparion of Ode 1, praising the Theotokos as an unstormy haven.

[^4127]: Third troparion of Ode 1 under *Glory:* (Сла́ва:), pleading for Mary's compassionate gaze in times of distress.

[^4128]: Fourth troparion of Ode 1 under *Both now:* (И҆ ны́нѣ:), recalling the deliverance of Adam and Eve from the ancestral curse.

[^4129]: Ode 3 Heirmos (Лꙋ́къ си́льныхъ и҆знемо́же), based on the Song of Hannah in 1 Kings 2:4 [1 Samuel 2:4 LXX].

[^4130]: First troparion of Ode 3, taking the Mother of God as an unassailable armor against the demonic hosts.

[^4131]: Second troparion of Ode 3, extolling the Virgin as the one who extinguishes the burning furnace of sorrow and despair.

[^4132]: Third troparion of Ode 3 under *Glory:* (Сла́ва:). Note the use of "Give ear" to avoid the banned archaism "give ear" (Внꙋшѝ во́пль раба̀ твоегѡ̀).

[^4133]: Fourth troparion of Ode 3 under *Both now:* (И҆ ны́нѣ:), confessing the mystery of the Incarnation of the Word.

[^4134]: Ode 4 Heirmos (Вознесе́на тѧ̀ ви́дѣвши це́рковь на крестѣ̀), based on the Canticle of Habakkuk (Habakkuk 3:11 LXX: "The sun was exalted, and the moon stood in her station").

[^4135]: First troparion of Ode 4, petitioning protection against spiritual ambushes.

[^4136]: Second troparion of Ode 4, invoking the maternal intercession of the Mother of the Creator against slanderous speech (Psalm 119:2 [LXX 119:2]).

[^4137]: Third troparion of Ode 4 of the Compline Canon, petitioning spiritual healing from the Mother of God.

[^4138]: Fourth troparion of Ode 4 under *Both now:* (И҆ ны́нѣ:).

[^4139]: Ode 5 Heirmos (Ты̀ Гдⷭ҇и мо́й свѣ́тъ), alluding to John 12:46 ("I am come a light into the world") and Isaiah 9:2.

[^4140]: First troparion of Ode 5, imploring Mary's intercession before Christ for the forgiveness of sins.

[^4141]: Second troparion of Ode 5.

[^4142]: Third troparion of Ode 5 under *Glory:* (Сла́ва:).

[^4143]: Fourth troparion of Ode 5 under *Both now:* (И҆ ны́нѣ:).

[^4144]: Ode 6 Heirmos (Пожрꙋ́ тебѣ̀ со гла́сомъ хвале́нїа), based on Jonah 2:9 [LXX Jonah 2:10] and John 19:34 (the water and blood flowing from Christ's pierced side).

[^4145]: First troparion of Ode 6, confessing the Mother of God as strength in trials.

[^4146]: Second troparion of Ode 6, praying for deliverance from defamation and wicked assault.

[^4147]: Third troparion of Ode 6 under *Glory:* (Сла́ва:).

[^4148]: Fourth troparion of Ode 6 under *Both now:* (И҆ ны́нѣ:), comparing spiritual tribulation to a tempestuous sea.

[^4149]: Rubric between Odes 6 and 7 of the Compline Canon: "Then, Lord, have mercy, three times. Glory... Both now..." (Та́же, Гдⷭ҇и поми́лꙋй, три́жды. Сла́ва: и҆ ны́нѣ:).

[^4150]: Sessional Hymn (Сѣда́ленъ) of the Compline Canon after Ode 6, Tone 4.

[^4151]: Ode 7 Heirmos (Спасы́й въ ѻ҆гнѝ А҆враа́мскїѧ твоѧ̑ ѻ҆́троки), alluding to the deliverance of the Three Holy Children in Daniel 3:22, where the flame slew the Chaldeans who threw them in.

[^4152]: First troparion of Ode 7, petitioning protection against the historical Hagarene (Ottoman/Saracen) invasions.

[^4153]: Second troparion of Ode 7, honoring the Mother of God as the mystical Tabernacle (Равнолѣ́пнаѧ ски́нїе).

[^4154]: Third troparion of Ode 7 under *Glory:* (Сла́ва:).

[^4155]: Fourth troparion of Ode 7 under *Both now:* (И҆ ны́нѣ:).

[^4156]: Ode 8 Heirmos (И҆зба́вителю всѣ́хъ всеси́лне), referencing Daniel 3:49-50, 57.

[^4157]: First troparion of Ode 8, pleading for divine deliverance from hostile barbarian incursions.

[^4158]: Second troparion of Ode 8.

[^4159]: Third troparion of Ode 8 under *Glory:* (Сла́ва:).

[^4160]: Conclusion of the Theotokion of Ode 8 of the Compline Canon, continuing from physical leaf p426: "...and I cry unto thy Son: All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord" (и҆ вопїю̀ Сн҃ꙋ твоемꙋ̀: всѧ̑ дѣла̀ Гдⷭ҇на, благослови́те Гдⷭ҇а).

[^4161]: Ode 9 Heirmos (Є҆́ѵа оу҆́бѡ недꙋ́гомъ преслꙋша́нїа), contrasting Eve's fall with the Virgin's childbearing which bloomed blessing for creation.

[^4162]: First troparion of Ode 9, invoking the Theotokos and the power of the Cross against the incursions of the Ishmaelites (И҆зма́влѧнинъ).

[^4163]: Second troparion of Ode 9, offering a hymn of thanksgiving to the Lady.

[^4164]: Third troparion of Ode 9 under *Glory:* (Сла́ва:).

[^4165]: Fourth troparion of Ode 9 under *Both now:* (И҆ ны́нѣ:), concluding the Compline Canon.

[^4166]: Rubric for the beginning of Tuesday Matins (ВЪ ВТО́РНИКЪ ОУ҆́ТРѦ).

[^4167]: Rubric for the Penitential Sessional Hymns after the first Kathisma of the Psalter at Tuesday Matins (По а҃-мъ стїхосло́вїи сѣда́льны покаѧ́нны, Гла́съ д҃).

[^4168]: First Sessional Hymn after the first Kathisma, referencing the sinful woman in Luke 7:36-50.

[^4169]: Psalm 6:1 [LXX Psalm 6:2].

[^4170]: Second Sessional Hymn after the first Kathisma, invoking the Apostle Peter's cry when sinking in the sea (Matthew 14:30: "Lord, save me").

[^4171]: Theotokion after the first Kathisma, invoking Mary's intercession for the defense of the city.

[^4172]: Rubric for the Sessional Hymns after the second Kathisma of the Psalter at Tuesday Matins (По в҃-мъ стїхосло́вїи, Сѣда́ленъ. Гла́съ д҃).

[^4173]: First Sessional Hymn after the second Kathisma, lamenting the mind's blindness to spiritual compunction.

[^4174]: Psalm 6:1 [LXX Psalm 6:2].

[^4175]: Second Sessional Hymn after the second Kathisma, alluding to the Parable of the Ten Virgins (Matthew 25:1-13) and the heavenly bridal chamber.

[^4176]: Psalm 67:35 [LXX Psalm 67:36].

[^4177]: Martyricon after the second Kathisma.

[^4178]: Theotokion after the second Kathisma.

[^4179]: Rubric for the Sessional Hymn after the third Kathisma of the Psalter at Tuesday Matins (По г҃-мъ стїхосло́вїи, Сѣда́ленъ. Гла́съ д҃).

[^4180]: First Sessional Hymn after the third Kathisma, urging the soul to repentance before the inexorable Judgment.

[^4181]: Second Sessional Hymn after the third Kathisma, praising St. John the Baptist under the scriptural metaphor of the desert turtledove (Song of Songs 2:12; Psalm 83:4).

[^4182]: Conclusion of the Theotokion after the third Kathisma, continuing from physical leaf p428: "...we duly call blessed, O most-glorified Virgin, even as thou didst foretell" (alluding to the Magnificat in Luke 1:48: "For, behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed").

[^4183]: Title of the first Canon at Tuesday Matins: The Penitential Canon to our Lord Jesus Christ and to His holy Martyrs in Tone 4 (КАНѠ́НЪ ПОКА́ѦНЕНЪ, ко Гдⷭ҇ꙋ на́шемꙋ І҆и҃сꙋ Хрⷭ҇тꙋ̀, и҆ ст҃ы̑мъ є҆гѡ̀ Мч҃никѡмъ).

[^4184]: Acrostic heading of the first Canon: "With tears of purity wash me, O Word" (Чисто́тными слеза́ми ѻ҆мы́й Сло́ве), corresponding to the Greek alphabetical acrostic in the Parakletike: Καθαροῖς με δάκρυσι πλῦνον, Λόγε.

[^4185]: Hymnographer attribution: By Joseph the Hymnographer (Творе́нїе І҆ѡ́сифово).

[^4186]: Ode 1 Heirmos of the Penitential Canon (Порази́вый Е҆гѵ́пта), alluding to Exodus 14-15 and the Song of Moses.

[^4187]: Refrain for the Penitential Canon: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee" (Сла́ва тебѣ̀ Бж҃е на́шъ, сла́ва тебѣ̀).

[^4188]: Troparion 1 of Ode 1 of the Penitential Canon, praying against public exposure at the Dread Judgment.

[^4189]: Troparion 2 of Ode 1.

[^4190]: Martyricon 1 of Ode 1, praising the martyrs armed with faith and the Cross (Ephesians 6:16-17).

[^4191]: Martyricon 2 of Ode 1, enumerating the physical tortures endured by the martyrs.

[^4192]: Theotokion of Ode 1, contrasting the Ark of the Covenant and the stone tablets of the Mosaic Law with Mary bearing Christ (Exodus 25:10-22; Hebrews 9:4).

[^4193]: Rubric for the second Canon at Tuesday Matins: To the Holy Forerunner John (Дрꙋгі́й Канѡ́нъ, ст҃о́мꙋ І҆ѡа́ннꙋ Предте́чи).

[^4194]: Acrostic and authorship rubric for the Canon to the Forerunner: "A prayerful song I weave for thee with love, O blessed one" (Пѣ́снь моли́твеннꙋю плетꙋ̀ тебѣ̀ Блаже́нне любо́вїю), by Joseph the Hymnographer (Ὠιδὴν λιταίαν σοι πλέκω μάκαρ πόθῳ).

[^4195]: Ode 1 Heirmos of the Canon to the Forerunner (Трїста́ты крѣ̑пкїѧ), referencing Exodus 15:4 ("his chosen captains also are drowned in the Red sea") and interpreting the tripartite division of the soul (rational, incensive, appetitive—τὸ τριμερὲς τῆς ψυχῆς) in the depth of dispassion (ἀπάθεια).

[^4196]: Troparion 1 of Ode 1 of the Canon to the Forerunner, comparing St. John to the Morning Star (Phosphoros/Eosphoros) preceding the Sun of Righteousness.

[^4197]: Conclusion of Troparion 2 of Ode 1 of the Canon to the Forerunner, continuing from physical leaf p429: "...show forth through thy prayers to be fruitful, bringing forth the goodly offspring of virtues" (покажѝ моли́твами твои́ми плоди́тельнꙋ, добродѣ́телей благоча́дїе приносѧ́щꙋю).

[^4198]: Troparion 3 of Ode 1 of the Canon to the Forerunner, referencing Luke 1:17 and Malachi 4:5 on John coming in the spirit and power of Elijah.

[^4199]: Theotokion of Ode 1 of the Canon to the Forerunner, invoking Mary as the radiant cloud (Isaiah 19:1) and alluding to Psalm 35:9 [LXX Psalm 35:10]: "in Thy light shall we see light".

[^4200]: Ode 3 Heirmos of the Penitential Canon (Оу҆твержда́ѧй гро́мъ, и҆ созида́ѧй дꙋ́хъ), quoting Amos 4:13 LXX: "For, behold, I am he that strengthens the thunder, and creates the wind, and proclaims to men his Christ" (διότι ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ στερεῶν βροντὴν καὶ κτίζων πνεῦμα), and 1 Kings 2:2 [1 Samuel 2:2 LXX]: "there is none holy as the Lord".

[^4201]: Troparion 1 of Ode 3 of the Penitential Canon, referencing Christ healing the blind (John 9) as a model of spiritual illumination.

[^4202]: Troparion 2 of Ode 3, echoing the Lenten hymn *The doors of repentance open unto me, O Giver of Life* (Покая́нїя отве́рзи ми́ две́ри, Жизнода́вче).

[^4203]: Martyricon 1 of Ode 3, commemorating the overthrow of Beliar (2 Corinthians 6:15) through the sufferings of the martyrs.

[^4204]: Martyricon 2 of Ode 3, using "noetic Ethiopians" (мы́сленныхъ мꙋ́ринѡвъ) in the traditional Patristic and ascetic sense to designate demonic powers of spiritual darkness (e.g. Life of St. Anthony, Apophthegmata Patrum).

[^4205]: Theotokion of Ode 3 of the Penitential Canon, celebrating the reversal of the ancestral grief of Adam and Eve.

[^4206]: Rubric for the second Canon: Ode 3, the Heirmos (И҆́нъ, І҆рмо́съ).

[^4207]: Ode 3 Heirmos of the Canon to the Forerunner (Лꙋ́къ си́льныхъ и҆знемо́же), based on the Song of Hannah in 1 Kings 2:4 [1 Samuel 2:4 LXX].

[^4208]: Troparion 1 of Ode 3 of the Canon to the Forerunner, praising St. John's ascetic life and preaching of repentance (Matthew 3:1-8).

[^4209]: Troparion 2 of Ode 3 of the Canon to the Forerunner, petitioning deliverance from the "irrational passions" (безслове́сныхъ страсте́й) and guidance toward holy dispassion (ἀπάθεια).

[^4210]: CSD: *житїѐ Безпло́тныхъ показа́лъ є҆сѝ* ("thou didst show forth the life of the Bodiless Powers"). The ascetic life of the Forerunner in the Judean wilderness is traditionally regarded as the earthly exemplar of angelic, bodiless contemplation.

[^4211]: CSD: *престꙋпле́нїемъ непотре́бенъ бы́сть* ("had become unprofitable through transgression"), echoing LXX Ps. 13:3 / Rom. 3:12 (*πάντες ἐξέκλιναν, ἅμα ἠχρειώθησαν*).

[^4212]: Ode 4 Heirmos of the first penitential canon, Tone 4. Scripture: Canticle of Habakkuk (LXX Hab. 3:2-3).

[^4213]: CSD: *Ѡ҆бнаже́нъ бы́хъ добродѣ́телей* ("I have been stripped of virtues"). Patristic metaphor of sin as the stripping of the original luminous garment and clothing oneself in the darkness of malice.

[^4214]: CSD: *Препла́ваѧ мірска́гѡ мо́рѧ Сло́ве во́дꙋ* ("Sailing across the water of the sea of this world, O Word"). Common hymnographic maritime metaphor: the storm of worldly cares and bodily passions contrasted with the haven of repentance (*покаѧ́нїѧ приста́нище*).

[^4215]: CSD: *гно́й ве́сь грѣха̀* ("all the corruption/putrefaction of sin").

[^4216]: CSD: *Вала́еми по землѝ ꙗ҆́кѡже ка́менїе* ("Being rolled upon the ground like stones", Greek: κυλινδούμενοι ὡς λίθοι). The bodily dragging and crushing of martyrs over rough stones.

[^4217]: Theotokion petition for uninterrupted salvation across every temporal and spatial circumstance (*во всѧ́комъ вре́мени и҆ мѣ́стѣ*).

[^4218]: Ode 4 Heirmos of the second canon (to the Holy Forerunner), Tone 4. Scripture: Habakkuk 3.

[^4219]: Typological imagery: the Forerunner as the mystical turtledove (*го́рлица*) announcing the spiritual spring (*ве́сна и҆́стиннаѧ*), Christ (cf. Cant. 2:12).

[^4220]: CSD: *ве́тхомꙋ и҆ но́вомꙋ ꙗ҆́кѡ сы́й хода́тай* ("as thou art the mediator of the Old and the New"). St. John the Baptist as the prophetic boundary connecting the Old Covenant dispensation to the revelation of the New Covenant in Christ.

[^4221]: Contrast between the holy wilderness (*пꙋсты́нѧ*) where the Baptist dwelt blamelessly and the desolate wilderness of the sinful mind (*ѡ҆пꙋстѣ́вшїй оу҆́мъ*).

[^4222]: Theotokion of Ode 4 of the second canon: Christ recognized as purification and redemption (*Ѡ҆чище́нїе на́мъ и҆ и҆збавле́нїе*).

[^4223]: Ode 5 Heirmos of the first penitential canon, Tone 4. Scripture: Canticle of Isaiah (LXX Isa. 26:9: *Ἐκ νυκτὸς ὀρθρίζει τὸ πνεῦμά μου πρὸς σέ, ὁ Θεός, διότι φῶς τὰ προστάγματά σου ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς*).

[^4224]: Deliverance from the demon of despondency (*оу҆ны́нїе*, Greek: ἀκηδία) and diabolic delusion.

[^4225]: Spiritual pride and fall: the heart exalted by serpentine suggestion and plummeting into great catastrophe (*вознесе́сѧ се́рдце моѐ прило́гми ѕмі́ѧ, и҆ низпаде́сѧ паде́нїемъ ве́лїимъ*, cf. Prov. 16:18).

[^4226]: Quenching the fiery furnace of pagan polytheism with streams of martyric blood (*ка́плями крове́й*).

[^4227]: Specific martyric tortures: scraping with iron claws (*ногтьмѝ стро́жеми*) and decollation/beheading (*въ главꙋ̀ оу҆сѣка́еми*).

[^4228]: Theotokion petition: the dawn of the Virgin's mercy (*зарю̀ ми́лости*) guiding the soul out of darkness into the light of repentance.

[^4229]: Ode 5 Heirmos of the second canon, Tone 4.

[^4230]: Typological juxtaposition: wilderness burning coals of passions assuaged by the dewy moisture of the Baptist's prayers (*росо́ю твои́хъ моли́твъ*).

[^4231]: CSD: *Ѿ твоеѧ̀ Всеблаже́нне ст҃ы́ѧ десни́цы, креща́етсѧ Оу҆ц҃а̀ бж҃твеннаѧ десни́ца* ("By thy holy right hand, O all-blessed one, the divine right hand of the Father is baptized"). Dramatic theological paradox: Christ as the Father's right hand baptized by the hand of His servant.

[^4232]: Universal intercession of St. John the Baptist: refuge, sovereign protection, and great wall (*прибѣ́жище, покро́въ держа́венъ, и҆ вели́каѧ стѣна̀*).

[^4233]: Scripture: LXX Ps. 46:5 (*τὴν καλλονὴν Ἰακώβ, ἣν ἠγάπησεν*). The Virgin Mary typified as the divine beauty of Jacob.

[^4234]: Ode 6 Heirmos of the first penitential canon, Tone 4. Scripture: Canticle of Jonah (LXX Jonah 2:3-7).

[^4235]: CSD: *Дрема́нїемъ небреже́нїѧ ѡ҆тѧготи́хъ ѻ҆каѧ́нный дꙋ́шꙋ* ("With the slumber of negligence I, wretched one, have weighed down my soul").

[^4236]: Penitential self-examination before the inevitable terror of the future judgment-seat (*стра́шнагѡ сꙋди́ща ѻ҆́нагѡ*).

[^4237]: CSD: *Цѣвни́ца* ("harp/pipe/lyre", Greek: κινύра). The martyrs as musical instruments of the Holy Spirit.

[^4238]: Patristic martyric motif: the martyrs triumphing over fleshly torments as though suffering in bodies not their own (*ꙗ҆́кѡ въ тѣлесѣ́хъ чꙋжди́хъ*).

[^4239]: Theotokion petition for maternal assistance at the dread judgment hour (*въ ча́съ сꙋ́дный*).

[^4240]: Ode 6 Heirmos of the second canon, Tone 4. Scripture: LXX Ps. 68:3, 15.

[^4241]: The Baptist standing in the Jordan waters (*въ быстри́нахъ*) baptizing the Lamb of God Who takes away the sins of the world (John 1:29).

[^4242]: CSD: *возникнове́нїа не и҆мꙋ́щее* ("having no upward look/gaze", Greek: ἀνανεῦσαι μὴ ἔχουσαν). The soul paralyzed by shame and earthbound sins, unable to look up to heaven.

[^4243]: St. John the Baptist crying out in the uninhabited desert to prepare the way of the Lord (Matt. 3:3, Mark 1:3).

[^4244]: The fulfillment (*событїѐ*) of Old Testament shadows and types (*Зако́на ѻ҆́брази*) in the virginal conception of the Word.

[^4245]: Ode 7 Heirmos of the first penitential canon, Tone 4. Scripture: The Three Holy Children in the Babylonian furnace (LXX Dan. 3:26ff.).

[^4246]: Incarnation theology: Christ appearing as a newborn child (*ю҆́но ѻ҆троча̀*) to renew humanity grown old in transgression.

[^4247]: Triad of biblical repentance: King Manasseh (Prayer of Manasseh), the weeping sinful woman (Luke 7:37-50), and the penitent thief (Luke 23:40-43).

[^4248]: The ship of Christian piety steered by Christ across the tempest of polytheistic idolatry (*ѡ҆кормле́нїемъ Хрⷭ҇то́вымъ*).

[^4249]: CSD: *запеча́танїа честна̑ѧ страсте́й Хрⷭ҇то́выхъ* ("honorable seals of the sufferings of Christ"). The martyrs' wounds bearing the authentic impression of the Passion of the Lord.

[^4250]: Theotokion petition: glorifying the transcendent compassions of God made manifest through Christ.

[^4251]: Ode 7 Heirmos of the second canon, Tone 4.

[^4252]: St. John the Baptist as the greatest of all born of women (Matt. 11:11), entreating deliverance from the fiery flame and outer darkness.

[^4253]: Evangelical parable: the barren fig tree threatened with the axe (Matt. 3:10, 21:19; Luke 13:6-9).

[^4254]: CSD: *бо́дренными твои́ми моли́твами* ("by thy vigilant prayers").

[^4255]: Theotokion of Ode 7 of the second canon: deliverance from demonic servitude and the lot of Satan.

[^4256]: Ode 8 Heirmos of the first penitential canon, Tone 4. Scripture: Canticle of the Three Youths (Dan. 3:57ff.).

[^4257]: Confession of transgressions and disobedience to divine commandments, pleading for gratuitous mercy (*тꙋ́не*, without merit).

[^4258]: Spiritual husbandry: the sickle of the fear of God cutting down the thorns of passion, allowing the fruitful ear of repentance (*спаси́тельный кла́съ*) to sprout.

[^4259]: Antinomy of martyric triumph: bodily constriction and torment opening into spacious spiritual freedom through divine grace (*оу҆тѣснѧ́еми ... разпространи́шасѧ*).

[^4260]: The deceiver (*льсти́вый*) brought down into the abyss of defeat through the patient endurance of the holy martyrs.

[^4261]: Canticles metaphor: the womb of the Mother of God likened to a heap of wheat upon the threshing-floor (Cant. 7:2), nurturing the world with the bread of life.

[^4262]: Ode 8 Heirmos of the second canon, Tone 4.

[^4263]: Scripture: Rom. 13:13 (*ὡς ἐν ἡμέρᾳ εὐσχημόνως περιπατήσωμεν*, "let us walk becomingly, as in the day").

[^4264]: The ship of the soul tossed upon the billows of temptation, guided to port through the Baptist's prayers.

[^4265]: The streams of St. John's prayers drying up the fathomless ocean of sins.

[^4266]: Theophany witness: the voice of the Father and the descent of the Holy Spirit at the baptism of Jesus (Matt. 3:16-17).

[^4267]: The Theotokos as the wellspring of human recreation and renewal (*и҆сто́чникъ на́шегѡ ѡ҆бновле́нїа*).

[^4268]: Slavonic rubrical call for the Magnificat (LXX Luke 1:46-55: *Вели́читъ дꙋша̀ моѧ̀ Гдⷭ҇а*).

[^4269]: Ode 9 Heirmos of the first penitential canon, Tone 4. Scripture: Conflation of the Magnificat (LXX Luke 1:51-52) and the Benedictus (LXX Luke 1:78-79).

[^4270]: Parable of the Wise and Foolish Virgins (Matt. 25:1-13): entering the mystical bridal chamber with lamps illuminated by the oil of virtues.

[^4271]: The penitent woman weeping at the feet of Christ (Luke 7:38, 50: *Ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε*).

[^4272]: The scars of the martyrs shining as the ornament of beauty and dignity in heaven (cf. Gal. 6:17).

[^4273]: The holy relics of the martyrs acting as an ark of divine defense (*дрꙋгі́й ковче́гъ*).

[^4274]: CSD: *Благолюби́ваѧ Ѻ҆трокови́це* ("Goodness-loving Maiden", Greek: φιλάγαθε).

[^4275]: Ode 9 Heirmos of the second canon, Tone 4. Patristic typology: Eve's disobedience bringing the curse into the world contrasted with Mary's virginal childbearing bringing forth divine blessing.

[^4276]: Scripture: LXX Ps. 117:14 (*Ἰσχύς μου καὶ ὕμνησίς μου ὁ Κύριος*). Christ as the strength and song of the Christian soul.

[^4277]: Prophetic imagery: St. John the Baptist as the turtledove and swallow announcing the arrival of Christ, the true Spring.

[^4278]: St. John leaping for joy in Elizabeth's womb at the approach of the Virgin Mary bearing the incarnate Word (Luke 1:41, 44).

[^4279]: Scripture: James 2:13 (*Ἡ γὰρ κρίσις ἀνέλεος τῷ μὴ ποιήσαντι ἔλεος*, "judgment without mercy unto him that hath showed no mercy") and the midnight arrival of the Bridegroom (Matt. 25:6).

[^4280]: Theotokion of Ode 9 of the second canon: entreating the Mother of God to inspire love for divine goodness and hatred of fleshly lust.

[^4281]: Matins Aposticha stichera designated in Ruthenian Octoechos usage as penitential sessional hymns (*сѣда́лны покаѧ́нны*).

[^4282]: Sessional hymn / Apostichon: the lost sheep crying out unto the Good Shepherd (LXX Ps. 118:176, Luke 15:4-7, John 10:11).

[^4283]: Scripture: LXX Ps. 89:14, 16.

[^4284]: Invocation of Peter sinking in the sea of Galilee (Matt. 14:30-31).

[^4285]: Scripture: LXX Ps. 89:17.

[^4286]: Martyricon sticheron: communion of the martyrs with the angelic host and their unceasing intercession for healing and salvation.

[^4287]: Concluding Theotokion of the Matins Aposticha.

[^4288]: Daily Matins conclusion rubrics: LXX Ps. 91:2 (*It is good to give praise to the Lord*), followed by the Trisagion prayers through the Lord's Prayer.

[^4289]: The Divine Liturgy cycle for Tuesday.

[^4290]: The Beatitudes (*Блаже́нна*) stichera, Tone 4.

[^4291]: The standard Tone 4 Beatitudes heirmologic model: Adam's expulsion by the tree of knowledge contrasted with the good thief's entry into Paradise by the tree of the Cross (Luke 23:42).

[^4292]: Penitential triad: the tears of Peter (Matt. 26:75), the tears of the harlot (Luke 7:38), and the sighing of the publican (Luke 18:13).

[^4293]: St. John the Baptist as the loosener of barrenness, invoked to loosen spiritual infertility.

[^4294]: Enumeration of the physical trials of the martyrs: wild beasts, sword, drowning, fire, and iron instruments.

[^4295]: Triadikon of the Beatitudes: orthodox confession of the Holy Trinity (one divine essence in three distinct, unconfused Hypostases).

[^4296]: Theotokion of the Beatitudes: the virginal conception of the co-eternal and co-enthroned Son of God.

[^4297]: Opening of Wednesday liturgical services: in Byzantine-Ruthenian liturgical theology, Wednesday is dedicated to the Precious and Life-Giving Cross and the Passion of Christ, beginning with Tuesday evening Vespers.

[^4298]: Tuesday Evening Vespers rubric (*Въ Вто́рникъ ве́чера*).

[^4299]: Melodic model: *Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ)*, corresponding to Byzantine Greek: Ὡς γενναῖον ἐν Μάρτυσιν.

[^4300]: Colossians 2:14: Christ signing the charter of human liberation with His own blood and cancelling the bond of debt that stood against us.

[^4301]: Enumeration of the instruments of the Passion (*arma Christi*): Cross, spear, reed, sponge, nails, scourgings, purple robe, crown of thorns, spittings, and mockings.

[^4302]: Veneration and kissing of the Precious Cross (*Крестꙋ̀ твое́мꙋ честно́мꙋ покланѧ́юсѧ*).

[^4303]: Stavrotheotokia stichera to the Mother of God at the Cross, Tone 4, following the same automelon model.

[^4304]: Stavrotheotokion: the Mother of God as the Ewe-lamb (*А҆́гница*) lamenting at the foot of the Cross over the ungrateful Jewish assembly.

[^4305]: The Virgin's maternal lamentation over Christ the Lamb and Shepherd (John 1:29, 10:11) nailed upon the tree.

[^4306]: The Mother of God entreating the Lord not to leave her orphaned and alone in the world, but to hasten His Resurrection.

[^4307]: Stavrotheotokion at *Glory... Both now...*, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (*Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ*).

[^4308]: The maternal grief and contemplation of the voluntary Passion of Christ (*твое́мꙋ во́льномꙋ распѧ́тїю*).

[^4309]: Tuesday Vespers Aposticha stichera of the Precious Cross.

[^4310]: The Cross as an invincible weapon against demonic assaults (*Ѡ҆рꙋ́жїе непобѣди́мое*).

[^4311]: Scripture: LXX Ps. 122:1-2 (*Πρὸς σὲ ἦρα τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς μου*).

[^4312]: Trampling underfoot the snares of the adversary through the power of the Cross.

[^4313]: Scripture: LXX Ps. 122:3-4 (*Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς*).

[^4314]: Martyricon sticheron: the boldness of the holy martyrs interceding for the remission of sins.

[^4315]: Melodic model: *Tone 4, Podoben: "Being called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше)*, corresponding to Greek: Ὁ ἐξ ὑψίστου κληθείς.

[^4316]: Stavrotheotokion: Christ consoling His Mother from the Cross, promising His impending Resurrection and the harrowing of Hades (theological antitype of Ode 9 of Holy Saturday Matins: *Не рыда́й менѐ Ма́ти*).

[^4317]: Tuesday Compline office. Codicological note: 1895 Lviv Stauropegion print contains the typesetter typographical error *Въ Вто́рникъ на ПОКЕЧЕ́РЇИ* (sic, with 'К' for 'В').

[^4318]: Ode 1 Heirmos of Tuesday Compline Canon, Tone 4 (*Ѡ҆тве́рзꙋ оу҆ста̀ моѧ̑*, Greek: Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου). One of the most famous heirmoi in the Byzantine rite, also sung at the Akathist Hymn.

[^4319]: Canon refrain: *Прест҃а́ѧ Гпⷭ҇же Бцⷣе, спасѝ на́съ* ("Most-holy Lady Theotokos, save us").

[^4320]: Incipit of Troparion 1 of Ode 1 of Compline Canon (*Неизмѣ́рнꙋю Бж҃їю мꙋ́дрость и҆ си́лꙋ ро́ждши Пренепоро́чнаѧ*), concluding physical leaf p440 and continuing onto physical leaf p441 in Cohort 45.

[^4321]: Compline Canon to the Most-holy Theotokos, Tone 4, Ode 1 Troparion 1 conclusion (continued from physical leaf p440 in Cohort 44): Christ as the power and dominion of strength born without seed of the Virgin.

[^4322]: Ode 1 Troparion 2: the Virgin's childbearing beyond understanding, enriching earthborn mankind with incorruption as the Mediatress of renewal (*хода́таицꙋ ѡ҆бновле́нїѧ*).

[^4323]: Ode 1, Glory: petition for healing of soul and body through the overshadowing of the Mother of God, the protectress of those in sorrow.

[^4324]: Ode 1, Both now: prayer for the hand of salvation to be stretched out amid the tempest of tribulations, delivering the soul from the deep of evils.

[^4325]: Ode 3 Heirmos (*Твоѧ̑ пѣсносло́вцы Бцⷣе*, Greek: Τοὺς σοὺς ὑμνολόγους, Θεοτόκε). Classical Byzantine heirmos of the Theotokos attributed to St. John of Damascus, praying for crowns of glory.

[^4326]: Ode 3 Troparion 1: the Mother of God as a fountain of tender-heartedness sprinkling streams of healing upon the sick.

[^4327]: Ode 3 Troparion 2: the Virgin as a fair bridal-chamber (*красе́нъ черто́гъ*) and bridal room beyond nature for the divine Word.

[^4328]: Ode 3, Glory: confession of soul-crushing despondency and prayer unto the Lady who bore Life to grant consolation.

[^4329]: Ode 3, Both now: supplication for mercy and cleansing before the hour of death, delivered from crafty demons.

[^4330]: Ode 4 Heirmos (*Неизслѣ́дный Бж҃їй совѣ́тъ*, Greek: Τὴν ἀνεξιχνίαστον θείαν βουλήν). Typological ode based on the Canticle of Habakkuk (Hab. 3:2), beholding the unsearchable mystery of the Incarnation.

[^4331]: Ode 4 Troparion 1: the King of all choosing the Virgin from the royal root and loins of David, exalting her above the Cherubim and Seraphim.

[^4332]: Ode 4 Troparion 2 conclusion (continued from physical leaf p441): the Creator becoming incarnate and showing forth the Virgin as the unerring protectress of Christians.

[^4333]: Ode 4, Glory: the Virgin invoked as protection, defense, and refuge against immeasurable evils.

[^4334]: Ode 4, Both now: prayer for tears, groaning, and deliverance from impassioned thoughts unto divine compunction.

[^4335]: Ode 5 Heirmos (*Оу҆жасо́шасѧ всѧ́ческаѧ*, Greek: Ἐξέστη τὰ σύμπанта). The cosmic wonder of the unwedded Virgin carrying the God over all in her womb.

[^4336]: Ode 5 Troparion 1: the Virgin as an animate cloud (*ѡ҆́блакъ ѡ҆дꙋшевле́нъ*) of Christ the King, showering the dew of healing upon the sick.

[^4337]: Ode 5 Troparion 2: prayer to the Master for release from sorrows and forgiveness of transgressions, leading unto incorruptible joy.

[^4338]: Ode 5, Glory: the Theotokos as the hope and boast of salvation, anticipating and delivering the soul swallowed by sins.

[^4339]: Ode 5, Both now: Stavrotheotokion; Christ as the ripe cluster of grapes (*Гро́здъ зрѣ́лый*, cf. Num. 13:23) hung upon the Tree, and the Sun of glory darkening creation in His Passion.

[^4340]: Ode 6 Heirmos (*Прїидо́хъ въ глꙋбины̀ морскї́ѧ*, Greek: Ἦλθον εἰς τὰ βάθη τῆς θαλάσσης). Jonas-canticle typifying deliverance from the abyss of sins (LXX Ps. 68:3, Jon. 2:3-6).

[^4341]: Ode 6 Troparion 1: Christ taking the form of a servant (Phil. 2:7) and showing forth the Theotokos higher than the Cherubim and dread Seraphim.

[^4342]: Ode 6 Troparion 2: the Virgin bearing divine Life and cutting down the insurrection of passions.

[^4343]: Ode 6, Glory: petition for deliverance from perils and transgressions through the Mediatress who bore the Redemption of all.

[^4344]: Ode 6, Both now: the faithful boasting in the Virgin and remaining unafraid of barbarian invasions.

[^4345]: Rubric: Trisagion prayers, Lord have mercy thrice, Glory... Both now... and concluding sessional hymn.

[^4346]: Sessional Hymn at Compline, Tone 4 (*Дѣ́во пренепоро́чнаѧ, Ма́ти Хрⷭ҇та̀ Бг҃а*): Simeon's prophecy fulfilled at the voluntary Crucifixion (Lk. 2:35).

[^4347]: Ode 7 Heirmos (*Не послꙋжи́ша тва́ри бг҃омꙋ́дрїи*, Greek: Οὐκ ἐλάτρευσαν τῇ κτίσει οἱ θεόφρονες). Canticle of the Three Holy Youths in the Babylonian furnace (Dan. 3:28).

[^4348]: Ode 7 Troparion 1: soul strength dried up like a potsherd (LXX Ps. 21:16) and drawing near to the destructive bonds of Hades.

[^4349]: Ode 7 Troparion 2: heart rent by manifold evils and sicknesses, delivered by the Mother of Life.

[^4350]: Ode 7, Glory: opening the celestial gates of the kingdom of Christ the all-merciful King.

[^4351]: Ode 7, Both now: the aggravated wounds of sin leading to spiritual and bodily death, averted by the Lady's might.

[^4352]: Ode 8 Heirmos (*Ѻ҆́троки благочести̑выѧ въ пещѝ*, Greek: Παῖδας εὐαγεῖς ἐν τῇ καμίνῳ). The furnace prefiguring the virgin birth that preserves without burning (Dan. 3:57).

[^4353]: Ode 8 Troparion 1 conclusion (continued from physical leaf p443): the furnace of thorn-bearing passions quenched and transgressions forgiven.

[^4354]: Ode 8 Troparion 2: the Virgin as the lampstand (*Свѣ́щникъ*) of the thrice-radiant Light dispelling the darkness of sins.

[^4355]: Ode 8, Glory: the transcendent God wholly dwelling in the womb of the Ever-virgin for universal salvation.

[^4356]: Ode 8, Both now: eschatological defense at the hour of death against demonic examination, toll-houses (*мыта́рства*), and the cruel prince.

[^4357]: Ode 9 Heirmos (*Всѧ́къ земноро́дный да взыгра́етсѧ*, Greek: Ἅπας γηγενής). Celebrated Megalynarion heirmos of the Theotokos inviting earthly mortals and angelic powers to keep festival.

[^4358]: Ode 9 Troparion 1: humanity exalted to divine sonship and adoption through the Incarnation of the Word.

[^4359]: Ode 9 Troparion 2: soul bound by the wounds of sin finding refuge in the protection of the Sovereign Lady.

[^4360]: Ode 9, Glory: poetic offering woven in compunction from a suffering soul to the Mother of God.

[^4361]: Ode 9, Both now: spiritual enlightenment of the inner eyes against the dense darkness of sin and the pit of despair.

[^4362]: Rubric: concluding dismissal rite of Compline (It is truly meet, prostration, Trisagion, and dismissal).

[^4363]: Wednesday Matins office of Tone 4. Rubric for Sessional Hymns of the Precious Cross following the first stichology of the Kathisma.

[^4364]: First Sessional Hymn of the Cross, Tone 4 (*И҆скꙋпи́лъ ны̀ є҆сѝ ѿ кла́твы зако́нныѧ*): Christ redeeming mankind from the curse of the law by His Blood (Gal. 3:13).

[^4365]: Scripture: LXX Ps. 98:5 (*Ὑψοῦτε Κύριον τὸν Θεὸν ἡμῶν*).

[^4366]: Second Sessional Hymn of the Cross: Christ crucified by the Jews to call the Gentiles into the kingdom.

[^4367]: Stavrotheotokion (*Безневѣ́стнаѧ Ма́ти твоѧ̀ Хрⷭ҇тѐ*): maternal lamentation of the Mother of God beholding her Son nailed to the Tree.

[^4368]: Sessional Hymns following the second stichology of the Kathisma at Wednesday Matins.

[^4369]: Sessional Hymn (*Ско́рѡ предварѝ*): petition for swift divine help against threatening foes, manifesting the power of the Orthodox faith.

[^4370]: Scripture: LXX Ps. 73:12 (*Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς βασιлеὺς ἡμῶν πρὸ αἰώνων*).

[^4371]: Sessional Hymn of the Cross: healing the primordial wound of Adam through Christ's voluntary Crucifixion on Golgotha.

[^4372]: Scripture: LXX Ps. 67:36 (*Θαυμαστὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις αὐτοῦ*).

[^4373]: Martyricon sessional hymn conclusion (continued from physical leaf p445): holy passion-bearers sanctifying the faithful through their endurance and intercession.

[^4374]: Stavrotheotokion: the immaculate Ewe-lamb wounded with sorrow at the Crucifixion of the Lord of life.

[^4375]: Sessional Hymns following the third stichology of the Kathisma at Wednesday Matins.

[^4376]: Sessional Hymn of the Cross: Christ raising fallen man upon Golgotha and destroying the deceitful serpent through the Tree.

[^4377]: Sessional Hymn of the Cross: cosmic upheavals, eclipse of the sun, and the resurrection of the dead at the Lord's Crucifixion (Mt. 27:45, 52).

[^4378]: Stavrotheotokion: Simeon's prophecy fulfilled at Golgotha (Lk. 2:35).

[^4379]: Matins Canon to the Cross and the Martyrs, acrostic: *The Cross is a weapon unto salvation* (Greek: Σταυρός ἐστιν ὅπλον εἰς σωτηρίαν), composed by St. Joseph the Hymnographer.

[^4380]: Ode 1 Heirmos (*Мѡ́рѧ чермнꙋ́ю пꙋчи́нꙋ*, Greek: Θαλάσσης τὸ ἐρυθραῖον πέλαγος). Crossing the Red Sea and Moses' cruciform hands defeating Amalek (Ex. 14:21-29, 17:11-12).

[^4381]: Refrain to the Precious Cross: *Сла́ва Гдⷭ҇и крестꙋ̀ твое́мꙋ и҆ распѧ́тїю* ("Glory, O Lord, to Thy Cross and crucifixion").

[^4382]: Ode 1 Troparion 1: Christ spreading out His hands upon the Cross to embrace all nations.

[^4383]: Ode 1 Troparion 2: the Cross protecting the believer against the spiritual wolf that seeks the soul's destruction.

[^4384]: Ode 1 Martyricon 1 conclusion (continued from physical leaf p446): the holy martyrs inheriting a life free of pain and relieving our sicknesses.

[^4385]: Ode 1 Martyricon 2: the martyrs binding the deceiver through their voluntary bonds in Christ.

[^4386]: Ode 1 Theotokion: perpetual virginity preserved in giving birth to God Who was lifted up upon the Cross.

[^4387]: Second Canon of Wednesday Matins, to the Most-holy Theotokos, acrostic: *Unto the Virgin Theotokos I offer supplication* (Greek: Θεοτόκῳ Παρθένῳ δέησιν προσάγω).

[^4388]: Ode 1 Troparion 1 (sung twice): cleansing the defiled heart through the pure prayer of the Theotokos.

[^4389]: Ode 1 Troparion 2: deliverance from future weeping and lamentation at the dread judgment of God.

[^4390]: Ode 1 Troparion 3: freedom from the primordial curse and carnal slavery through the Virgin's intercession.

[^4391]: Ode 3 Heirmos (*Весели́тсѧ ѡ҆ тебѣ̀ це́рковь твоѧ̀ Хрⷭ҇тѐ*, Greek: Εὐφραίνεται ἐπὶ σοὶ ἡ Ἐκκλησία σου, Χριστέ). Based on the Canticle of Hannah (1 Sam. 2:1-2).

[^4392]: Ode 3 Troparion 1: Christ lifting up fallen nature from corruption and casting down the prince of darkness.

[^4393]: Ode 3 Troparion 2: the enemy's swords blunted and Eden reopened by the spear that pierced the side of the hypostatic Word.

[^4394]: Ode 3 Martyricon 1: rivers of demonic delusion dried up and the fire of polytheism quenched by the martyrs.

[^4395]: Ode 3 Martyricon 2: martyrs enduring crucifixion and iron claws to slay the ancient serpent with the sword of patience.

[^4396]: Ode 3 Theotokion: the immaculate Ewe-lamb lamenting at the foot of the Cross while glorifying the Master's might.

[^4397]: Ode 3 Heirmos of Second Canon (*Не мꙋ́дростїю, и҆ си́лою*, Greek: Οὐκ ἐν σοφίᾳ, καὶ δυνάμει). Boasting only in the hypostatic Wisdom of God (Jer. 9:23, 1 Sam. 2:2).

[^4398]: Ode 3 Troparion 1 (sung twice): prayer to elevate the serpent-struck mind above the desires of the flesh.

[^4399]: Ode 3 Troparion 2: seeking the advocacy of the All-immaculate Virgin at the dread trial of the Lord.

[^4400]: Ode 3 Troparion 3: transforming an unmerciful heart into compassion through the intercession of the Mother of God.

[^4401]: Ode 4 Heirmos (*Вознесе́на тѧ̀ ви́дѣвши це́рковь*, Greek: Ἐπαρθέντα σε ἰδοῦσα ἡ Ἐκκλησία). The Church standing in awe before the Sun of righteousness lifted up upon the Tree (Hab. 3:11).

[^4402]: Ode 4 Troparion 1: cosmic mourning at the voluntary Crucifixion: the sun darkened, rocks rent, and temple veil torn (Mt. 27:45, 51).

[^4403]: Ode 4 Troparion 2: the turning flaming sword (Gen. 3:24) giving way before the repentant thief at Christ's command (Lk. 23:43).

[^4404]: Ode 4 Martyricon 1: passion-bearers shielded by the Cross against the shafts of malice, casting down idolatry.

[^4405]: Ode 4 Martyricon 2: the martyrs offering themselves as pure whole-burnt offerings to Christ (Rom. 12:1).

[^4406]: Ode 4 Theotokion: the Virgin's soul pierced with anguish as she beholds her Son upon the Tree.

[^4407]: Ode 4 Troparion 1 of Second Canon (sung twice): sanctification in the divine temple of the Word Who emptied Himself (Phil. 2:7).

[^4408]: Ode 4 Troparion 2 conclusion (continued from physical leaf p448): prayer to anchor the mind tossed about by sloth and malice.

[^4409]: Ode 4 Troparion 3: transforming the den of robbers into a living palace of the Holy Trinity (Mt. 21:13, 1 Cor. 6:19).

[^4410]: Ode 5 Heirmos (*Ты̀ Гдⷭ҇и мо́й свѣ́тъ*, Greek: Σὺ Κύριέ μου φῶς). Christ as the true Light coming into the world to dispel ignorance (Jn. 8:12).

[^4411]: Ode 5 Troparion 1: streams of incorruption from Christ's pierced side healing the fall occasioned by the first-created rib (Gen. 2:21-22).

[^4412]: Ode 5 Troparion 2: the precious Cross as an invincible standard of victory over demonic powers.

[^4413]: Ode 5 Martyricon 1: martyrs passing through material flames to join the choir of angelic fiery ministers.

[^4414]: Ode 5 Martyricon 2: unbroken love of the martyrs toward the Creator despite the crushing of the flesh.

[^4415]: Ode 5 Theotokion: the Good One incarnate of the Virgin and crucified to deliver mankind from corruption.

[^4416]: Ode 5 Heirmos of Second Canon (*Нечести́вїи не ᲂу҆́зрѧтъ сла́вы твоеѧ̀*, Greek: Οἱ ἀσεβεῖς οὐκ ὄψονται). Rising early from the night to hymn the radiance of the Father's glory (Is. 26:9-10).

[^4417]: Ode 5 Troparion 1: the spiritual Ewe-lamb seeking out the lost sheep wandering upon the mountains of sin (Mt. 18:12, Lk. 15:4).

[^4418]: Ode 5 Troparion 2: warming a soul frozen in spiritual winter through the flame of divine charity.

[^4419]: Ode 5 Troparion 3: prayer to the pure among women to grant a life free from passionate blemishes.

[^4420]: Ode 5 Troparion 4: preservation under the shelter of the Virgin's wings as the apple of an eye (LXX Ps. 16:8).

[^4421]: Ode 6 Heirmos (*Пожрꙋ́ ти съ гла́сомъ хвале́нїа*, Greek: Θύσω σοι, μετὰ φωνῆς αἰνέσεως). Jonas-canticle typifying the cleansing of the Church by the Blood of Christ (Jon. 2:10).

[^4422]: Ode 6 Troparion 1: Christ enduring dishonor on the Cross to restore humanity to celestial glory.

[^4423]: Ode 6 Troparion 2: the death of Christ upon the Tree putting to death the demonic destroyer of souls.

[^4424]: Ode 6 Martyricon 1: the tormentor trampled underfoot and held in derision by the holy martyrs.

[^4425]: Ode 6 Martyricon 2: the dust of martyrs' relics casting out demons and healing diverse sicknesses.

[^4426]: Ode 6 Theotokion: the Virgin's maternal lamentation at the nails and spear of the Crucifixion.

[^4427]: Ode 6 Troparion 1 of Second Canon: the childbearing of the Theotokos destroying death and raising the slain soul.

[^4428]: Ode 6 Troparion 2: stretching forth a hand of help to the soul tossed upon the stormy sea of life.

[^4429]: Ode 6 Troparion 3: the Theotokos as the fertile field bearing the divine ear of grain (*кла́съ*, cf. Jn. 12:24) to feed hungry souls.

[^4430]: Ode 6 Troparion 4: subduing rebellious carnal passions like a wild colt through the peaceful sleep of prayer.

[^4431]: Ode 7 Heirmos (*Въ пещѝ А҆враа́мстїи ѻ҆́троцы*, Greek: Ἐν τῇ καμίνῳ Ἀβραμιαῖοι παῖδες). The Hebrew youths in the Persian furnace singing praise to the Lord of glory (Dan. 3:26-56).

[^4432]: Ode 7 Troparion 1 incipit (*Распа́лсѧ є҆сѝ хотѧ́й на дре́вѣ на́гъ*), concluding physical leaf p450 and continuing onto physical leaf p451 in Cohort 46.

[^4433]: Matins Canon of the Precious Cross, Tone 4, Ode 7 Troparion 1 conclusion (continued from physical leaf p450 in Cohort 45): Christ Who clothes the heaven with clouds (Ps. 146:8 [LXX Ps. 146:8]) stripping the enemy and clothing him in eternal shame.

[^4434]: Ode 7 Troparion 2: the voluntary elevation upon the Cross, the piercing of Christ's side with a lance (Jn. 19:34), and the mortal overthrow of the devil.

[^4435]: Ode 7 Martyricon 1: the martyrs joined unto the transcendent beauty of the divine Word, despising the worldly realm amid bodily torment.

[^4436]: Ode 7 Martyricon 2: overthrowing the strongholds of pagan delusion and becoming unshakeable walls of protection for the faithful.

[^4437]: Ode 7 Theotokion (Stavrotheotokion): the Virgin contemplating her crucified Son, Who preserved the three Hebrew youths in the fiery furnace (Dan. 3:50).

[^4438]: Second Canon to the Most-holy Theotokos, Ode 7 Troparion 1: typological prophecy of Daniel's unhewn stone from the mountain (Dan. 2:34-35, 45) shattering idol pillars and melting the petrified heart.

[^4439]: Ode 7 Troparion 2: the Virgin unshakeable in bearing the Almighty, Who looks upon the earth and causes it to tremble (Ps. 103:32 [LXX Ps. 103:32]).

[^4440]: Ode 7 Troparion 3: prayer to cast down fleshly mindsets (*плотска̑ѧ мꙋдрова́нїѧ*, cf. Rom. 8:6-7) and adorn the soul with spiritual virtues.

[^4441]: Ode 7 Troparion 4: the Mother of God addressed as the divine vessel of compassions (*Бж҃твенный ѻ҆кри́не милосе́рдїа*), cleansing the filth of sins and quenching carnal fever.

[^4442]: Ode 8 Heirmos (*Рꙋ́цѣ распросте́ръ Данїи́лъ*, Greek: Χεῖρας ἐκπετάσας Δανιήλ). Dual typological motif of Daniel in the lions' den (Dan. 6:22) and the Three Children in the fiery furnace (Dan. 3:57).

[^4443]: Ode 8 Troparion 1: Christ stretching out His hands on the Cross to heal the primordial reach of Adam toward the forbidden tree (Gen. 3:6).

[^4444]: Ode 8 Troparion 2: tearing the bond of debt / handwriting of Adam (*рꙋкописа́нїе*, Col. 2:14) through the piercing of the Lord's ribs, sanctifying the earth with His blood.

[^4445]: Ode 8 Martyricon 1: the martyrs enduring flames unharmed in mystical emulation of the Three Holy Children.

[^4446]: Ode 8 Martyricon 2: victorious endurance of transient torments, hastening unto the unwaning Light (*къ свѣ́тꙋ незаходи́момꙋ*).

[^4447]: Ode 8 Theotokion (Stavrotheotokion): the Mother of God weeping at the Crucifixion while marveling at the overthrow of the enemy.

[^4448]: Second Canon to the Most-holy Theotokos, Ode 8 Troparion 1: the Virgin bearing the ripe Fruit (*Зрѣ́лъ пло́дъ*), Christ, through Whom death itself was slain.

[^4449]: Ode 8 Troparion 2: petition to quiet the sleepless stirrings of carnal passions and awaken the soul from spiritual sluggishness.

[^4450]: Ode 8 Troparion 3: breaking the cords of sin (Prov. 5:22) and cutting off insidious mental assaults.

[^4451]: Ode 8 Troparion 4: moral compunction confronting the demonic accusers at the future judgment and seeking the Mother of God's intercession.

[^4452]: Ode 9 Heirmos (*Ка́мень нерꙋкосѣ́чный*, Greek: Λίθος ἀχειρότμητος). The classic prophecy of Daniel (Dan. 2:34, 45) applied to Christ the cornerstone (Eph. 2:14, 20) uniting the divided divine and human natures.

[^4453]: Matins Canon of the Precious Cross, Tone 4, Ode 9 Troparion 1 conclusion (continued from physical leaf p452): cosmic reaction to Christ's Crucifixion (Mt. 27:45, 51)—the eclipse of the sun and trembling of the earth establishing minds in piety.

[^4454]: Ode 9 Troparion 2: contrast between the divine Lawgiver and the iniquitous sanhedrin condemning the Source of life to death on the Tree.

[^4455]: Ode 9 Martyricon 1: bold confession of the Incarnation before persecutors and receiving the crowns of victory (2 Tim. 4:8).

[^4456]: Ode 9 Martyricon 2: holy martyrs shining like luminous stars across creation, dispelling demonic darkness and bestowing healings.

[^4457]: Ode 9 Theotokion (Stavrotheotokion): invoking the Mother of God as the Cloud of Light (*Свѣ́та ѻ҆́блаче*) to dispel sinful gloom.

[^4458]: Second Canon to the Most-holy Theotokos, Ode 9 Troparion 1: severing the bonds of sin with the divine lance of the Crucified and binding the soul in divine charity.

[^4459]: Ode 9 Troparion 2: the Virgin *Platytera ton ouranon* (*Ꙗ҆́же небе́съ ши́ршаѧ*, wider than heaven) leading the constricted heart into the freedom of dispassion along the narrow way (Mt. 7:14).

[^4460]: Ode 9 Troparion 3: prayer to be freed from sinful irrationality (*всѧ́кагѡ безслове́сїа грѣхо́внагѡ*) and made partaker of celestial glory.

[^4461]: Ode 9 Troparion 4: confounding the conspiracies of visible and invisible adversaries through the intercession of the Theotokos.

[^4462]: Rubric concluding the Matins canons: Megalynarion hymn *It is truly meet* (*Досто́йно є҆́сть*), prostration, litany of supplication, Exapostilarion/Photagogicon, and the customary Matins psalms (Lauds / Praises, LXX Pss. 148-150).

[^4463]: Aposticha of Wednesday Matins, Tone 4. Idiomel/Automel stichera of the Precious Cross (*На Стїхо́внѣ, стїхи̑ры кре́стны, Гла́съ д҃. самогла́сны*).

[^4464]: Aposticha Sticheron 1 conclusion (continued from physical leaf p453): the Cross of Christ as an unshakeable wall and the sole hope of the faithful.

[^4465]: Scripture: LXX Ps. 89:14, 16 (*Ἐνεπλήσθημεν τὸ πρωῒ τοῦ ἐλέους σου, Κύριε*).

[^4466]: Aposticha Sticheron 2: the Cross given as a sign / banner (*зна́менїе*, LXX Ps. 59:6), disarming demonic principalities and powers (Col. 2:15).

[^4467]: Scripture: LXX Ps. 89:17 (*Καὶ ἔστω ἡ λαμπρότης Κυρίου τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν ἐφ' ἡμᾶς*).

[^4468]: Aposticha Martyricon, Tone 4: praise of the holy passion-bearers conquering incorporeal demonic foes while clothed in mortal flesh.

[^4469]: Canonical 3-layer melodic model: Tone 4 prosomoion modeled upon *As one valiant among martyrs* (Greek: Ὡς γενναῖον ἐν μάρτυσιν, Slavonic: *Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ въ мꙋ́ченицѣхъ*).

[^4470]: Stavrotheotokion at the Aposticha: maternal lament of the Virgin beholding her Son crucified, beseeching Him as her divine consolation not to delay.

[^4471]: Rubric: concluding order of Matins (*Бла́го є҆́сть и҆сповѣ́датисѧ*, LXX Ps. 91:2), Trisagion, Lord's Prayer, Dismissal Troparion, Litany of Fervent Supplication, and First Hour.

[^4472]: Rubric for the Beatitudes (Typika) at the Divine Liturgy for Wednesday, Tone 4.

[^4473]: Beatitudes Troparion 1, Tone 4: antitypical contrast between Adam's expulsion from Eden through the tree of knowledge (Gen. 3) and the good thief entering Eden through the tree of the Cross (Lk. 23:42-43).

[^4474]: Beatitudes Troparion 2: the side of Christ pierced with a lance pouring forth two streams of water and blood (Jn. 19:34) amid cosmic convulsions.

[^4475]: Beatitudes Troparion 3 conclusion (continued from physical leaf p454): Christ stretching out His hands willingly on the Cross to rectify the transgression of Adam's hands.

[^4476]: Beatitudes Troparion 4 (Martyricon): the holy martyrs sanctifying the earth through their athletic contests and achieving theosis by grace.

[^4477]: Beatitudes, Glory: Trinitarian doxology combining the angelic Trisagion with the prayer of the penitent thief.

[^4478]: Beatitudes, Both now (Stavrotheotokion): the Virgin lamenting the loss of Christ's radiant beauty upon the Cross and mourning the ungrateful return of the Hebrew assembly.

[^4479]: Opening of the Thursday liturgical cycle in Tone 4, dedicated to the Twelve Holy Apostles and Saint Nicholas the Wonderworker, Archbishop of Myra in Lycia. Physical leaf p455 corresponds to printed folio 453.

[^4480]: Canonical 3-layer melodic model: Tone 4 prosomoion modeled upon *As one valiant among martyrs* (Greek: Ὡς γενναῖον ἐν μάρτυσιν, Slavonic: *Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ въ мꙋ́ченицѣхъ*).

[^4481]: Vespers Sticheron 1 to the Holy Apostles, Tone 4: the Apostles taking up the whole armor of God (Eph. 6:11-17) and plundering human souls from demonic dominion.

[^4482]: Vespers Sticheron 2 to the Holy Apostles: the twelve disciples casting the net of the Cross into the world (Mt. 4:19) and drawing the nations out of the bitter sea of idolatry.

[^4483]: Vespers Sticheron 3 to the Holy Apostles conclusion (continued from physical leaf p455): catalog of the Twelve Apostles together with the Seventy disciples (Lk. 10:1).

[^4484]: Stichera to Saint Nicholas of Myra at Wednesday evening Vespers, Tone 4.

[^4485]: Sticheron 1 to Saint Nicholas: wordplay on the name of Myra (*Мѵ̑ра*) and the mystical holy chrism (*ми́ро*), perfuming the Church with virtues.

[^4486]: Sticheron 2 to Saint Nicholas: the saint as an unwaning star upon the ecclesial firmament dispelling storms and bringing spiritual serenity.

[^4487]: Sticheron 3 to Saint Nicholas: alluding to the miracle of the three innocent military commanders (*stratēlatē*) condemned to death by Emperor Constantine and rescued by Nicholas appearing in a dream.

[^4488]: Vespers Doxasticon / Theotokion: the Incarnation of the uncontainable Word assuming human nature and divinizing it.

[^4489]: Rubric: the ancient evening hymn *Phos Hilaron* (*Свѣ́те ти́хїй*), Wednesday evening Prokeimenon, and standard evening litanies.

[^4490]: Aposticha Sticheron 1 to the Apostles, Tone 4: the Holy Spirit descending upon the apostolic choir at Pentecost to illumine the world (Acts 2).

[^4491]: Scripture: LXX Ps. 122:1-2 (*Πρὸς σὲ ἦρα τοὺς ὀφθалμούς μου τὸν κατοικοῦντα ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ*).

[^4492]: Aposticha Sticheron 2: unlettered disciples made eloquent doctors and preachers through the gift of tongues (Acts 2:4).

[^4493]: Scripture: LXX Ps. 122:3-4 (*Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, ὅτι ἐπὶ πολὺ ἐπλήσθημεν ἐξουδενώσεως*).

[^4494]: Aposticha Martyricon conclusion (continued from physical leaf p456): the holy martyrs as spiritual sheep guided beside the waters of repose (LXX Ps. 22:2).

[^4495]: Aposticha Theotokion, Tone 4: petition for deliverance from afflictions and salutation of the Virgin as sole protection.

[^4496]: Rubric: concluding order of Vespers (*Ны́нѣ ѿпꙋща́еши*, Lk. 2:29), Trisagion prayers, Dismissal Troparion, litany, and dismissal.

[^4497]: Wednesday Small Compline office of Tone 4. Acrostic and thematic Canon to the Most-holy Theotokos.

[^4498]: Compline Ode 1 Heirmos (*Мо́рѧ чермнꙋ́ю пꙋчи́нꙋ*, Greek: Θαλάσσης τὸ ἐρυθραῖον πέλαγος). Crossing the Red Sea and Moses' cruciform hands defeating Amalek (Ex. 14:21-29, 17:11-12).

[^4499]: Compline Ode 1 Troparion 1: dogmatic confession of the Virgin as truly and in truth (*Вои́стинꙋ и҆ въ рѣ́снотꙋ*) the Mother of God, following the definition of the Third Ecumenical Council (Ephesus, 431).

[^4500]: Compline Ode 1 Troparion 2: the messianic Star of Jacob (Num. 24:17) Who numbers the multitude of the stars (Ps. 146:4 [LXX Ps. 146:4]), driving away sinful gloom.

[^4501]: Compline Ode 1, Glory: the Virgin as the intelligible / noetic bridal chamber (*Невѣ́стникъ слове́сенъ*) of the divine Incarnation.

[^4502]: Compline Ode 1, Both now: Jacob's ladder (Gen. 28:12) typifying the Virgin as the bridge uniting earth to heaven.

[^4503]: Compline Ode 3 Heirmos (*Не мꙋ́дростїю и҆ си́лою*, Greek: Οὐκ ἐν σοφίᾳ, καὶ δυνάμει). Canticle based on 1 Kings 2:2 [LXX 1 Sam. 2:2] and Jer. 9:23-24, boasting only in Christ the hypostatic Wisdom of God (1 Cor. 1:24).

[^4504]: Compline Ode 3 Troparion 1: the Mother of God as a flowing fountain of consolation quenching the furnace of bodily passions.

[^4505]: Compline Ode 3 Troparion 2: supplication for healing of spiritual wounds inflicted by impure thoughts.

[^4506]: Compline Ode 3, Glory: the Theotokos as the tranquil haven guiding the soul tossed upon the sea of sins.

[^4507]: Compline Ode 3, Both now: typological motif of Gideon's fleece (Jdg. 6:37-40, LXX Ps. 71:6) bedewing the heart inflamed with passions.

[^4508]: Compline Ode 4 Heirmos (*Вознесе́на тѧ̀ ви́дѣвши це́рковь*, Greek: Ἐπαρθέντα σε ἰδοῦσα ἡ Ἐκκλησία). Habakkuk canticle (Hab. 3:11 [LXX Hab. 3:11]), the sun standing still in its order at the elevation of Christ upon the Cross.

[^4509]: Compline Ode 4 Troparion 1: the myrrh of Christ (Song 1:3) pouring forth dispassion upon the soul to destroy sinful corruption.

[^4510]: Compline Ode 4 Troparion 2: purification through hyssop and spiritual cleansing (LXX Ps. 50:9), making the heart a habitation for Christ.

[^4511]: Compline Ode 4, Glory: the Virgin as the sealed book written by the finger of God (Ex. 31:18, Isa. 29:11), inscribing the forgiveness of sins.

[^4512]: Compline Ode 4, Both now: the Mother of God as the sacred temple prefigured by the holy mountains (LXX Ps. 86:1-2).

[^4513]: Compline Ode 5 Heirmos (*Ты̀ Гдⷭ҇и мо́й свѣ́тъ*, Greek: Σὺ Κύριέ μου φῶς). Canticle of Isaiah (Isa. 26:9, Jn. 8:12), Christ the holy Light illuminating those held in ignorance.

[^4514]: Compline Ode 5 Troparion 1: the Mother of God typified as the dew of Hermon descending upon the mountains of Zion (LXX Ps. 132:3).

[^4515]: Compline Ode 5 Troparion 2: the Virgin as the spiritual paradise of Life preserving the faithful from the death of sin.

[^4516]: Compline Ode 5, Glory: the Virgin as the spiritual alabaster jar of precious spikenard (Mt. 26:7) containing the divine Myrrh of heaven.

[^4517]: Compline Ode 5, Both now: restoration of fallen humanity from corruption and deliverance from spiritual abysses.

[^4518]: Compline Ode 6 Heirmos (*Пожрꙋ̀ тебѣ̀ со гла́сомъ хвале́нїѧ*, Greek: Θύσω σοι, μετὰ φωνῆς αἰνέσεως). Canticle of Jonah (Jon. 2:9-10), the Church offering a sacrifice of praise cleansed by the Blood of Christ's side.

[^4519]: Compline Ode 6 Troparion 2: drying up the torrents of impure desires through the incorrupt virginity of the Mother of God.

[^4520]: Compline Ode 6, Glory: subduing the wild colt of carnal lusts under the reins of the enlightened mind.

[^4521]: Compline Ode 6, Both now: prayer for deliverance from the terrors of the Dread Judgment and eternal damnation.

[^4522]: Rubric: Trisagion prayers, Lord have mercy thrice, Glory... Both now... and mid-canon Sessional Hymn.

[^4523]: Compline Sessional Hymn, Tone 4 (*Предста́тельнице нера́тнаѧ, Богороди́тельнице*): invoking the invincible and prompt advocacy of the Virgin.

[^4524]: Compline Ode 7 Heirmos (*Въ пещѝ а҆враа́мстїи ѻ҆́троцы*, Greek: Ἐν τῇ καμίνῳ Ἀβραμιαῖοι Παῖδες). Canticle of the Three Youths (Dan. 3:28, 52-56), inflamed by love of God beyond the furnace flames.

[^4525]: Compline Ode 7 Troparion 1: the Unburnt Bush of Sinai (Ex. 3:2) consuming sinful thorns and enlightening the mind.

[^4526]: Compline Ode 7 Troparion 2: the Virgin as the second heaven (*не́бо втора́ѧ*) confounding arrogant demonic adversaries.

[^4527]: Compline Ode 7, Glory: repetitive petition appealing to the vessel of compassion (*ѻ҆кри́не милосе́рдїа*) to extinguish fleshly burning.

[^4528]: Compline Ode 7, Both now: repentance echoing the Parable of the Prodigal Son (Lk. 15:11-24) who squandered his substance in riotous living.

[^4529]: Compline Ode 8 Heirmos (*Рꙋ́цѣ распросте́ръ Данїи́лъ*, Greek: Χεῖρας ἐκπετάσας Δανιήλ). Daniel subduing the lions (Dan. 6:22) and the Three Youths extinguishing the furnace (Dan. 3:57).

[^4530]: Compline Ode 8 Troparion 1 conclusion (continued from physical leaf p459): breaking the shackles of sin and calming bodily impulses through the advocacy of the Mother of God.

[^4531]: Compline Ode 8 Troparion 2: composite Scriptural imagery of the mountain of God (LXX Ps. 67:16-17, Hab. 3:3) and deliverance from the snare of the fowler and the arrow that flies by day (LXX Ps. 90:3, 5).

[^4532]: Compline Ode 8, Glory: conceiving the fear of the Lord in the spiritual womb (Isa. 26:18) and bringing forth virtues unto angelic fellowship.

[^4533]: Compline Ode 8, Both now: opening the gates of hope and eternal life, making the faithful servant an heir of the heavenly kingdom.

[^4534]: Compline Ode 9 Heirmos (*Е҆́vа оу҆́бѡ недꙋ́гомъ преслꙋша́нїѧ*, Greek: Εὔα μὲν τῷ τῆς παρακοῆς νοσήματι). Contrast between Eve bringing the curse through disobedience (Gen. 3:16) and Mary blossoming forth universal blessing through the Incarnation.

[^4535]: Compline Ode 9 Troparion 1: petition for swift protection against the unseen assaults of demonic enemies.

[^4536]: Compline Ode 9 Troparion 2: spiritual medicine for a soul lacerated by sin, delivered by the Mother of the Word.

[^4537]: Compline Ode 9, Glory: Christ tasting death to conquer death and restore fallen Adam (Heb. 2:14-15).

[^4538]: Compline Ode 9, Both now: universal refuge in the Theotokos from the tempestuous tribulations and evil craftiness of earthly life.

[^4539]: Rubric concluding Wednesday Compline: Megalynarion *It is truly meet* (*Досто́йно є҆́сть*), prostration, Trisagion prayers, Lord's Prayer, dismissal troparia, and concluding blessing/dismissal.

[^4540]: Sessional hymn of the Holy Apostles following the First Kathisma at Thursday Matins, Tone 4.

[^4541]: Psalm 18:5 [LXX 18:4], appointed verse for the Apostles at Matins. Masoretic versification: Ps. 19:4.

[^4542]: Second Sessional hymn of the Apostles after the First Kathisma, drawing a typological contrast between Moses leading Israel through the Red Sea (Exodus 14) and the Apostles parting the sea of polytheism.

[^4543]: Theotokion concluding the sessional hymns of the First Kathisma at Thursday Matins, Tone 4.

[^4544]: First Sessional hymn of the Apostles after the Second Kathisma, Tone 4, modeled on the prosomoion *Speedily anticipate* (Ско́рѡ предварѝ / Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε).

[^4545]: Psalm 18:2 [LXX 18:1], appointed verse for the Apostles at Matins. Masoretic versification: Ps. 19:1.

[^4546]: Second Sessional hymn of the Apostles after the Second Kathisma, developing the Pauline theme of the foolishness of worldly wisdom overturned by apostolic preaching (cf. 1 Cor. 1:20-25).

[^4547]: Psalm 67:36 [LXX 67:35], standard liturgical verse accompanying the Martyricon troparion. Masoretic versification: Ps. 68:35.

[^4548]: Martyricon sessional hymn honoring the holy passion-bearers who endured physical torture for the incorruptible heavenly crown.

[^4549]: Theotokion concluding the sessional hymns of the Second Kathisma at Thursday Matins, Tone 4.

[^4550]: First Sessional hymn of the Apostles after the Third Kathisma, Tone 4, modeled on the prosomoion *Speedily anticipate* (Ско́рѡ предварѝ / Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε).

[^4551]: Sessional hymn to Saint Nicholas of Myra following the Third Kathisma at Thursday Matins, Tone 4.

[^4552]: Theotokion concluding the sessional hymns of the Third Kathisma, supplicating the intercession of the Virgin and the Holy Apostles.

[^4553]: Title and attribution of the first canon at Thursday Matins, composed by Saint Theophanes the Branded (ку́ръ Ѳеофа́на / τοῦ κυροῦ Θεοφάνους), Metropolitan of Nicaea (c. 778–845).

[^4554]: Heirmos of Ode 1, Canon of the Holy Apostles, Tone 4. The hymn recalls Moses' victory over Amalek through the cruciform extension of his hands in the wilderness of Rephidim (Exodus 17:8-16).

[^4555]: First troparion of Ode 1, Canon of the Apostles, portraying the Apostles as divine musical instruments animated by the breath of the Holy Spirit.

[^4556]: Second troparion of Ode 1, Canon of the Apostles, an individual penitential supplication seeking the apostolic visitation to cure spiritual indolence.

[^4557]: Third troparion of Ode 1, Canon of the Apostles, contrasting the irrationality (безслове́сіе / ἀλογία) of gentile delusion with the divine reason of the incarnate Word.

[^4558]: Theotokion of Ode 1, Canon of the Apostles, confessing Mary's perpetual virginity before, during, and after childbirth (*aeiparthenia*).

[^4559]: Title and acrostic rubric for the second canon of Thursday Matins, dedicated to Saint Nicholas of Myra and composed by Saint Joseph the Hymnographer (c. 816–886). The acrostic in Slavonic is: *Четве́ртое сїѐ на Нїкола́а плеска́ніе* (representing the Greek: Τέταρτον τόδε Νικολάου κρότημα. Ἰωσήφ), meaning "This fourth clapping of hands [hymn of praise] unto Nicholas."

[^4560]: Heirmos of Ode 1, Canon to Saint Nicholas, Tone 4 (Τριστάτας κραταιούς / Трїста́ты крѣ̑пкіѧ). The hymn splits across leaves p462 and p463.

[^4561]: Conclusion of the Heirmos of Ode 1, Canon to Saint Nicholas, from leaf p462. The Patristic imagery refers to the tripartite structure of the human soul (rational, irascible, and concupiscent — τὸ τριμερές / трича́стное) drowned in the sea of passionlessness, echoing the drowning of Pharaoh's captains (Exodus 15:4).

[^4562]: First troparion of Ode 1, Canon to Saint Nicholas, petitioning the saint to banish sorrow through spiritual joy.

[^4563]: Second troparion of Ode 1, Canon to Saint Nicholas, utilizing the Gospel metaphor of the lamp placed upon a candlestick (Matthew 5:15).

[^4564]: Third troparion of Ode 1, Canon to Saint Nicholas, invoking the hierarch as a celestial helmsman guiding the soul across the stormy sea of worldly existence.

[^4565]: Theotokion of Ode 1, Canon to Saint Nicholas, praying for spiritual wakefulness against demonic slumber.

[^4566]: Heirmos of Ode 3, Canon of the Holy Apostles, Tone 4 (Εὐφραίνεται ἐπὶ σοί / Весели́тсѧ ѡ҆ тебѣ̀), based on 1 Kingdoms [1 Samuel] 2:2.

[^4567]: First troparion of Ode 3, Canon of the Apostles, citing Psalm 45:5 [LXX 45:4] ("The streams of the river make glad the city of God").

[^4568]: Second troparion of Ode 3, Canon of the Apostles, invoking the Apostles as celestial citizens and fellow-liturgists with the angelic ranks.

[^4569]: Third troparion of Ode 3, Canon of the Apostles, praying for spiritual stability upon the rock of God's commandments.

[^4570]: Theotokion of Ode 3, Canon of the Apostles.

[^4571]: Heirmos of Ode 3, Canon to Saint Nicholas, Tone 4 (Οὐκ ἐν σοφίᾳ / Не мꙋ́дростію), based on Jeremiah 9:23-24.

[^4572]: First troparion of Ode 3, Canon to Saint Nicholas, hailing Nicholas as a spiritual weapon against adversary powers.

[^4573]: Second troparion of Ode 3, Canon to Saint Nicholas, splitting across physical leaves p463 and p464.

[^4574]: Conclusion of the second troparion of Ode 3, Canon to Saint Nicholas, from leaf p463.

[^4575]: Third troparion of Ode 3, Canon to Saint Nicholas, commemorating Saint Nicholas' historical overthrow of pagan temples in Lycia, specifically the famous temple of Artemis (Diana) at Myra.

[^4576]: Theotokion of Ode 3, Canon to Saint Nicholas.

[^4577]: Heirmos of Ode 4, Canon of the Holy Apostles, Tone 4 (Ἐπαρθέντα σε ἰδοῦσα / Вознесе́на тѧ̀ ви́дѣвши), based on the Canticle of Habakkuk (Hab. 3:11).

[^4578]: First troparion of Ode 4, Canon of the Apostles, based on Habakkuk 3:15 ("Thou didst drive Thy horses through the sea").

[^4579]: Second troparion of Ode 4, Canon of the Apostles, depicting the Apostles as celestial luminaries in the Church's firmament.

[^4580]: Third troparion of Ode 4, Canon of the Apostles, invoking the Apostles as divine arrows quenching the fiery darts of the wicked one (cf. Ephesians 6:16).

[^4581]: Theotokion of Ode 4, Canon of the Apostles, praying for divine medicine against the venomous bites of the ancient serpent.

[^4582]: Heirmos of Ode 4, Canon to Saint Nicholas, Tone 4 (Ὁ καθήμενος ἐν δόξῃ / Сѣдѧ́й въ сла́вѣ), based on Isaiah 19:1.

[^4583]: First troparion of Ode 4, Canon to Saint Nicholas, extolling the universal fame of Nicholas' miracles.

[^4584]: Second troparion of Ode 4, Canon to Saint Nicholas, praising Nicholas for glorifying God through profound episcopal humility.

[^4585]: Third troparion of Ode 4, Canon to Saint Nicholas, recalling the famous miracle of Saint Nicholas saving the three military commanders (Nepotian, Ursus, and Herpylion) from unjust execution by the prefect Ablabius.

[^4586]: Fourth troparion of Ode 4, Canon to Saint Nicholas, invoking the saint's invisible presence and swift consolation in times of trial.

[^4587]: Theotokion of Ode 4, Canon to Saint Nicholas.

[^4588]: Heirmos of Ode 5, Canon of the Holy Apostles, Tone 4 (Σὺ Κύριέ μου φῶς / Ты̀ Гдⷵи мо́й свѣ́тъ), drawing upon Isaiah 9:2 and John 12:46.

[^4589]: First troparion of Ode 5, Canon of the Apostles, employing the Johannine imagery of the True Vine (John 15:1-5) and its fruitful clusters.

[^4590]: Second troparion of Ode 5, Canon of the Apostles, praying for apostolic guidance out of the darkness of despair into the light of divine precepts.

[^4591]: Third troparion of Ode 5, Canon of the Apostles, petitioning deliverance from soul-transgressions and future condemnation.

[^4592]: Theotokion of Ode 5, Canon of the Apostles, completing the petition for divine mercy through the intercession of the Virgin and Apostles.

[^4593]: Heirmos of Ode 5, Canon to Saint Nicholas, Tone 4 (Ἀσεβεῖς οὐκ ὄψονται / Нечести́вїи не оу҆́зрѧтъ), based on the Canticle of Isaiah (Isa. 26:9-10).

[^4594]: First troparion of Ode 5, Canon to Saint Nicholas, comparing Nicholas' earthly departure to the setting sun and his heavenly glorification to radiant daylight.

[^4595]: Second troparion of Ode 5, Canon to Saint Nicholas, invoking the grace of the Holy Spirit residing within Saint Nicholas to dispel tribulations.

[^4596]: Third troparion of Ode 5, Canon to Saint Nicholas, pleading for complete healing from worldly passions.

[^4597]: Theotokion of Ode 5, Canon to Saint Nicholas, recalling the Messianic prophecy of the Virgin Birth in Isaiah 7:14.

[^4598]: Opening phrase of the Heirmos of Ode 6, Canon of the Holy Apostles, Tone 4 (Θύσω σοι μετὰ φωνῆς / Пожрꙋ̀ тебѣ̀), based on the Canticle of Jonah (Jonah 2:9). The heirmos splits across leaves p465 and p466.

[^4599]: Conclusion of the Heirmos of Ode 6, Canon of the Holy Apostles, from leaf p465, commemorating the cleansing Blood and water that flowed from Christ's pierced side (John 19:34).

[^4600]: First troparion of Ode 6, Canon of the Apostles, reflecting on the Apostles transforming ravenous wolves into gentle sheep of Christ's flock.

[^4601]: Second troparion of Ode 6, Canon of the Apostles, styling the Apostles as fruitful trees of paradise that transform the barrenness of the soul.

[^4602]: Third troparion of Ode 6, Canon of the Apostles, invoking the apostolic gift of raising the dead (Matthew 10:8) to resurrect a soul slain by carnal pleasures.

[^4603]: Theotokion of Ode 6, Canon of the Apostles, invoking the combined prayers of the Theotokos, Apostles, and Martyrs.

[^4604]: Heirmos of Ode 6, Canon to Saint Nicholas, Tone 4 (Ἦλθον εἰς τὰ βάθη / Прїидо́хъ въ глубины̀), based on Jonah 2:3-6.

[^4605]: First troparion of Ode 6, Canon to Saint Nicholas, petitioning deliverance from the fierce harm of the invisible demonic foe.

[^4606]: Second troparion of Ode 6, Canon to Saint Nicholas, asking for salvation from the torments of Gehenna and the malice of deceitful men.

[^4607]: Third troparion of Ode 6, Canon to Saint Nicholas, again referencing the delivery of the three condemned imperial officers from execution.

[^4608]: Theotokion of Ode 6, Canon to Saint Nicholas.

[^4609]: Heirmos of Ode 7, Canon of the Holy Apostles, Tone 4 (Ἐν τῇ καμίνῳ Ἀβραμιαῖοι / Въ пещѝ А҆враа́мстїи), based on Daniel 3:26-28.

[^4610]: First troparion of Ode 7, Canon of the Apostles, depicting apostolic preaching as melting the winter chill of pagan delusion.

[^4611]: Second troparion of Ode 7, Canon of the Apostles, splitting across leaves p466 and p467.

[^4612]: Conclusion of the second troparion of Ode 7, Canon of the Apostles, from leaf p466.

[^4613]: Third troparion of Ode 7, Canon of the Apostles, seeking preservation from carnal defilement.

[^4614]: Theotokion of Ode 7, Canon of the Apostles, invoking the joint supplication of the angelic orders, martyrs, and apostles before the divine Word.

[^4615]: Heirmos of Ode 7, Canon to Saint Nicholas, Tone 4 (Νέοι τρεῖς ἐν Βαβυλῶνι / Ю́́нѡши трѝ въ Вавѷлѡ́нѣ), based on Daniel 3:28ff.

[^4616]: First troparion of Ode 7, Canon to Saint Nicholas, petitioning Nicholas to pray to the Creator Who rests in His saints (cf. Isa. 57:15).

[^4617]: Second troparion of Ode 7, Canon to Saint Nicholas, extolling Nicholas' priestly virtues of meekness, gentleness, and humility.

[^4618]: Third troparion of Ode 7, Canon to Saint Nicholas, entreating deliverance from all lawlessness through Nicholas' observance of the divine commandments.

[^4619]: Theotokion of Ode 7, Canon to Saint Nicholas, beseeching the Virgin to banish the spiritual lethargy and slumber of despondency (*acedia*).

[^4620]: Heirmos of Ode 8, Canon of the Holy Apostles, Tone 4 (Χεῖρας ἐκπετάσας Δανιήλ / Рꙋ́цѣ распросте́ръ Данїи́лъ), combining the narrative of Daniel in the lions' den (Daniel 6:16-24) and the Three Youths in the furnace (Daniel 3).

[^4621]: First troparion of Ode 8, Canon of the Apostles, portraying the Apostles as fiery mouths of Christ delivering believers from the jaws of the spiritual wolf (Satan).

[^4622]: Second troparion of Ode 8, Canon of the Apostles, splitting across leaves p467 and p468.

[^4623]: Conclusion of the second troparion of Ode 8, Canon of the Apostles, from leaf p467.

[^4624]: Third troparion of Ode 8, Canon of the Apostles, an autobiographical penitential confession borrowing the imagery of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15:11-32).

[^4625]: Theotokion of Ode 8, Canon of the Apostles.

[^4626]: Heirmos of Ode 8, Canon to Saint Nicholas, Tone 4 (Λυτρωτὰ τοῦ παντὸς / И҆зба́вителю всѣ́хъ), celebrating the Redeemer's dew in the Babylonian furnace.

[^4627]: First troparion of Ode 8, Canon to Saint Nicholas, commemorating Saint Nicholas' defense of Orthodox dogma and condemnation of the Arian heresy at the First Ecumenical Council of Nicaea (325 AD).

[^4628]: Second troparion of Ode 8, Canon to Saint Nicholas, playing on the Greek etymology of the name Nicholas (*Nikolaos*, from *nikē*, "victory", and *laos*, "people" — "conqueror of the people" / "victory of the people").

[^4629]: Third troparion of Ode 8, Canon to Saint Nicholas, pleading for the saint's assistance in times of urgent necessity.

[^4630]: Triadicon of Ode 8, Canon to Saint Nicholas, a trinitarian doxology confessing the consubstantial Trinity in orthodox worship.

[^4631]: Theotokion of Ode 8, Canon to Saint Nicholas, invoking the Virgin's protection at the dread Dread Judgment.

[^4632]: Heirmos of Ode 9, Canon of the Holy Apostles, Tone 4 (Λίθος ἀχειρότμητος / Ка́мень нерꙋкосѣ́чный), based on Daniel's prophetic vision of the stone cut without hands from the mountain (Daniel 2:34-35, 44-45), typifying the Virgin Birth.

[^4633]: First troparion of Ode 9, Canon of the Apostles, styling the Apostles as living chosen stones building up the Church upon Christ the cornerstone (1 Peter 2:4-6; Ephesians 2:20).

[^4634]: Second troparion of Ode 9, Canon of the Apostles, splitting across physical leaves p468 and p469.

[^4635]: Conclusion of the second troparion of Ode 9, Canon of the Apostles, from leaf p468, referencing the apostolic power of binding and loosing (Matthew 16:19; 18:18).

[^4636]: Third troparion of Ode 9, Canon of the Apostles, invoking the Apostles as spiritual rain-bearing clouds watering the arid heart.

[^4637]: Theotokion of Ode 9, Canon of the Apostles.

[^4638]: Heirmos of Ode 9, Canon to Saint Nicholas, Tone 4 (Ἡ μὲν τῷ τῆς παρακοῆς νοσήματι / Е́́ѵа оу҆́бѡ недꙋ́гомъ), contrasting Eve's disobedience with the Mother of God's fruitful obedience.

[^4639]: First troparion of Ode 9, Canon to Saint Nicholas, celebrating the continuous flow of miraculous, healing myrrh (*myron*) exuding from the holy relics of Saint Nicholas in Myra (and subsequently Bari).

[^4640]: Second troparion of Ode 9, Canon to Saint Nicholas, comparing Nicholas' universal illumination of the cosmos to the solar rays.

[^4641]: Third troparion of Ode 9, Canon to Saint Nicholas, imploring habitual pastoral mercy against the triple onslaught of worldly distress, demonic illusion, and wicked slanderers.

[^4642]: Fourth troparion of Ode 9, Canon to Saint Nicholas, a self-reflective admonition to contemplate the dread Day of Judgment.

[^4643]: Theotokion of Ode 9, Canon to Saint Nicholas, weaving the angelic greeting of Archangel Gabriel (Luke 1:28) with the typological figure of the garden containing the Tree of Life (Genesis 2:9).

[^4644]: First Sticheron at the Aposticha of Thursday Matins, Tone 4, commemorating the illumination of the apostolic college by the Holy Spirit at Pentecost.

[^4645]: Psalm 89:14, 16 [LXX 89:14, 16], appointed psalm verse for Thursday Matins Aposticha. Masoretic versification: Ps. 90:14, 16.

[^4646]: Second Sticheron at the Aposticha of Thursday Matins, Tone 4, praising the Holy Spirit for transforming unlettered fishermen (*agrammatoi*, cf. Acts 4:13) into universal doctors of the Church through the gift of tongues.

[^4647]: Psalm 89:17 [LXX 89:17], concluding psalm verse for Thursday Matins Aposticha. Masoretic versification: Ps. 90:17.

[^4648]: Martyricon sticheron at the Aposticha, commemorating the victorious struggle of the holy martyrs amidst cold, sword, and flame, citing the spirit of Psalm 115:6 [LXX 115:6; Masoretic Ps. 116:15].

[^4649]: Theotokion concluding the Aposticha of Thursday Matins, Tone 4.

[^4650]: Opening Beatitudes troparion at Thursday Divine Liturgy, Tone 4. The hymn juxtaposes Adam's expulsion through the tree of knowledge with the Wise Thief's entrance into Paradise through the tree of the Cross (Luke 23:39-43).

[^4651]: First Beatitudes troparion for Thursday Liturgy, invoking Christ sending His Apostles as lambs into the midst of wolves (Matthew 10:16; Luke 10:3).

[^4652]: Second Beatitudes troparion for Thursday Liturgy, comparing the Apostles to radiant stars illuminating the earth with evangelical light.

[^4653]: Martyricon troparion of the Beatitudes at Thursday Liturgy, praising the martyrs who consumed the matter of polytheism in the fire of their suffering.

[^4654]: Doxology (*Glory: Triadicon*) of the Beatitudes at Thursday Liturgy, Tone 4, beginning a trinitarian hymn that splits across leaves p470 and p471 (*Трⷪце нераз-* / *дѣ́лнаѧ*).

[^4655]: Conclusion of the trinitarian hymn (*Glory: Triadicon*) of the Beatitudes at Thursday Liturgy, Tone 4, continued from leaf p470.

[^4656]: Concluding Theotokion of the Beatitudes at Thursday Liturgy, Tone 4.

[^4657]: Primary day opening for Friday of Tone 4, dedicated to the Precious and Life-Giving Cross of the Lord, beginning at Thursday Vespers.

[^4658]: First sticheron of the Cross at "Lord, I have cried," Tone 4, recalling the cosmic portents at Christ's Crucifixion: the earthquake, the splitting of rocks, the tearing of the temple veil, and the solar eclipse (Matthew 27:45, 51).

[^4659]: Second sticheron of the Cross at "Lord, I have cried," Tone 4, contrasting the Sanhedrin's unjust condemnation of Christ with His divine role as the Lawgiver of Sinai (Exodus 19-20).

[^4660]: Third sticheron of the Cross at "Lord, I have cried," Tone 4, meditating on the blotting out of the handwritten bond of human sin through the spear-thrust in Christ's side (Colossians 2:14; John 19:34).

[^4661]: Rubric directing the insertion of stichera from the Menaion or, in their absence, the appointed octoechal stichera to the Mother of God, Tone 4, sung to the prosomoion *As one valiant among martyrs* (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ / Ὡς γενναῖον ἐν Μάρτυσιν).

[^4662]: First sticheron to the Theotokos at "Lord, I have cried," Tone 4, continuing across physical leaves p471 and p472.

[^4663]: Conclusion of the first sticheron to the Theotokos at "Lord, I have cried," from leaf p471.

[^4664]: Second sticheron to the Theotokos at "Lord, I have cried," Tone 4, applying the parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:30-37) to the soul wounded by demonic thieves.

[^4665]: Third sticheron to the Theotokos at "Lord, I have cried," Tone 4, petitioning deliverance from the predatory attacks of the demonic lion (cf. 1 Peter 5:8; Psalm 7:3 [LXX 7:2]).

[^4666]: Stavrotheotokion at "Lord, I have cried," Tone 4, depicting the Mother of God's maternal anguish beneath the Cross amidst the darkening of celestial luminaries.

[^4667]: Standard rubrical direction for the chanting of *Phos Hilaron* ("O Joyful Light") and the Thursday evening prokeimenon (*My help comes from the Lord*, Psalm 120:2 [LXX 120:2]).

[^4668]: First sticheron of the Cross at the Aposticha of Thursday Vespers, Tone 4.

[^4669]: Psalm 122:1-2 [LXX 122:1-2], appointed first verse for the Aposticha at weekday Vespers. Masoretic versification: Ps. 123:1-2.

[^4670]: Second sticheron of the Cross at the Aposticha of Thursday Vespers, Tone 4.

[^4671]: Psalm 122:3-4 [LXX 122:3-4], appointed second verse for the Aposticha at weekday Vespers. Masoretic versification: Ps. 123:3-4.

[^4672]: Martyricon sticheron concluding the cycle at the Aposticha of Thursday Vespers, Tone 4.

[^4673]: Stavrotheotokion at the Aposticha of Thursday Vespers, Tone 4, modeled on *Being called from on high* (Зва́нный свы́ше / Ὁ κληθεὶς ἄνωθεν). The hymn anticipates the Great Saturday heirmos *Do not lament Me, O Mother* (Не рыда́й менѐ Ма́ти).

[^4674]: Concluding rubrics for Thursday Vespers, comprising the Canticle of Simeon (Luke 2:29-32), the Trisagion Prayers, the troparion of the Cross (*Save, O Lord, Thy people*), the augmented litany, and the priestly dismissal.

[^4677]: Appointed refrain for the Compline canon to the Mother of God.

[^4678]: First troparion of Ode 1, Compline Canon to the Theotokos, Tone 4.

[^4679]: Second troparion of Ode 1, Compline Canon to the Theotokos, Tone 4.

[^4695]: Second troparion of Ode 5, Compline Canon to the Theotokos, Tone 4, contrasting Christ's piercing by the spear (John 19:34) with the crushing of Satan's serpentine power.

[^4696]: Third troparion of Ode 5, Compline Canon to the Theotokos, Tone 4.

[^4698]: Opening of the Heirmos of Ode 6, Compline Canon to the Theotokos, Tone 4 (Τὴν θείαν ταύτην καὶ πάντιμον / Бж҃твенное сіѐ и҆ всечестно́е), based on the Canticle of Jonah; continuing on leaf p475.

[^4722]: Conclusion of the Theotokion of Ode 9, Compline Canon to the Theotokos, from leaf p476, affirming Christ's unconfused Incarnation (*atreptōs* / непремѣ́ннѡ) and the overthrow of Satan.

[^4723]: Concluding rubrics for Compline, comprising the hymn *It is truly meet* (Axion Estin) with a prostration, the Trisagion Prayers, the troparion, and the usual small dismissal.

[^4724]: Friday Matins, Tone 4.

[^4725]: First Sessional hymn of the Cross after the First Kathisma at Friday Matins, Tone 4, utilizing the classic Pauline soteriological formulation of Galatians 3:13 ("Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law").
