[^8138]: Ode 3 Troparion 2: Genesis 3:15; Acts 2:24. Christ's descent into hades by the power of the Cross to heal the spiritual venom of the serpent.

[^8139]: Ode 3 Theotokion: Codicological witness of the 1895 Lviv Stauropegion edition, providing the diplomatic petition for the reigning sovereign: "І҆мпера́торꙋ (И҆́мкꙋ) побѣ́дꙋ да́рꙋй на ва́рвары врагѝ" ("grant victory unto the Emperor [Name] over barbarian enemies"), commemorating Apostolic King Franz Joseph I of Austria-Hungary.

[^8140]: Canon of Cross & Resurrection, Ode 3 Heirmos: Psalm 103:2–5 LXX. The establishment of heaven and earth by divine volition as a type of the steadfastness of faith in Christ.

[^8141]: Ode 3 Troparion 1: Luke 23:43. Christ opening Paradise unto the penitent thief through the voluntary passion of the Cross.

[^8142]: Ode 3 Troparion 2: John 11:25. Christ the Giver of life rising on the third day and shining upon creation.

[^8143]: Ode 3 Theotokion: Genesis 3:16. The virginal conception of the Word delivering Eve from the curse.

[^8144]: Ode 3 Heirmos incipit of the Theotokos Canon, repeating the theme of the creation of the heavens.

[^8145]: Ode 3 Troparion 1: Genesis 3:4–5. The deceit of the serpent who promised deification through transgression, overturned by the divine condescension of the incarnate Word.

[^8146]: Ode 3 Troparion 2: Luke 1:42. Elizabeth's salutation to the Mother of God, whose fruit dispels ancestral sorrow.

[^8147]: Ode 3 Troparion 3: Ephesians 2:14–16. Christ as our peace reconciling humanity unto the Father through the mediation of the Virgin.

[^8148]: Ode 4 Heirmos: Habakkuk 3:2 LXX: "O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid; O Lord, I considered Thy works, and was astonished."

[^8149]: Ode 4 Troparion 1: Isaiah 50:6: "I gave My back to scourges, and My cheeks to blows." The sinless Master suffering stripes in place of the guilty servant.

[^8150]: Ode 4 Troparion 2: John 18:22; Matthew 26:67. The Judge of all standing before the earthly tribunal and struck by a hand of clay.

[^8151]: Ode 4 Theotokion: The Virgin Mother guiding the faithful into the spiritual haven of salvation (sentence bridges to physical leaf p763).

[^8152]: Continuation of Ode 4 Theotokion from leaf p762: "приста́нищꙋ, Всенепоро́чнаѧ, сла́внагѡ є҆гѡ̀ хотѣ́нїа" (haven of His glorious will).

[^8153]: Canon of Cross & Resurrection, Ode 4 Heirmos: Habakkuk 3:13 LXX: "Thou wentest forth for the salvation of Thy people, to save Thine anointed."

[^8154]: Ode 4 Troparion 1: 2 Corinthians 5:21; Hebrews 2:14. Christ, Who knew no sin, assuming human flesh to destroy the devil through death.

[^8155]: Ode 4 Troparion 2: Colossians 2:14. Christ lifted up upon the Cross to cancel the debt of Adam's transgression.

[^8156]: Ode 4 Theotokion: Christ's bodily death overcoming death and reviving Adam who had fallen through delusion.

[^8157]: Ode 4 Heirmos incipit of the Theotokos Canon: "Ѻ҆́тча нѣ́дра не ѡ҆ста́вль" (Leaving not the Father's bosom).

[^8158]: Ode 4 Troparion 1: Song of Songs 4:7: "Thou art all fair, My love; there is no spot in thee." The Virgin chosen in the divine counsel before all creation.

[^8159]: Ode 4 Troparion 2: The Mother of God bearing the Word incarnate from her pure blood, granting remission of sins.

[^8160]: Ode 4 Troparion 3: Rational human and angelic nature offering liturgical and sacerdotal praise unto Christ for the miracle of the Virgin birth.

[^8161]: Ode 5 Heirmos: Isaiah 26:9 LXX: "With my soul have I desired Thee in the night; yea, with my spirit within me will I seek Thee early."

[^8162]: Ode 5 Troparion 1: Zechariah 11:12; Matthew 26:15; Micah 5:1. Christ betrayed for thirty pieces of silver and smitten upon the cheek to procure divine freedom.

[^8163]: Ode 5 Troparion 2: 1 Corinthians 1:25. The divine strength manifested through the weakness of the flesh, triumphing over death.

[^8164]: Ode 5 Theotokion: Luke 1:34–35. The virgin birth accomplished by the overshadowing of the Holy Spirit without human fatherhood.

[^8165]: Canon of Cross & Resurrection, Ode 5 Heirmos: Isaiah 26:9 LXX. The soul's early dawn vigil seeking divine enlightenment and forgiveness.

[^8166]: Ode 5 Troparion 1: Matthew 27:45, 51; Mark 15:38. The darkening of the sun and renting of the temple veil at Golgotha testifying to the end of the Old Covenant.

[^8167]: Ode 5 Troparion 2: Hebrews 2:14. Christ destroying the tyrant's kingdom by His almighty Godhead and raising the dead.

[^8168]: Ode 5 Theotokion: Supplication to the Theotokos for cleansing of sins and divine intercession.

[^8169]: Ode 5 Heirmos incipit of the Theotokos Canon: "Но́щь несвѣ́тла невѣ́рнымъ" (Night without light is unto the unbelieving).

[^8170]: Ode 5 Troparion 1: Genesis 28:12. Jacob's ladder connecting heaven and earth as a prophetic prefiguration of the Incarnation through the Theotokos.

[^8171]: Ode 5 Troparion 2 (part 1): The faithful receiving eternal redemption through the Mother of God (text bridges to physical leaf p765).

[^8172]: Ode 5 Troparion 2 (part 2): Continuation from leaf p764: Gabriel's greeting ("Rejoice, O Bride of God") offered in spiritual joy.

[^8173]: Ode 5 Troparion 3: Song of Songs 2:2: "As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters." The heavenly Bridegroom choosing the all-pure Virgin.

[^8174]: Ode 6 Heirmos: Jonah 2:3–7 LXX. The prophet Jonah swallowed by the sea monster as a type of the soul tossed on the turbulent sea of life.

[^8175]: Ode 6 Troparion 1: 1 Peter 3:19–20; 4:6. Christ preaching deliverance and salvation unto the spirits held in hades.

[^8176]: Ode 6 Troparion 2: John 2:19–22. The temple of Christ's body destroyed by the Passion and rebuilt on the third day, transforming apostolic sorrow into triumph.

[^8177]: Ode 6 Theotokion (part 1): The ineffable mystery of the Virgin's virginal conception and childbirth (text bridges to physical leaf p765).

[^8178]: Continuation of Ode 6 Theotokion from leaf p764: "кто̀ ѿ человѣ́къ сказа́ти возмо́жетъ?" (who among men is able to recount? The uncircumscribed Word united unto flesh).

[^8179]: Canon of Cross & Resurrection, Ode 6 Heirmos: Jonah 2:2 LXX: "I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the Lord, and He heard me."

[^8180]: Ode 6 Troparion 1: Matthew 27:51. The shaking of the earth at the crucifixion of the Master, healing the wounds of creation.

[^8181]: Ode 6 Troparion 2: 1 Corinthians 15:20–22. Christ opening a path of life and resurrection for mankind through His triumph over hades.

[^8182]: Ode 6 Theotokion: The Theotokos as the steadfast hope and protectress of all faithful believers.

[^8183]: Ode 6 Heirmos incipit of the Theotokos Canon: "Пла́ваѧ въ молвѣ̀ жите́йскихъ" (Sailing in the surge of worldly cares).

[^8184]: Ode 6 Troparion 1: Hebrews 1:1. The Old Testament figures and prophecies prefiguring the incarnation of the universal Benefactor.

[^8185]: Ode 6 Troparion 2 (part 1): Adam exiled from the delight of Paradise through the serpent's malice (text bridges to right column of leaf p765).

[^8186]: Ode 6 Troparion 2 (part 2): The restoration of Adam and fallen humanity through the virgin birth of the Redeemer.

[^8187]: Ode 6 Troparion 3: Colossians 1:16; John 1:4–5. The Creator of all things illuminating the gloom of death with the lightning flashes of His Divinity.

[^8188]: Sunday Resurrectional Kontakion, Tone 7: The destruction of the power of death and the liberation of hades, summoning the faithful to enter into the resurrection.

[^8189]: Sunday Resurrectional Ikos, Tone 7: Hades and death trembling before One of the Trinity; the Tree of the Cross restoring Adam and his descendants to Paradise.

[^8190]: Ode 7 Heirmos: Daniel 3:49–50; Song of the Three Holy Children. The fiery furnace of Babylon transformed into dropping dew by the presence of the Angel of the Lord.

[^8191]: Ode 7 Troparion 1: Romans 5:12–19. The disobedience of Adam at the tree of Eden overturned by the voluntary obedience and crucifixion of the Son of God.

[^8192]: Ode 7 Troparion 2: Christ rising from the tomb as the radiant light blossoming in hades and imparting life to the dead.

[^8193]: Ode 7 Theotokion: The Virgin Mary addressed as daughter of Adam, through whom corruption was vanquished and salvation revealed.

[^8194]: Canon of Cross & Resurrection, Ode 7 Heirmos: Daniel 3:26, 52 LXX. The Three Youths praising the God of our fathers in the midst of the flames.

[^8195]: Ode 7 Troparion 1 (part 1): Colossians 2:14. Christ blunting the sting of sin and tearing up the handwriting of human debt with the soldier's spear (text bridges to leaf p767).

[^8196]: Ode 7 Troparion 1 (part 2): The biblical refrain of Ode 7: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers."

[^8197]: Ode 7 Troparion 2: Hebrews 9:13–14; John 19:34. The divine blood from Christ's pierced side cleansing the earth defiled by the blood of pagan sacrifices.

[^8198]: Ode 7 Triadikon: Orthodox Trinitarian theology confessing one undivided Divine Essence in three distinct Hypostases: Father, Word, and Holy Spirit.

[^8199]: Ode 7 Heirmos incipit of the Theotokos Canon: "Пе́щь ѻ҆́трѡцы ѻ҆гнепа́льнꙋ дре́вле" (Of old the Children showed forth the fiery furnace).

[^8200]: Ode 7 Troparion 1: Psalm 44:10, 14 LXX. The Queen arrayed in golden vesture, loved and honored by her Creator and Lord.

[^8201]: Ode 7 Troparion 2: Isaiah 6:6–7. The live coal of the Seraph touching the prophet's lips prefiguring the divine fire borne in the Virgin's womb.

[^8202]: Ode 7 Troparion 3: The ancient prophets rejoicing in the symbolic visions of the mystery of the virgin birth (text bridges to physical leaf p767).

[^8203]: Continuation of Ode 7 Troparion 3 from leaf p766: "ва́хꙋ: превозноси́мый ѻ҆тце́въ Бг҃ъ, и҆ препросла́вленъ" (crying aloud: The supremely exalted and supremely glorified God of our fathers).

[^8204]: Ode 8 Heirmos: Exodus 3:2; Daniel 3:57. The burning bush on Mount Sinai and the Three Youths in the furnace revealing the mystery of God without consuming human weakness.

[^8205]: Ode 8 Troparion 1: Hebrews 9:11–12; 10:1–14. Christ the rational Lamb slain for the sins of the world, replacing the shadow of Mosaic animal sacrifices.

[^8206]: Ode 8 Troparion 2: 1 Corinthians 15:42–44. Human flesh, once subject to corruption, made incorruptible and glorified through the Passion and Resurrection of the Savior.

[^8207]: Ode 8 Theotokion: The purity of the Mother of God sanctifying the defilement of creation and reconciling humanity unto God.

[^8208]: Canon of Cross & Resurrection, Ode 8 Heirmos: Daniel 3:57–90. The angelic choirs and all created works exhorted to supremely exalt the unoriginate King of glory.

[^8209]: Ode 8 Troparion 1: Christ's voluntary crucifixion and shattering of the power of hades.

[^8210]: Ode 8 Troparion 2: Hebrews 2:14–15. The abolition of death's dominion and the glorious rising from the tomb.

[^8211]: Ode 8 Theotokion: The pre-eternal Word born of the Virgin Mary, loosing the ancient curse of Eve.

[^8212]: Ode 8 Heirmos incipit of the Theotokos Canon: "Неѡпа́льнаѧ ѻ҆гню̀ въ Сїна́и прича́щшаѧсѧ" (The bush unconsumed by fire that had communion on Sinai).

[^8213]: Ode 8 Troparion 1: The light of the Nativity illuminating the world, as the Virgin holds the uncontainable God in her arms (text bridges to physical leaf p768).

[^8214]: Continuation of Ode 8 Troparion 1 from leaf p767: The liturgical refrain of the Benedicite: "All ye works of the Lord, sing the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages."

[^8215]: Ode 8 Troparion 2: The womb of the Virgin containing the uncircumscribed God and enlightening the faithful with divine knowledge.

[^8216]: Ode 8 Troparion 3: The Mother of God as the dwelling-place of light, transfiguring believers into children of divine illumination.

[^8217]: Sunday Matins rubric: The Canticle of the Theotokos (Magnificat, Luke 1:46–55) with the megalynarion "More honorable than the Cherubim" chanted before Ode 9.

[^8218]: Ode 9 Heirmos: The Virgin Mary lending flesh unto the divine Word, becoming the spiritual vessel of the uncontainable Creator.

[^8219]: Ode 9 Troparion 1: Patristic christological defense against Theopaschism: Christ suffered in the flesh on the Cross while remaining impassible in His Divine nature.

[^8220]: Ode 9 Troparion 2: 1 Corinthians 15:12–20. The empty tomb of Christ as incontrovertible proof and earnest of the universal physical resurrection.

[^8221]: Ode 9 Triadikon: Classical Trinitarian refutation of Sabellian modalism (confusing the Persons) and Arian subordinationism (dividing the Essence).

[^8222]: Canon of Cross & Resurrection, Ode 9 Heirmos: The paradox of virginal childbirth surpassing the laws of nature through the condescension of God.

[^8223]: Ode 9 Troparion 1: Nicene Creed; Hebrews 1:3. Christ as Light from Light and the radiance of the Father's glory dispelling spiritual darkness.

[^8224]: Ode 9 Troparion 2: Council of Chalcedon (451 AD). Refutation of Monophysitism: Christ possessing two natures without confusion, truly dying as man and rising as God.

[^8225]: Ode 9 Troparion 3: Mark 16:1–6; Luke 24:5. The angel at the sepulcher directing the myrrh-bearing women to offer hymns to the living God rather than myrrh for a corpse.

[^8226]: Ode 9 Theotokion: Psalm 44:11–12 LXX. The Church gathered from the Gentile nations confessing Christ as the only God and Bridegroom.

[^8227]: Rubric: Ode 9 Heirmos of the Theotokos Canon sung to the melody of the preceding canon.

[^8228]: Ode 9 Troparion 1: John 4:24. The Theotokos as the mediatress of eternal joy, giving birth to the Redeemer Who delivers all who worship Him in spirit and truth.

[^8229]: Ode 9 Troparion 2: Psalm 131:8 LXX. King David prophetically identifying the Mother of God as the spiritual Ark of holiness holding the pre-eternal Word.

[^8230]: Ode 9 Troparion 3 (part 1): The Virgin exalted above all creation, bearing the Creator in the flesh (text bridges to right column of leaf p769).

[^8231]: Ode 9 Troparion 3 (part 2): The Mother of God bearing victory over all adversaries as Mother of the supreme Master.

[^8232]: Post-Canon Matins rubrics: The Little Litany, the hymn "Holy is the Lord our God" (Psalm 98:9 LXX), and the Morning Exapostilarion according to the appointed Sunday Eothinon Gospel cycle.

[^8233]: Matins Praises (Lauds), Tone 7: Psalm 148:1–4; Psalm 150:1. The Resurrectional Sticheron announcing the shattering of death and cosmic joy in heaven and earth.

[^8234]: Praises Sticheron 2: The ancient resurrectional hymn of devotion: worshipping the holy and sinless Lord Jesus Christ.

[^8235]: Praises Sticheron 3: Ceaseless veneration of the third-day Resurrection as the divine victory over iniquity and death.

[^8236]: Praises Sticheron 4 (part 1): Psalm 115:3 LXX; John 1:14; Malachi 4:2. The recapitulation of the Incarnation: the Word becoming flesh, acting as Benefactor, Liberator, and Sun of righteousness (text bridges to physical leaf p770).

[^8237]: Praises Sticheron 4 (part 2): Doxological conclusion: "Къ немꙋ́же возопїи́мъ: Бж҃е на́шъ, сла́ва тебѣ̀" (unto Whom let us cry aloud: O our God, glory to Thee!).

[^8238]: Anatolian (Eastern) Sticheron 1, Tone 7: Christ shattering the gates of hades and raising those who slept in darkness from the beginning of the world.

[^8239]: Anatolian Sticheron 2, Tone 7: The summons to rejoice in the Lord for freeing souls from the unloosed bonds of hades and granting eternal life.

[^8240]: Matins Praises Stichos: Psalm 9:33 LXX (Masoretic 9:12 / 10:12): "Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor unto the end."

[^8241]: Anatolian Sticheron 3, Tone 7: Matthew 28:2–7; Mark 16:5–7. The angel shining on the stone of the tomb, commanding the women to tell the disciples that Christ goes before them into Galilee.

[^8242]: Matins Praises Stichos: Psalm 9:2 LXX: "I will give thanks unto Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; I will tell of all Thy marvelous works."

[^8243]: Anatolian Sticheron 4, Tone 7: Psalm 117:22; Daniel 2:34–35, 45; Daniel 7:13–14; Numbers 20:11. Comprehensive prophetic typology: the rejected cornerstone, the rock flowing with water in the desert, the stone cut from the mountain without hands, and the Son of Man coming on the clouds to receive an everlasting kingdom.

[^8244]: Matins concluding rubrics: Doxasticon on "Glory" from the 11 Evangelical Stichera, "Both now" with the Theotokion "Most blessed art thou", chanting of the Great Doxology, and the Sunday Resurrectional Troparion "Today salvation is come unto the world" (Дне́сь спасе́нїе мі́рꙋ бы́сть).

[^8245]: Liturgical rubric opening the Divine Liturgy: The Beatitudes (Matthew 5:3–12) in Tone 7 with appointed Resurrectional troparia.

[^8246]: Liturgy Beatitudes Troparion 1: Genesis 2:9, 17; 3:6; Luke 23:42. The contrast between the deadly fruit of Eden and Christ the true Tree of Life, joined with the cry of the penitent thief.

[^8247]: Liturgy Beatitudes Troparion 2: Colossians 2:14. Christ lifted up upon the Cross to blot out the handwriting of Adam's ancient transgression (sentence bridges to physical leaf p771).

[^8248]: Physical leaf p771 (printed fol. 771, ѱѻ҃а). Continuation of Troparion 2 of the Sunday Beatitudes (Tone 7) from p770: "рукописа́ніе дре́внягѡ греха̀ А҆да́м... / ...ха̀ загла́дилъ є҆сѝ, и҆ спа́слъ є҆сѝ ѿ пре́лести ве́сь ро́дъ человѣ́ческій; тѣ́мже воспѣва́емъ тѧ̀, благодѣ́телю Гдⷭ҇и" (Thou hast blotted out the handwriting of Adam's ancient sin, and hast saved the whole human race from deception; therefore we sing unto Thee, O Benefactor and Lord).

[^8249]: Physical leaf p771. Troparion 3 of the Sunday Beatitudes (Tone 7): contrasting the venom of the serpent poured into Eve's hearing with the sweetness of eternal life poured forth into the world from Christ's pierced side upon the Tree of the Cross.

[^8250]: Physical leaf p771. Troparion 4 of the Sunday Beatitudes (Tone 7): Christ laid in the tomb as mortal yet breaking the iron bars of hades as almighty God and enlightening all by His third-day resurrection.

[^8251]: Physical leaf p771. Troparion 5 of the Sunday Beatitudes (Tone 7): the resurrection of Christ raising Adam and restoring the ancient incorruption of paradise; concluding with the prayer of the wise thief (Luke 23:42).

[^8252]: Physical leaf p771. Troparion 6 of the Sunday Beatitudes (Tone 7): Christ's post-resurrection bestowal of peace upon the disciples and the apostolic commission to bring all nations into His kingdom (cf. Matt. 28:18–20; John 20:19–21).

[^8253]: Physical leaf p771. Triadikon (Glory...): orthodox confession of the Holy Trinity as one Light in three Hypostases (Father, Son, and Holy Spirit), undivided and unconfused in one Divine nature and principle.

[^8254]: Physical leaf p771. Theotokion (Both now...): the ineffable incarnation of the pre-eternal Word from the Virgin Mother for the deification (theosis) of mankind and the salvation of Christians.

[^8255]: Physical leaf p771. Codicological and liturgical landmark: opening of the weekly liturgical cycle of Monday, dedicated to the Holy Bodiless Powers of Heaven (Archangels, Angels, and the celestial hierarchies).

[^8256]: Physical leaf p771. Rubric: Sunday Evening Vespers (Въ Недѣ́лю ве́чера), which initiates the liturgical day of Monday in the Byzantine rite.

[^8257]: Physical leaf p771. Rubric: Penitential Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" in Tone 7 (На Гдⷭ҇и воззва́хъ: стїхи̑ры покаѧ́нны. Гла́съ з҃).

[^8258]: Physical leaf p771. Melodic model heading: *Tone 7, Podoben: "Today Judas watches" (Дне́сь бди́тъ І҆ꙋ́да):*, registered under canonical identifier POD.T7.DNES_BDIT_IUDA.

[^8259]: Physical leaf p771. Sticheron 1 on "Lord, I have cried" (opens on p771, concluding on p772): compunctionate contemplation of the soul calling upon the divine condescension (kenosis) whereby God bowed the heavens and descended to raise man from the mire of passions unto the rock of faith.

[^8260]: Physical leaf p772 (printed fol. 772, ѱѻ҃в). Conclusion of Sticheron 1 on "Lord, I have cried" from p771: "...ry to Thy condescension, O Lover of mankind!" (Сла́ва и҆стоща́нію твоемꙋ̀, Человѣколю́бче).

[^8261]: Physical leaf p772. Sticheron 2 on "Lord, I have cried": dramatic rhetorical examination of conscience; the sinner marvelling that the earth has not swallowed him nor beasts devoured him, calling for immediate repentance before the Lord.

[^8262]: Physical leaf p772. Sticheron 3 on "Lord, I have cried": petition for deliverance from spiritual adversity, worldly turmoil, and passion, praying to find Christ a clement and merciful Master on the Day of Judgment.

[^8263]: Physical leaf p772. Rubric: Stichera to the Saint of the day from the Menaion; in their absence, the following three stichera to the Holy Bodiless Angels are appointed.

[^8264]: Physical leaf p772. Melodic model heading: *Tone 7, Podoben: "No longer are we forbidden" (Не ктомꙋ̀ возбрани́ми):*, registered under canonical identifier POD.T7.NE_KTOMU_VOZBRANENI.

[^8265]: Physical leaf p772. Sticheron 1 to the Bodiless Angels: petition unto the Holy Archangels, who are enlightened by the uncreated rays of the Trinity, to enlighten the faithful.

[^8266]: Physical leaf p772. Sticheron 2 to the Bodiless Angels: the celestial powers characterized as "secondary lights" (свѣ́ти вторі́и) by participation in the Primary Light (свѣ́тъ пе́рвый), reflecting Dionysian angelology (De Coelesti Hierarchia).

[^8267]: Physical leaf p772. Sticheron 3 to the Bodiless Angels: asking the angelic shelter and protection against demonic darkness and the spirits of malice.

[^8268]: Physical leaf p772. Theotokion (Glory... Both now...): praising the Ever-Virgin Mother who nursed the Redeemer with milk and delivered the world from demonic deception.

[^8269]: Physical leaf p772. Rubric: chanting of the evening hymn "O Gladsome Light" (Свѣ́те ти́хїй), the daily Prokeimenon of Sunday evening, and the customary litanies.

[^8270]: Physical leaf p772. Rubric: Penitential Stichera at the Aposticha in Tone 7 (На Стїхо́внѣ, стїхи̑ры покаѧ́нны. Гла́съ з҃).

[^8271]: Physical leaf p772. Sticheron 1 at the Aposticha: returning unto the Father like the prodigal son (Luke 15:11–32) and pleading to be received as one of His hired servants.

[^8272]: Physical leaf p772. Scriptural verse: Psalm 122:1–2 (LXX versification; Masoretic Ps. 123:1–2): "Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes..."

[^8273]: Physical leaf p772. Sticheron 2 at the Aposticha: spiritual allegorization of the Parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:30–37); the soul wounded by robber-passions fleeing unto the heavenly Physician.

[^8274]: Physical leaf p772. Scriptural verse (opens on p772, concluding on p773): Psalm 122:3–4 (LXX versification; Masoretic Ps. 123:3–4): "Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us..."

[^8275]: Physical leaf p773 (printed fol. 773, ѱѻ҃г). Conclusion of Scriptural verse from p772: "...our soul with the reproach of them that are at ease, and with the contempt of the proud" [LXX Ps. 122:4].

[^8276]: Physical leaf p773. Sticheron 3 at the Aposticha (Martyrion/Apostolicum): glorifying Christ as the praise of the Apostles and crown of the Holy Martyrs who confessed the consubstantial Trinity.

[^8277]: Physical leaf p773. Theotokion (Glory... Both now...): Marian greeting ("Rejoice!") uniting classic Old Testament types: bridal chamber, heavenly portal, fiery throne of the Cherubim, unhewn mountain of Daniel, and the burning bush of Sinai.

[^8278]: Physical leaf p773. Rubric: Canticle of Simeon (Ны́нѣ ѿпꙋща́еши / Nunc Dimittis, Luke 2:29–32), Trisagion prayers, Troparia, and standard dismissal of Vespers.

[^8279]: Physical leaf p773. Rubric: Small Compline on Sunday evening (Въ Недѣ́лю на Повече́ріи), preceding Monday Matins.

[^8280]: Physical leaf p773. Rubric: Supplicatory Canon to the Most Holy Mother of God in Tone 7 (Канѡ́нъ моле́бный прест҃ѣ́й Бцⷣѣ. Гла́съ з҃).

[^8281]: Physical leaf p773. Ode 1. Heirmos: the miraculous crossing of the Red Sea by Israel dry-shod when the fluid waters solidified by divine command (Exod. 14:21–29).

[^8282]: Physical leaf p773. Liturgical refrain: "Most Holy Lady Mother of God, save us" (Прест҃а́ѧ Гпⷭ҇жѐ Бцⷣе, спасѝ на́съ).

[^8283]: Physical leaf p773. Troparion 1 of Ode 1: contrasting the sublime angelic praise of the Mother of God with the humble, compunctionate prayer offered from human clay lips.

[^8284]: Physical leaf p773. Troparion 2 of Ode 1: petition unto the Mother of Life to put to death the living lusts of the flesh and grant deliverance from sinful habits.

[^8285]: Physical leaf p773. Glory... Troparion 3 of Ode 1: the eternal Word as "Sun from the Sun" (Со́лнце ѿ Со́лнца) shining forth in time from the Virgin to illumine and instruct human souls.

[^8286]: Physical leaf p773. Both now... Theotokion of Ode 1: perpetual praise due unto the Theotokos as the sure refuge of mortals in worldly tribulation.

[^8287]: Physical leaf p773. Ode 3. Heirmos: the creation and establishment of the heavens by the Word and the Holy Spirit; petition to be grounded upon the unshakable rock of the confession of Christ.

[^8288]: Physical leaf p773. Troparion 1 of Ode 3: rendering grateful homage unto the Mother of the Word and praying for deliverance from worldly afflictions.

[^8289]: Physical leaf p773. Troparion 2 of Ode 3: the restoration of fallen Adam to eternal life through the birth of the Life-originating Word; petition for deliverance from deadly sin.

[^8290]: Physical leaf p774 (printed fol. 774, ѱѻ҃д). Glory... Troparion 3 of Ode 3: the internal warfare between the carnal law of passions and the spiritual law of God (cf. Rom. 7:22–23); petition for the peace of dispassion (apatheia).

[^8291]: Physical leaf p774. Both now... Theotokion of Ode 3: the conception of Christ freeing mortals from the subterranean gates of hades; prayer to rend the ropes of corruption.

[^8292]: Physical leaf p774. Ode 4. Heirmos: the prophetic vision of Christ's incarnation without separation from the Father's bosom (Habakkuk 3:2).

[^8293]: Physical leaf p774. Troparion 1 of Ode 4: spiritual struggle against nocturnal darkness and sorrow; petition unto the "Door of Light" for illumination.

[^8294]: Physical leaf p774. Troparion 2 of Ode 4: the soul bound in chains of multiple sins and trials calling upon the Virgin's unfailing protection.

[^8295]: Physical leaf p774. Glory... Troparion 3 of Ode 4: petition for the confounding of wicked, envious, and deceitful conspiracies against the servant of God.

[^8296]: Physical leaf p774. Both now... Theotokion of Ode 4: prayer to cut off slanderous and deceitful tongues with the sharp sword of the Theotokos's intercessions.

[^8297]: Physical leaf p774. Ode 5. Heirmos: night of blindness for the unbelieving, but dawn and sweetness of the divine words for the faithful; early morning hymnody of Christ's Godhead.

[^8298]: Physical leaf p774. Troparion 1 of Ode 5: the Virgin as an impregnable rampart and protective shelter against grievous tribulations.

[^8299]: Physical leaf p774. Troparion 2 of Ode 5: lamentation over debilitating spiritual and physical weakness, seeking total restoration through the prayers of the Mother of God.

[^8300]: Physical leaf p774. Glory... Troparion 3 of Ode 5: seeking refuge in the ocean of divine tender-heartedness against unjust oppression.

[^8301]: Physical leaf p774. Both now... Theotokion of Ode 5 (opens on p774, concluding on p775): extolling the universal power of the Virgin's intercession to rescue the soul from the storms of life.

[^8302]: Physical leaf p775 (printed fol. 775, ѱѻ҃є). Conclusion of Theotokion of Ode 5 from p774: "...deliver me from every assault of this present life" (мѧ всѧ́кагѡ и҆зба́ви жите́йскагѡ настоѧ́нїа).

[^8303]: Physical leaf p775. Ode 6. Heirmos: the allegorical storm of worldly anxieties and shipwreck of sin; invoking the prayer of Jonah from the belly of the sea monster (Jonah 2:3–10).

[^8304]: Physical leaf p775. Troparion 1 of Ode 6: the universal debt of human transgression blotted out by Christ's nativity; the Mother of God receiving the hymns of her suppliants.

Chalcedonian Christological confession: Christ, simple in His unoriginate divinity, compounded by the assumption of humanity, suffering as man while impassible as God, in two natures indivisibly and unconfusedly (ἀδιαιρέτως καὶ ἀσυγχύτως / нераздѣльно и неслїянно).

[^10901]: Theotokion (Both now) of Ode 5 of the second Canon in Tone 8, praising the Word Who took upon Himself ensouled, rational human flesh to destroy death.

[^10903]: First troparion (Martyrs) of Ode 6 of the first Canon in Tone 8, extolling the martyrs' wounds that heal souls and expel demons.

[^10911]: Doxological troparion (Glory) of Ode 6 of the second Canon in Tone 8, praying for release from tears and sighing in hades, spanning across physical leaves p985 and p986.

[^10913]: Theotokion (Both now) of Ode 6 of the second Canon in Tone 8, contemplating the paradox of the Creator being created in the womb and the Immortal One dying for the salvation of all.

[^10917]: First troparion (Martyrs) of Ode 7 of the first Canon in Tone 8, asking the martyrs who destroyed the fortress of impiety to disperse the burden of sins.

[^10918]: Second troparion (Hierarchs) of Ode 7 of the first Canon in Tone 8, extolling the hierarchs who quenched the fire of heresies and burned up the tares of deceit.

[^10919]: Third troparion (Ascetics, Prophets, and Holy Women) of Ode 7 of the first Canon in Tone 8, commemorating all classes of the righteous.

[^10920]: Doxological troparion (Glory, For the Departed) of Ode 7 of the first Canon in Tone 8, praying for the pardon and rest of the departed.

[^10921]: Theotokion (Both now) of Ode 7 of the first Canon in Tone 8, petitioning the Virgin to cleanse soul and body, spanning across physical leaves p986 and p987.

[^10922]: Conclusion of the Theotokion (Both now) of Ode 7 of the first Canon in Tone 8, continuing from physical leaf p986.

[^10923]: Heirmos of Ode 7 of the second Canon (for the Departed) in Tone 8, recalling the Hebrew children trampling the flame in the furnace.

[^10924]: First troparion (Martyrion) of Ode 7 of the second Canon in Tone 8, celebrating the martyrs' single-minded desire for the Master.

[^10925]: Second troparion of Ode 7 of the second Canon in Tone 8, praying that the departed may receive the garment of incorruption and the light of the Kingdom.

[^10926]: Doxological troparion (Glory) of Ode 7 of the second Canon in Tone 8, asking Christ to fill the departed with joy and gladness.

[^10927]: Theotokion (Both now) of Ode 7 of the second Canon in Tone 8, praising the Savior Who dwelt in the Virgin to loose the curse of Eve.

[^10928]: Heirmos of Ode 8 of the first Canon in Tone 8, based on Daniel 3:57 (Song of the Three Holy Youths).

[^10929]: First troparion (Martyrs) of Ode 8 of the first Canon in Tone 8, praising the martyrs who destroyed idol temples and became temples of the Trinity.

[^10930]: Second troparion (Priests and Hierarchs) of Ode 8 of the first Canon in Tone 8, celebrating the priests clothed in righteousness (Psalm 131:9 LXX) who gaze upon divine beauty.

[^10931]: Third troparion (Prophets, Holy Women, and Righteous) of Ode 8 of the first Canon in Tone 8, entreating mercy through their collective prayers.

[^10933]: Doxological troparion (Glory, For the Departed) of Ode 8 of the first Canon in Tone 8, appealing to the Righteous Judge to preserve the departed uncondemned.

[^10934]: Theotokion (Both now) of Ode 8 of the first Canon in Tone 8, invoking the Mother of the Sun of Righteousness to dispel the darkness of the soul.

[^10935]: Heirmos of Ode 8 of the second Canon (for the Departed) in Tone 8, describing the musical instruments and idol in the plain of Dura (Daniel 3:1-7) resisted by the three youths.

[^10936]: First troparion (Martyrion) of Ode 8 of the second Canon in Tone 8, praising the martyrs who finished earthly combats and received heavenly crowns.

[^10937]: Second troparion of Ode 8 of the second Canon in Tone 8, confessing Christ's descent into the nethermost pit to resurrect the dead.

[^10938]: Doxological troparion (Glory) of Ode 8 of the second Canon in Tone 8, addressing Christ as the fountain of eternal life and stream of delight.

[^10939]: Theotokion (Both now) of Ode 8 of the second Canon in Tone 8, invoking the Virgin Mother of God the Savior.

[^10941]: Heirmos of Ode 9 of the first Canon in Tone 8, magnifying the unwedded Mother of God exalted above the heavenly powers.

[^10942]: First troparion (Martyrs) of Ode 9 of the first Canon in Tone 8, praising the martyrs standing before unjust judges and winning crowns of righteousness.

[^10943]: Second troparion (Hierarchs) of Ode 9 of the first Canon in Tone 8, likening the holy bishops and pastors to the helms of the Church guiding the spiritual vessel unto the harbor of the commandments.

[^10944]: Third troparion (Prophets, Venerables, and Holy Women) of Ode 9 of the first Canon in Tone 8, invoking their collective intercession for divine compassions.

[^10945]: Doxological troparion (Glory, For the Departed) of Ode 9 of the first Canon in Tone 8, praying that the departed may partake of eternal honor and glory.

[^10946]: Theotokion (Both now) of Ode 9 of the first Canon in Tone 8, asking the all-immaculate Mother carrying all good things in her arms to guide our way toward God.

[^10947]: Heirmos of Ode 9 of the second Canon (for the Departed) in Tone 8, meditating with awe upon the ineffable condescension of the Most High taking flesh from the Virgin.

[^10948]: First troparion (Martyrs) of Ode 9 of the second Canon in Tone 8, extolling the martyrs illuminated by Trinity-rays who defied the tyrants' decrees.

[^10949]: Second troparion of Ode 9 of the second Canon in Tone 8, praising the destruction of bitter hades and petitioning unwaning light for the departed.

[^10950]: Doxological troparion (Glory) of Ode 9 of the second Canon in Tone 8, contemplating Christ as all sweetness, all desire, and ineffable beauty, and praying for the departed to enjoy His comeliness.

[^10951]: Theotokion (Both now) of Ode 9 of the second Canon in Tone 8, dogmatically professing Christ as twofold in nature, only-begotten of the Father and firstborn of creation from the Virgin.

[^10952]: Rubric prescribing "It is truly meet" (*Досто́йно є҆́сть*), the Little Litany, the Exapostilarion, and the customary morning psalms of the Praises (Psalms 148-150 LXX).

[^10953]: Rubric introducing the Stichera of the Martyrs at the Praises on Saturday in Tone 8. The printed Slavonic text errantly reads *Гла́съ г҃.* (Tone 3) due to a recurring typographical defect where the letter *и҃* (8) was typeset or damaged as *г҃* (3); the hymns and melodic models follow Tone 8 throughout.

[^10954]: First Sticheron of the Martyrs at the Praises on Saturday in Tone 8 (*Что̀ ва́съ нарече́мъ, Ст҃і́и?...*), addressing the martyrs through typological comparisons to Cherubim, Seraphim, Angels, and Powers.

[^10955]: Second Sticheron of the Martyrs at the Praises on Saturday in Tone 8, praising their public confession before kings and their ongoing healings in the world.

[^10956]: Third Sticheron of the Martyrs at the Praises on Saturday in Tone 8, commemorating their victory over deception through the Cross, spanning across physical leaves p989 and p990.

[^10957]: Conclusion of the third Sticheron of the Martyrs at the Praises on Saturday in Tone 8, continuing from physical leaf p989.

[^10958]: Fourth Sticheron of the Martyrs at the Praises on Saturday in Tone 8, depicting the martyrs clad in the breastplates of faith and armed with the sign of the Cross.

[^10959]: Doxological Sticheron (Glory) at the Praises on Saturday in Tone 8, presenting a sobering contemplation of the unmerciful Judge, the gnashing of teeth, outer darkness, and eternal fire, while praying for rest for the elect.

[^10960]: Theotokion (Both now) at the Praises on Saturday in Tone 8, invoking the pure Virgin as the Gate of the Word.

[^10961]: Rubric introducing the Aposticha Stichera for the Departed at Saturday Matins in Tone 8.

[^10962]: Melodic model heading (*Podoben*) in Tone 8, referencing the automelon "O most marvelous wonder" (*Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ*).

[^10963]: First Sticheron for the Departed at the Aposticha on Saturday in Tone 8 (*Ца́рское мнѣ̀ подписа́лъ є҆сѝ свобожде́ніе...*), meditating on Christ signing our charter of liberty with the scarlet ink of His own blood.

[^10964]: First psalm verse at the Aposticha of Saturday Matins (Psalm 64:5 LXX: *Блаже́ни, ꙗ҆̀же и҆збра́лъ, и҆ прія́лъ є҆сѝ Гдⷭи*).

[^10965]: Second Sticheron for the Departed at the Aposticha on Saturday in Tone 8 (*Свѧще́нствовавъ ꙗ҆́кѡ человѣ́къ...*), portraying Christ offering Himself as Priest and Lamb unto the Father, and praying for the departed to dwell beside the streams of delight.

[^10966]: Second psalm verse at the Aposticha of Saturday Matins (Psalm 24:13 LXX: *Дꙋ́ши и҆́хъ во благи́хъ водворѧ́тсѧ*).

[^10967]: Third Sticheron for the Departed at the Aposticha on Saturday in Tone 8 (*Глꙋбино́ю мꙋ́дрости...*), invoking Christ's providence over human life and petitioning rest beside the waters of repose (Psalm 22:2 LXX).

[^10968]: Third psalm verse at the Aposticha of Saturday Matins (Psalm 101:13 / 111:6 LXX: *И҆ па́мѧть и҆́хъ въ ро́дъ и҆ ро́дъ*).

[^10969]: Fourth Sticheron for the Departed at the Aposticha on Saturday in Tone 8 (*Сло́во сы́й неви́димый...*), confessing the invisible Word co-originate with the Father and the Spirit, spanning across physical leaves p990 and p991.

[^10970]: Conclusion of Sticheron 4 for the Departed at the Aposticha of Saturday Matins in Tone 8, continuing from physical leaf p990.

[^10971]: Doxological Theotokion (*Сла́ва: и҆ ны́нѣ: Бг҃оро́диченъ*) at the Aposticha of Saturday Matins in Tone 8 (*Ꙗ҆́кѡ заче́нши безнача́льное Сло́во...*), petitioning the Mother of God to settle her servants where the righteous keep unending festival.

[^10972]: Rubric introducing the Beatitudes (*Блаже́нна*) at the Divine Liturgy on Saturday in Tone 8.

[^10973]: Opening troparion / Beatitude verse at the Divine Liturgy on Saturday in Tone 8 (*Поманѝ на́съ Хрⷭтѐ Сп҃се мі́ра...*), invoking the prayer of the wise thief upon the tree.

[^10974]: First troparion (Martyrs) of the Beatitudes on Saturday in Tone 8, extolling the passion-bearers who wounded demonic hosts through their holy wounds.

[^10975]: Second troparion (Hierarchs, Prophets, and Venerables) of the Beatitudes on Saturday in Tone 8, praising the saints who attained the heavenly inheritance.

[^10976]: Third troparion (For the Departed) of the Beatitudes on Saturday in Tone 8, praying for the faithful departed to inherit paradise.

[^10977]: Doxological troparion (Glory) of the Beatitudes on Saturday in Tone 8, offering a final Trinitarian hymn for the rest of the departed and mercy for the singer.

[^10978]: Theotokion (Both now) of the Beatitudes on Saturday in Tone 8, petitioning the Virgin Mother of all goodness for remission of sins and great mercy.

[^10979]: Colophon rubric marking the completion of the entire Tone 8 weekly cycle (*Коне́цъ ѻ҆смо́мꙋ Гла́сꙋ*).

[^10980]: Title and liturgical rubric introducing the Triadica of St. Gregory of Sinai (*Тро́йчни Григо́рїа Сїнаі́та*), appointed to be chanted on all Sundays after the Triadic Canon at the Midnight Office (*на Полꙋ́нощницѣ*).

[^10981]: First Triadicon of Gregory of Sinai (*Досто́йно є҆́сть бг҃олѣ́пнѡ сла́вити тѧ̀...*), confessing the Holy Trinity as boundless, transcendent, Monad in essence and three in hypostases.

[^10982]: Second Triadicon of Gregory of Sinai (*Господонача́льнꙋю Херꙋвї́мъ...*), exalting the Trinity as Master-Origin of the Cherubim and Seraphim.

[^10983]: Third Triadicon of Gregory of Sinai (*Ѻ҆тцꙋ̀ безначáльнꙋ и҆ Бг҃ꙋ...*), worshipping the unoriginate Father, co-unoriginate Word, and the Spirit in inseparable essence.

[^10984]: Fourth Triadicon of Gregory of Sinai (*Воспои́мъ всѝ бг҃олѣ́пнѡ...*), offering divine songs unto the three-hypostatic dominion and one Kingdom.

[^10985]: Fifth Triadicon of Gregory of Sinai (*Лꙋчеза̑рныѧ твоѧ̑ мѡ́лнїа возсїѧ́й мнѣ̀...*), petitioning the Creator of all for the radiant lightnings of divine grace.

[^10986]: Sixth Triadicon of Gregory of Sinai (*Є҆го́же трепе́щꙋтъ и҆ трѧсꙋ́тсѧ Херꙋвї́ми...*), praising Christ incarnate of the Virgin before Whom the heavenly powers quake.

[^10987]: Seventh Triadicon of Gregory of Sinai (*Досто́йно є҆́сть всеблагоговѣ́йнѡ моли́ти тѧ̀...*), praying with tears unto the All-Merciful Savior.

[^10988]: Eighth Triadicon of Gregory of Sinai (*Прїимѝ сле́зы Царю̀...*), begging the King of all for deliverance from the flame and outer darkness and a portion in the heavenly Kingdom.

[^10989]: Doxological Triadicon (Glory) of Gregory of Sinai (*Ѻ҆́тче Вседержи́телю, Сло́ве Бо́жїй...*), confessing the one power and godhead of the Trinity, spanning across physical leaves p992 and p993.

[^10990]: Conclusion of the doxological Triadicon (Glory) of Gregory of Sinai, continuing from physical leaf p992.

[^10991]: Theotokion (Both now) of the Triadica of Gregory of Sinai (*И҆зъ ме́ртвыхъ ви́дѣвши твоего̀ Сы́на...*), contemplating the joy of creation at Christ's Resurrection.

[^10992]: Rubric concluding the Sunday Midnight Office, prescribing "It is truly meet" (*Досто́йно є҆́сть*), Trisagion, Our Father, the Hypakoe of the Tone or the penitential troparia (*Поми́лꙋй на́съ Гдⷭи*), litany, and dismissal.

[^10993]: Rubric introducing the Resurrectional Evlogitaria (*Тропарѝ пѣва́еми по Непоро́чнахъ по всѧ̑ Недѣ́ли*), chanted after the 17th Kathisma (The Blameless / *Непоро́чны*, Psalm 118 LXX) at Sunday Matins in Tone 5.

[^10994]: Scriptural refrain (*Благослове́нъ є҆сѝ Гдⷭи, наꙋчи́ мѧ ѡ҆правда́нїємъ твои̑мъ*) taken from Psalm 118:12 LXX, chanted before each Evlogitarion troparion.

[^10995]: First Evlogitarion troparion in Tone 5 (*А҆́гг҃льскїй собо́ръ ᲂу҆диви́сѧ...*), recounting the astonishment of the angelic host at Christ's descent into hades and the raising of Adam.

[^10996]: Second Evlogitarion troparion in Tone 5 (*По что̀ мѵ́ра со ми́лостивными слеза́ми...*), depicting the radiant angel at the tomb asking the women why they mingle myrrh with tears.

[^10997]: Third Evlogitarion troparion in Tone 5 (*Зѣлѡ̀ ра́нѡ, мѵроно́сицы теча́хꙋ...*), showing the angel announcing that weeping has ceased and commanding them to proclaim the Resurrection to the Apostles.

[^10998]: Fourth Evlogitarion troparion in Tone 5 (*Мѵроно́сицы жены̀ съ мѵ́ры прише́дшїѧ...*), recording the angelic declaration: "Why seek ye the Living One among the dead?"

[^10999]: Doxological troparion (Glory: Triadicon) of the Evlogitaria in Tone 5 (*Поклони́мсѧ Ѻ҆тцꙋ̀...*), confessing the Holy Trinity in one essence with the Seraphic hymn.

[^11000]: Theotokion (Both now) of the Evlogitaria in Tone 5 (*Жизнода́вца ро́ждши...*), praising the Mother of God who delivered Adam from sin and gave joy unto Eve.

[^11001]: Concluding triple Alleluia and doxology (*А҆ллилꙋ́їа, г҃. Сла́ва тебѣ̀ Бо́же*) sealing the Sunday Evlogitaria.

[^11002]: Opening title heading of the Resurrectional Appendices: The Resurrectional Morning Gospels with the Resurrectional Exapostilaria and Evangelical Stichera (*Воскрⷭнаѧ Е҆ѵⷢлїа ᲂу҆́треннаѧ, со Свѣти́лны воскре́сными и҆ Стїхи́рами Е҆ѵ́лскими*).

[^11003]: Codicological and hymnographic attribution rubric: The Morning Stichera (Eothina) are the compositions of Byzantine Emperor Leo VI the Wise (886–912), while the Resurrectional Exapostilaria (Photogogika) are the work of his son, Emperor Constantine VII Porphyrogenitus (913–959).

[^11004]: Title heading for Resurrectional Gospel 1, appointed from Matthew, Pericope 116 (Matthew 28:16-20).

[^11005]: Full liturgical text of Resurrectional Gospel 1 (Matthew 28:16-20), recounting the Great Commission on the mountain in Galilee.

[^11007]: Theotokion of the first Exapostilarion (*Съ Оу҆чени́ки ра́доваласѧ є҆сѝ...*), commemorating the Mother of God's joy at the third-day Resurrection of her Son.

[^11008]: First Evangelical Sticheron (Eothinon 1) in Tone 1 (*На го́рꙋ Оу҆ченикѡ́мъ и҆дꙋ́щимъ...*), by Emperor Leo the Wise, meditating on Christ's appearance on the mountain and the Apostolic mission.

[^11009]: Title heading for Resurrectional Gospel 2, appointed from Mark, Pericope 70 (Mark 16:1-8).

[^11010]: Liturgical text of Resurrectional Gospel 2 (Mark 16:1-8), recounting the myrrh-bearers arriving at the tomb, spanning across physical leaves p994 and p995.

[^11011]: Conclusion of Resurrectional Gospel 2 (Mark 16:2-8), continuing from physical leaf p994.

[^11012]: Second Resurrectional Exapostilarion (*Свѣти́ленъ в҃: Ка́мень ᲂу҆зрѣ́вше ѿвале́нъ...*), recounting the myrrh-bearers witnessing the young man at the tomb.

[^11013]: Theotokion of the second Exapostilarion (*А҆́гг҃лъ ᲂу҆́бѡ принесѐ Дѣ́вѣ...*), drawing an antithetical parallel between the angel of the Annunciation and the angel of the Resurrection.

[^11014]: Second Evangelical Sticheron (Eothinon 2) in Tone 2 (*Съ мѵ́ры прише́дшимъ ꙗ҆̀же съ Марі́ею жена́мъ...*), by Emperor Leo the Wise.

[^11015]: Title heading for Resurrectional Gospel 3, appointed from Mark, Pericope 71 (Mark 16:9-20).

[^11016]: Printed marginal gloss / footnote clarifying the Hebraic idiom "the first of the sabbaths" (*въ пе́рвый сꙋббѡ́ты*) as signifying the first day of the week, namely Sunday (*Въ пе́рвый де́нь сꙋббѡ́ты, си є҆́сть седми́цы*).

[^11017]: Liturgical text of Resurrectional Gospel 3 (Mark 16:9-20), describing Christ appearing to Mary Magdalene, the two on the way to Emmaus, and the eleven, spanning across physical leaves p995 and p996.

[^11018]: Conclusion of Resurrectional Gospel 3 (Mark 16:14-20), continuing from physical leaf p995.

[^11019]: Third Resurrectional Exapostilarion (*Свѣти́ленъ г҃: Ꙗ҆́ко Хрїсто́съ воскре́се, никто́же да не вѣ́рꙋетъ...*), exhorting all to believe the Resurrection confirmed by many signs.

[^11020]: Theotokion of the third Exapostilarion (*Возсїѧ́вшее Со́лнце...*), invoking the Sun of Righteousness who shone forth from the tomb as a bridegroom from his chamber.

[^11021]: Third Evangelical Sticheron (Eothinon 3) in Tone 3 (*Магдали́нѣ Марі́и, Спа́сово благовѣ́ствꙋющей...*), by Emperor Leo the Wise.

[^11022]: Title heading for Resurrectional Gospel 4, appointed from Luke, Pericope 112 (Luke 24:1-12).

[^11023]: Printed marginal gloss / footnote clarifying "one of the sabbaths" (*во є҆ди́нꙋ ѿ сꙋббѡ́тъ*) as meaning the first day of the week, that is, Sunday (*Въ пе́рвый де́нь седми́цы, си є҆́сть, въ Недѣ́лю*).

[^11024]: Liturgical text of Resurrectional Gospel 4 (Luke 24:1-12), detailing the visit of the women to the tomb and the two men in shining garments, spanning across physical leaves p996 and p997.

[^11026]: Fourth Resurrectional Exapostilarion (*Свѣти́ленъ д҃: Добродѣ́телми блиста́вшеся...*), urging the faithful to shine with virtues and run with Peter unto the life-bearing tomb.

[^11027]: Theotokion of the fourth Exapostilarion (*Ра́доватися вѣща́вый...*), celebrating Christ transforming ancestral sorrow into resurrectional joy.

[^11028]: Fourth Evangelical Sticheron (Eothinon 4) in Tone 4 (*Оу҆́тро бѣ̀ глꙋбоко̀...*), by Emperor Leo the Wise.

[^11029]: Title heading for Resurrectional Gospel 5, appointed from Luke, Pericope 113 (Luke 24:12-35).

[^11033]: Theotokion of the fifth Exapostilarion (*Пою̀ безчи́сленнꙋю твою̀ ми́лость...*), praising the Kenosis and descent into hades of the Creator incarnate of the Virgin.

[^11034]: Fifth Evangelical Sticheron (Eothinon 5) in Tone 5 (*Ѡ҆ премꙋ́дрыхъ сꙋде́бъ твои́хъ Хрⷭтѐ!...*), by Emperor Leo the Wise, marveling at the divine dispensation on the way to Emmaus.

[^11035]: Title heading for Resurrectional Gospel 6, appointed from Luke, Pericope 114 (Luke 24:36-53).

[^11036]: Liturgical text of Resurrectional Gospel 6 (Luke 24:36-53), Christ appearing in the midst of the disciples, eating broiled fish and honeycomb, and ascending from Bethany.

[^11038]: Conclusion of the sixth Resurrectional Exapostilarion, continuing from physical leaf p999.

[^11039]: Theotokion of the sixth Exapostilarion (*Творе́цъ созда́нїа, и҆ Бг҃ъ всѣ́хъ...*), venerating the all-holy Virgin whose virginal integrity remained uninjured after childbirth.

[^11040]: Sixth Evangelical Sticheron (Eothinon 6) in Tone 6 (*И҆́стинный ми́ръ ты̀ Хрⷭтѐ...*), by Emperor Leo the Wise, extolling Christ who bestowed divine peace upon the disciples.

[^11041]: Title heading for Resurrectional Gospel 7, appointed from John, Pericope 63 (John 20:1-10).

[^11042]: Liturgical text of Resurrectional Gospel 7 (John 20:1-10), Peter and the beloved disciple running to the empty tomb and seeing the linen clothes and folded napkin.

These hymns represent the standard Daily Triadica of Tone 5 ("Пѣ́нїю вре́ма, и҆ моли́твѣ ча́съ").

[^11149]: Slavonic Столпѝ (Greek Στύλοι / Pillars): liturgical tables mapping the weekly cycle of the Octoechos Tones to the eleven Sunday Matins Resurrection Gospels (Eothina) throughout the liturgical year.

[^11150]: Rubrical heading explaining the function of the Pillars of the Octoechos and Sunday Matins Gospels.

[^11151]: Pillar 1 (Сто́лпъ а҃), beginning on the 5th Sunday after Pentecost (Descent of the Holy Spirit).

[^11152]: Pillar 2 (Сто́лпъ в҃), beginning after the Feast of the Holy Prophet Elijah (July 20).

[^11153]: Gospel 10 (John 21:1–14, Pericope 66).

[^11154]: Pillar 3 (Сто́лпъ г҃), beginning after the Universal Elevation of the Precious and Life-giving Cross (September 14).

[^11155]: Pillar 4 (Сто́лпъ д҃), beginning in the Nativity Fast (Philip's Fast, November 15).

[^11156]: Pillar 5 (Сто́лпъ є҃), beginning after the Baptism of the Lord (Theophany, January 6).

[^11157]: Pillar 6 (Сто́лпъ ѕ҃), beginning with the Holy Great Fast (Clean Week).

[^11158]: In the 1895 Lviv edition, the numeral for the 10th Resurrection Gospel is omitted and marked only by a centered dot (•), though the accompanying citation (ѿ І҆ѡа́нна, зача́ло ѯ҃ѕ) corresponds precisely to the 10th Gospel.

[^11159]: In the 1895 Lviv edition, Tone 8 is misprinted as Tone 3 (Гла́съ г҃) in the sixth pillar, following Tone 7.

[^11160]: Canonical H1 landmark opening Part 10 of the publication specification (General Parastas / Memorial Appendix, encompassing appendix folios 114–127 / physical leaves p1016–p1029).

[^11161]: Slavonic Оу҆каза́нїа (Rubrical Instructions / Typikon Ordinal).

[^11162]: Slavonic Оу҆ка́зъ ѡ҆ Слꙋ́жбѣ всеѧ̀ седми́цы, ка́кѡ пое́тсѧ О҆ктѡ́ихъ съ Минéею (Instruction on the Service of the Whole Week: how the Octoechos is sung with the Menaion).

[^11163]: Typikon rubric governing the concurrence of Sunday services with a Menaion feast of a Saint having a vigil, polyeleos, or six/four troparia, including canon distribution and the priority of the Resurrection Kontakion at Ode 6.

[^11164]: Typikon rubric governing Sunday evening Vespers and daily commemorations with the Menaion.

[^11165]: Typikon rubric governing the celebration of forefeasts, afterfeasts, and the order of Compline throughout the week.

[^11166]: Continuation of Compline rubrics, temple troparia, and Kontakion selection for Polyeleos feasts and forefeasts/afterfeasts.

[^11167]: Comprehensive Typikon rubric for the Midnight Office (Полꙋ́нощница) throughout the year, specifying when "Behold, the Bridegroom comes" and "Remember, O Lord, in hope" are omitted on Dominical Feasts, Theotokos Master Feasts, Lazarus Saturday, Mid-Pentecost, Apodosis of Pascha, and major Saints' days.

[^11168]: Rubric for Monday Matins at "God is the Lord," governing the Troparion of the Saint and lesser Theotokia.

[^11169]: Rubrical directions for weekday Matins Canons across Monday through Friday, governing the combination of the Penitential, Bodiless Powers, Forerunner, Cross, Apostles, Saint Nicholas, and Menaion Canons, as well as the omission of Martyria when a Saint is sung to 6.

[^11170]: Rubric governing Sessional Hymns (Cathismata) and Kontakia after Odes 3 and 6 of the Matins Canon on weekdays and feasts.

[^11171]: Slavonic Ѻ҆ свѣти́лнахъ, ка́кѡ глаго́лютсѧ въ седми́ци кромѣ̀ Недѣ́ли (Concerning the Photagogica: how they are said on weekdays apart from Sunday).

[^11172]: Rubric governing the assignment of Octoechos, Menaion, and Stavrotheotokion Photagogica throughout the weekdays, continuing onto leaf p1019.

[^11173]: Conclusion of weekday Photagogica rubric from leaf p1018.

[^11174]: Typikon rubric for the Praises (Lauds / На Хвали́техъ) on weekdays.

[^11175]: Detailed Typikon rubric for the Aposticha (На Стїхо́внѣ) at weekday Vespers and Matins, specifying the psalm verses [Ps. 89:14, 17 LXX], Saint's refrains, and concluding dismissal Troparia.

[^11176]: Typikon rubric governing the Troparia and Kontakia at the First, Third, Sixth, and Ninth Hours, and their alternation during forefeasts and afterfeasts.

[^11177]: Concluding order of Kontakia at the Hours and Typika when the Divine Liturgy is not celebrated.

[^11178]: Typikon directions for the Divine Liturgy on weekdays: Beatitudes (Макаризмы) from the Octoechos and Menaion, troparia/kontakia after the Little Entrance, and the suspension of the daily Octoechos during forefeasts and afterfeasts.

[^11179]: Slavonic Оу҆ка́зъ ѡ҆ Слꙋ́жбѣ Сꙋббѡ́тнѣй, є҆гда̀ пое́мъ Бг҃ъ Гдⷭ҇ь (Instruction on the Saturday Service, when we sing "God is the Lord").

[^11180]: Comprehensive Typikon rubric governing Saturday services when "God is the Lord" is sung: Friday evening Vespers (with the three Octoechos Martyria at the Aposticha using Psalm 122:1, 3 LXX), Compline, Midnight Office, and Saturday Matins troparia.

[^11181]: Slavonic: *Пое́мъ же Свѧта́гѡ Мине́и со і҆рмосо́мъ на ѕ҃...* Rubrical instructions for Saturday Matins specifying the order of canons combining the Menaion (which always takes precedence on Saturdays), the Temple patron, and the Octoechos martyr canon.

[^11182]: Slavonic: *Въ ку́ю ли́бо сꙋббѡ́тꙋ славосло́віе прилучи́тсѧ...* Typikon rubric governing Saturday Matins when a Doxology-ranked Saint occurs, detailing the disposition of the Temple canon, photagogica, Praises stichera, and the First and Third Hours.

[^11183]: Slavonic: *По трисвѧто́мъ конда́къ Свѧто́му...* Rubrical order for the Third and Sixth Hours, the Liturgy Beatitudes, and the reading order of the Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion verse from the Publican and Pharisee through All Saints.

[^11184]: Slavonic: *Оу҆ка́зъ ѡ҆ хра́мѣ Хрїсто́ва Воскресе́ніа.* Special rubrical instruction for parishes or monasteries where the primary church is dedicated to Christ's Resurrection (*Хра́мъ Воскресе́ніа Хрїсто́ва*), prescribing a 4-troparion Resurrection canon on Saturday Matins.

[^11185]: Slavonic: *А́ще прилучи́тсѧ предпра́зднство и҆лѝ попра́зднство...* Rule governing forefeasts and afterfeasts of Dominical and Theotokos feasts, as well as the Deposition of the Robe (*Положе́ніе Ри́зы*) and Deposition of the Sash (*Положе́ніе честна́гѡ По́яса*), which entirely suppress the weekday Octoechos except for the Friday evening Dogmatikon.

[^11186]: Slavonic: *Є҆гда̀ бꙋ́детъ въ Сꙋббѡ́тꙋ А҆ллилꙋ́їа.* General rubrical directive for Memorial Saturdays (Soul Saturdays) when *Alleluia* is sung instead of *God is the Lord* at Matins.

[^11187]: Slavonic: *Въ Пѧто́къ на Вече́рни по ѻ҆бы́чномъ стїхосло́віи...* Friday Vespers and Saturday Matins opening rubrics for *Alleluia* Saturdays, specifying the stichera on *Lord, I have cried*, the Aposticha of repose, and the general Troparia of Tone 2.

[^11188]: Slavonic: *Бг҃ъ Гдⷭ҇ь: пое́мъ А҆ллилꙋ́їа, на Гла́съ в҃...* The *Alleluia* chants with verses from Isaiah 26:9 LXX, the troparia, and the division of Kathisma 17 (*Amomos* / Psalm 118 LXX) into two stases with memorial refrains.

[^11189]: Slavonic: *Є҆щѐ моли́мсѧ ѡ҆ блаже́ннѣмъ оу҆покое́ніи...* The Great Diaconal Ektenia for the Departed with the full hierarchical diptychs commemorating ecumenical hierarchs, metropolitans, archbishops, bishops, monastics, emperors, sovereigns, founders, and all Orthodox Christians, followed by the silent priestly prayer *O God of spirits and of all flesh*.

[^11190]: Slavonic: *Та́же пое́мъ дрꙋгꙋ́ю статі́ю: Тво́й є҆́смь, а҆́зъ спаси́ мѧ...* Second stasis of Psalm 118 beginning at v. 94 LXX with the refrain *Give rest, O Lord, to the souls of Thy servants* (or *O Savior, save the souls of Thy servants*), concluding with the Funeral Troparia (*Evlogetaria*).

[^11191]: Slavonic: *І҆ере́й же чте́тъ Помѧни́къ...* Reading of the commemoration diptychs (*Pomyannyk*), Sessional Hymn in Tone 5, Canon of Repose, Praises, Beatitudes, and concluding procession into the narthex.

[^11192]: Slavonic: *Оу҆ка́зъ, ка́кѡ подоба́етъ пѣ́ти Параста́съ ѡ҆ оу҆со́пшихъ правовѣ́рныхъ Хрїстїа́нѣхъ.* Master rubric governing the standalone General Parastas (Great Panikhida) for departed Orthodox Christians, sung on Friday evening after Vespers.

[^11193]: Realia loanword *Tetrapod* (Church Slavonic: *тетрапо́дъ*), the central four-legged table in the nave before the iconostasis upon which the dish of *kolyvo* (or *kutia*) and the memorial cross are set for the service of the departed.

[^11194]: Slavonic: *Ѱало́мъ ч҃. Живы́й въ по́мощи Вы́шнѧгѡ...* Opening prayer, Psalm 90 LXX (*He that dwells in the aid of the Most High*), and the Litany of Repose for individual and congregational memorial services.

[^11195]: Slavonic: *Та́же, А҆ллилꙋ́їа, г҃, на Гла́съ и҃...* Concluding petitions of the litany, Tone 8 Alleluia with memorial verses from Psalms 64:5, 101:13, and 24:13 LXX, and the memorial troparion *Who by the depth of wisdom*.

[^11196]: Slavonic: *По се́мъ каѳі́сма: Блаже́ни непоро́чніи...* Chanting of Kathisma 17 (Psalm 118 LXX) in two stases in Tone 5 with intermediate diaconal commemoration and silent priestly prayer.

[^11197]: Slavonic: *Свѧты́хъ ли́къ ѡ҆брѣ́те и҆сто́чникъ жи́зни...* Funeral Troparia (*Evlogetaria* of the Departed) in Tone 5, Stanza 1, with the psalm refrain *Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach me Thy statutes* (Ps. 118:12 LXX).

[^11198]: Slavonic: *Дла́нію ѿ не сꙋ́щихъ созда́вый мѧ...* Funeral Troparia (*Evlogetaria*), Stanza 2, commemorating the creation of humanity from nothingness, the Fall, and the return unto dust.

[^11199]: Slavonic: *О́бразъ є҆́смь неизрече́нныѧ твоеѧ̀ сла́вы...* Funeral Troparia (*Evlogetaria*), Stanza 3, pleading for divine cleansing and restoration to the primordial homeland of Paradise.

[^11200]: Slavonic: *Въ пꙋ́ть оу҆́зкій хо́ждшіи приско́рбный...* Funeral Troparia (*Evlogetaria*), Stanza 4, the voice of the Savior welcoming those who bore the cross along the narrow path into celestial crowns.

[^11201]: Slavonic: *А́гнца Бж҃їа проповѣ́давшіи...* Funeral Troparia (*Evlogetaria*), Stanza 5, invocation of the holy Martyrs slain like lambs to intercede for the remission of debts.

[^11202]: Slavonic: *Оу҆поко́й Бж҃е рабы̑ твоѧ̑...* Funeral Troparia (*Evlogetaria*), Stanza 6, petition for repose among the choirs of Saints and Righteous in Paradise.

[^11203]: Slavonic: *Трисїѧ́тельное є҆ди́нагѡ Бж҃тва̀...* Funeral Troparia (*Evlogetaria*), Triadikon stanza in praise of the consubstantial Trinity, begging deliverance from the eternal fire.

[^11204]: Slavonic: *Ра́дуйсѧ Чи́стаѧ, Бг҃а пло́тію ро́ждшаѧ...* Funeral Troparia (*Evlogetaria*), Theotokion stanza honoring the Virgin Mother of God through whom salvation was wrought for mankind.

[^11205]: Slavonic: *Оу҆поко́й, Спа́се на́шъ, съ Пра́ведными рабы̑ твоѧ̑...* Sessional troparion of repose in Tone 5 with its Theotokion, praying that the departed be numbered among the righteous.

[^11206]: Slavonic: *Ѿ Дѣ́вы возсіѧ́вый мі́рꙋ Хрⷭ҇тѐ Бж҃е...* Sessional Theotokion in Tone 5 confessing Christ as the Light of the world.

[^11207]: Slavonic: *Вои́стинꙋ сꙋета̀ всѧ́ческаѧ, житіѐ же сѣ́нь и҆ со́ніе...* Patristic funeral sessional hymn in Tone 6 attributed to Saint John of Damascus, meditating on the vanity of earthly wealth and universal mortality.

[^11208]: Slavonic: *Всесвѧта́ѧ Бц҃е, въ вре́мѧ живота̀ моегѡ̀ не ѡ҆ста́ви менѐ...* Sessional Theotokion in Tone 6 begging the Mother of God not to abandon the soul in the hour of death.

[^11209]: Slavonic: *Со Свѧты́ми оу҆поко́й Хрⷭ҇тѐ дꙋ́ши ра̑бъ твои́хъ...* The classic funeral Kontakion in Tone 8 (*With the Saints give rest...*), sung at every service for the departed.

[^11210]: Slavonic: *Са́мъ є҆ди́нъ є҆сѝ Безсме́ртный...* Funeral Ikos in Tone 8 citing Genesis 3:19 LXX (*Earth thou art, and unto earth shalt thou return*), leading into the grave-side Alleluia.

[^11211]: Slavonic: *Со дꙋ́хи Пра́ведныхъ, сконча́вшихсѧ ду́ши ра̑бъ твои́хъ Спа́се оу҆поко́й...* Concluding memorial troparia in Tone 4 sung after Ode 9 and the Trisagion (*With the spirits of the Righteous made perfect...*).

[^11212]: Slavonic: *Въ поко́ищи твое́мъ Гдⷭ҇и...* Memorial troparion in Tone 4 pleading for repose in the resting-places of the Saints.

[^11213]: Slavonic: *Ты̀ є҆сѝ Бг҃ъ сше́дый въ а҆́дъ...* Memorial troparion in Tone 4 confessing Christ's descent into Hades and deliverance of the bound.

[^11214]: Slavonic: *Є҆ди́на чи́стаѧ и҆ непоро́чнаѧ Дѣ́во...* Memorial Theotokion in Tone 4 invoking the Mother of God for the salvation of departed souls.

[^11215]: Slavonic: *Бж҃е духѡ́въ и҆ всѧ́кїѧ пло́ти...* The central Absolution Prayer of Repose recited by the priest (*O God of spirits and of all flesh*), followed by the solemn Funeral Dismissal (*May He Who rose from the dead, Christ our true God...*).

[^11216]: Slavonic: *Въ блаже́нномъ оу҆спе́ніи вѣ́чный поко́й...* Diaconal proclamation of eternal rest and the triple chanting of *Memory Eternal* (*Вѣ́чнаѧ па́мѧть* / *Vichnaya Pamyat*).

[^11217]: Slavonic: *Се́й Чи́нъ подоба́етъ твори́ти въ всѧ̑ Пѧткѝ...* Final liturgical rubric specifying that this Parastas order is to be chanted on all Friday evenings over kolyvo for departed fathers and brethren.

[^11218]: Slavonic: *Коне́цъ, и҆ Бг҃у Сла́ва.* Concluding colophon of the 1895 Lviv Stauropegion Complete Octoechos, marking the completion of the 1,029-page liturgical monument.
